title: register_agent does not reconcile sqlite identity row with on-disk key npub
description: Witness 2026-08-19 (flywheel bd-zncc investigation): in a persistent toron data root, after agents/<name>/key.ncryptsec is removed or recreated, register_agent upserts leave the sqlite agents row pointing at the OLD npub while the disk key derives a NEW npub. whois returns the stale row (old last_active untouched); roster sends gift-wrap to the stale npub; unwrap cannot find the key → delivery reports count=N but inbox projection stays empty. title: Canonical catalog: 38 tool names + 25 resource URIs
description:
# Task: Enumerate all 38 AM-Rust tool names + 25 resource URIs (canonical catalog)

## Background
Parity is name-for-name. Agents and conformance need a single first-party catalog committed in-repo so implementers do not reverse-engineer from memory or risk license issues with AM-Rust sources.

## What
1. Produce `docs/parity/am-rust-tool-catalog.md` (or `tests/conformance/CATALOG.md`) listing:
   - All 38 tools by cluster with exact names, required args, return shape summary
   - All 25 MCP resource URIs + schema summaries
2. Cross-check counts: 4+6+5+4+5+2+4+5+3 = 38
3. Flag any ADR abbreviation gaps (macros names especially underspecified in ADR)
4. This catalog is the source of truth for `bd-led.7.2` and `bd-77u.1` fixtures

## Why users (agents) care
Shell-only agents and MCP clients need identical surfaces. Missing one tool = integration break.

## Success
- Catalog committed; CI can count tools == 38 and resources == 25
- Every Phase-1 mailbox bead references tools by exact name from catalog

## Does NOT require crates
Can start in parallel with workspace reshape (same as fixtures).
close_reason: docs/parity/am-rust-tool-catalog.md committed: 38 tools (9 clusters) + 25 resource URIs, counts verified programmatically, derived from public AM-Rust interface (README + #[tool]/#[resource] attrs), no test code vendored. ADR gaps flagged (macros names).

description:
# Buzz + AgentMail comparative study (2026-08-07)

Full study at docs/notes/2026-08-07-buzz-agentmail-comparison.md.

## Verdict
toron matches agentmail on the 38-tool mailbox parity (bd-96a catalogues intentional
divergences). toron matches/exceeds buzz on adopted primitives (kind-as-dispatch, relay
pipeline, @mention dispatch, YAML workflows, NIP-29 channels, presence) + uniquely wins
on crypto identity (Schnorr npub), E2E DMs (NIP-17 gift-wrap), federation, durable
workflow resumption (Resonate — buzz WF-08 unbuilt).

toron LAGS on operational surface (doctor reconstruct/archive-scan, share/export, golden
capture, ATC, robot depth, TUI) and the Forge (NIP-34 git events).

## Quick-win beads filed (this session)
- bd-bzu (P1) mention coalescing — Buzz L2 [highest leverage]
- bd-nsv (P1) workflow loop-prevention hardening — Buzz L5 [correctness]
- bd-jwa (P2) doctor reconstruct — AM A1
- bd-n87 (P2) bound workflow guard evaluation — Buzz L4
- bd-o1h (P2) operator-bypass (Overseer) — AM A6

## Research epics filed
- ATC learning loop (AM A5) — bd-<atc>
- Forge NIP-34 (Buzz L3) — bd-<forge>

## Key insight
toron is architecturally ahead (Nostr-native + federation + durable + local-first),
operationally behind. Path: ship 5 quick wins → 5 medium → decide ATC vs Forge.

title: P0: file-reservation hard-conflict floor BROKEN (distinct agents both granted same exclusive path)
description:
# P0 — file-reservation hard-conflict floor is BROKEN (data-integrity defect)

# Confirmed symptom (live e2e, 2026-08-10)
Two DISTINCT registered agents both granted the SAME exclusive path with ZERO conflict detected:
- flywheel mail locks toron --as CoralFinch --paths src/final-test/* --exclusive -> granted:1, conflicts:0
- flywheel mail locks toron --as E2eTester  --paths src/final-test/* --exclusive -> granted:1, conflicts:0  (E2eTester is a separately-registered agent with its own key)
- flywheel mail conflicts toron --paths src/final-test/* -> conflict_free:true, conflicts:[]  (does not see CoralFinch's hold AT ALL)
- flywheel mail locks toron (list) -> empty for those paths

So acquires return success but the reservations are NOT persisted / NOT readable by the conflict check. The corruption-prevention invariant (two agents must never hold the same exclusive path) is NOT enforced.

# What is NOT the cause (ruled out by code read + live test)
- conflict_view logic is CORRECT: self-exclude (agent_pubkey != own), exclusive filter, overlaps() (proven by the soft-conflict test which DID fire), status Held => true.
- lease_status DOES default status-less 30031 -> Held (the _ => Held arm). Backward-compat parsing is correct.
- TTL is 90 days (DEFAULT_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECS) — not expiry.
- The soft-conflict (intent) path WORKS (oc intent vs pi acquire -> 1 SOFT conflict). So the conflict MACHINERY works for explicit-status intents; only the HELD-via-mail-locks path fails to persist/be-read.

# Root cause (needs isolation — the first task)
The reservations from flywheel mail locks are claimed-granted but not reaching the store conflict_view reads (resolved_leases -> collect_replay). Candidate layers:
1. flywheel mail locks wrapper does not actually publish/persist the 30031 to the bus/replay (claims success, writes nothing).
2. toron-core projection/indexing drops the held 30031 before collect_replay reads it.
3. Identity resolution: flywheel --as CoralFinch resolves to a key that the toron CLI/MCP does not recognize (toron reserve acquire --agent CoralFinch -> "no local key in project toron"). The flywheel-registered agent key vs the toron-project agent key may diverge -> the reservation is published under a key the conflict check can't attribute.

# Isolation steps (do these FIRST)
1. Acquire via the toron MCP tool directly (toron_file_reservation_paths) with two distinct project-agent keys, then check_file_reservation_conflicts — does the MCP path persist+conflict? (isolates flywheel-wrapper vs toron-core)
2. If MCP works: bug is in flywheel mail locks wrapper (not calling the MCP / not persisting).
3. If MCP also fails: bug is in toron-core persistence/projection (resolved_leases/collect_replay not returning held 30031s).
4. git-bisect: was mail locks persisting before the ADR-0011 reservation refactor (status field, resolved_leases, resolve_coordinate)? Determines regression vs pre-existing.

# Why P0
The reservation system is the corruption-prevention floor (ADR-0011: "the atomic conflict-check is NEVER removed"). Two agents editing the same exclusively-reserved files = data corruption / lost work. This MUST be fixed before any coalition/crew work relies on it. ADR-0011 gate 4 (soft-conflict) + the cross-cutting hard-conflict regression test are both failing for the held case.

# Fix direction (after isolation)
Reservations acquired via every path (flywheel mail locks, coalition reserve, toron CLI, MCP) MUST persist to the store conflict_view reads, AND the conflict check MUST hard-block a cross-agent exclusive overlap. Likely a one-coordinate-per-agent fix (d-tag includes agent) + ensure the acquire publishes to the replay bus.

# Verification gate (the bead is done when)
Two distinct registered agents: A locks src/X/* exclusive -> B locks src/X/* exclusive -> B is HARD-blocked (conflicts:[src/X/*], granted:0); flywheel mail conflicts --paths src/X/* shows A's hold; flywheel mail locks lists A's hold. Repeat via coalition reserve + toron CLI + MCP — all four paths consistent.
close_reason:
P0 hard-conflict floor FIXED + live-verified.

Root cause (isolated per bead plan): BusEventStore::replay applied the SQL LIMIT (default 1000, ORDER BY created_at ASC) to the RAW scan BEFORE the Rust filter match. With 1518 stored events, the NEWEST (recent reservations) fell outside the replay window -> conflict check (resolved_leases -> collect_replay) saw no holders -> same exclusive path granted to two distinct agents. Isolation: MCP acquire path reproduced (both agents granted, zero conflicts) -> rules out the flywheel wrapper; hermetic two-agent test PASSED on toron-core -> narrowed to persistence/projection -> the replay-window truncation.

Fix (commit bd97afb, toron-core): kind filter pushed into SQL (WHERE kind IN (...)); filter limit applied to MATCHED output, not the raw scan. Kind-scoped mailbox queries now always see their events.

Regression tests: event_store::test_replay_kind_pushdown_returns_all_30031 (two authors' 30031s both replay) + reservations::test_two_agents_same_exclusive_path_hard_blocks (B hard-blocked on A's exclusive path, holder named, third-party check sees it, own re-check clear).

Gate verified live after daemon restart: E2eTester acquired src/final-test-1pzd/* exclusive -> CoralFinch acquire returned conflicts:[E2eTester], granted:[]; flywheel mail conflicts + MCP conflicts both show the holder; flywheel mail locks path also hard-blocks. All four acquire paths consistent (MCP, flywheel CLI, conflicts checks). 365 toron-core + 427 flywheel tests green (20 reservation tests incl. 1 new; 1 new event-store test).

title: ADR-0012: Standalone Cron Type (distinct from workflow; shared engine; Resonate-native)

User dirs: global ~/.config/flywheel/crons + per-project .flywheel/crons, precedence project>global>builtin. Amends ADR-0005 Spec 3. See docs/decisions/0012-standalone-cron-type.md.
close_reason: ADR-0012 STANDALONE CRON TYPE COMPLETE (captain 2026-08-11). All phases landed + verified: P1 CronSpec schema + parse_cron + lint_cron (toron-workflow, commit 6822344); P2 engine cron path (CronManager + CronSpecRegistration + run_cron_tick + ctx.sleep durable function); P3 flywheel cron CLI over the new cron YAMLs (lint/list/run + user dirs + precedence, source shown); P4 migrate (crons.toml removed; weekly-review -> standalone YAML, source=global); P5 cron-authoring skill ref rewritten to the standalone model. title: P12.1 CronSpec schema + parse_cron + cron lint (toron-workflow; distinct type)
description:
# P1 — CronSpec schema + parse_cron + cron lint (toron-workflow)
ADR-0012 Spec 1/3. Cron is a DISTINCT type (not a workflow).

What:
- CronSpec struct in toron-workflow/src/schema.rs: { name, schedule (Vixie 5-field), owner (profile), scope (host|project), mode (headless|pane), policy { on_failure, on_repeat_failure, repeat_threshold, on_success, max_retries, no_claim_timeout, catchup }, steps: Vec<Step> }. The steps body uses the SAME Step/Action DSL as Workflow (shared engine).
- parse_cron(yaml) -> CronSpec (serde, like parse_workflow).
- cron lint: validate schedule (cron expr parse), owner-profile resolution (flywheel-tier, deferred to the CLI), policy fields, step/action resolution, graph acyclicity if used. DISTINCT from workflow lint (a cron-YAML has schedule+owner; a workflow-YAML does not).

Blast radius: toron/crates/toron-workflow/src/schema.rs (CronSpec + parse_cron) + lint.rs (cron lint path). No flywheel change this phase.

Repo: toron (crates/toron-workflow).

Verification gate: parse_cron reads the ADR-0012 example YAML (weekly-upgrade); cron lint validates it; a workflow lint REJECTS a cron-YAML (the two types are distinct at lint). Unit tests for parse_cron + cron-lint.

Dependency: none (foundational schema).
close_reason:
Phase 1 (ADR-0012) landed in toron-workflow (commit 6822344: schema.rs + lint.rs only).
WHAT:
- CronSpec { name, description, schedule, owner, scope, mode, policy, steps, graph } — DISTINCT type, no trigger. Reuses CronScope + shared Step/Action DSL + Graph.
- CronSpecPolicy (cron-specific: on_failure/on_repeat_failure/repeat_threshold/on_success/max_retries/no_claim_timeout/catchup). Deliberately separate from workflow CronPolicy (which has no catchup; ADR-0012: cron policy does not belong on a plain workflow; CronPolicy is fully-literal-constructed in bd-m7ac in-flight cron_failure.rs — untouched).
- CronMode (headless|pane) + CronCatchup (latest|skip), parse_cron(yaml).
- lint_cron + cron_lint_yaml: 5-field vixie validation via shared normalize_cron + cron::Schedule, owner non-empty/identifier, policy sanity (repeat_threshold>=1, no_claim_timeout>0), shared step checks + graph acyclicity (check_name/check_steps extracted, workflow lint messages byte-identical).
- WORKFLOW LINT REJECTS cron-YAML: lint_yaml sniffs top-level schedule/owner -> blocking error naming cron (distinct at lint, ADR-0012).
GATE: ADR-0012 weekly-upgrade example parses verbatim (parse_adr_example_cron) + lints clean (cron_lint_adr_example_clean); workflow lint rejects it (workflow_lint_rejects_cron_yaml); 9 schema + 8 lint unit tests; 148 toron-workflow lib tests green; clippy --no-deps -p toron-workflow --lib -- -D warnings clean; toron-mcp/toron-cli/flywheel build.
FINDING for Phase 2 (engine): step-level `if:` in the ADR example is silently ignored by serde (probe-verified; unknown step keys are dropped) — the example parses but the conditional is unrepresented until the engine phase. Locks released.

title: P12.2 Engine cron path: cron YAML -> Resonate durable function (shared engine)
description:
# P2 — Engine: cron YAML -> Resonate durable function (shared engine, cron input path)
ADR-0012 Spec 2/3. The shared toron-workflow engine runs a cron as a scheduled durable function.

What:
- The engine gains a cron-input path: parse a CronSpec -> a Resonate durable function whose schedule is a ctx.sleep loop (next-due computation + sleep until tick) and whose body is the CronSpec.steps (call_workflow / delay / branch / etc.) run as durable steps.
- catchup: latest (run the most-recent due tick on wake after a flywheel restart); skip alternative.
- ONE engine, TWO input types (workflow invoke + cron scheduled). The body's call_workflow composes workflows on the same engine.

Blast radius: toron/crates/toron-workflow/src/engine/ (cron durable function) + cron.rs (the durable-sleep schedule driver, reusing the existing P4.3 cron-manager Resonate substrate). No separate cron engine.

Repo: toron (crates/toron-workflow).

Verification gate: a cron YAML (weekly-upgrade) runs as a Resonate durable function; the schedule fires via ctx.sleep; the body's call_workflow steps execute; a restart mid-sleep resumes + catchup:latest runs the most-recent due tick. The shared engine also still runs an on-demand workflow invoke (no regression).

Dependency: P1 (CronSpec).
close_reason: Engine cron path (P12.2): CronSpec -> Resonate durable function on the shared engine. cron_loop schedule = recorded catch-up decision (decide_tick child) + ctx.sleep(next-due) loop; body = CronSpec.steps via spec_tick_workflow -> run_cron_tick child -> run_workflow (SAME step DSL, one engine two input types; call_workflow composes on the same engine). catchup:latest = recorded decision, single most-recent missed tick on wake; skip honored. Found+fixed replay-determinism bug: old loop re-derived wall-clock decisions on resume -> phantom policy events + early tick fires after restart; now every iteration has fixed terminal-op parity (decide->sleep->tick) and side effects live in the deduped tick child. Verification: cargo build clean, clippy clean, 157 lib tests + integration pass; gate test cron_spec_loop_fires_tick_with_catchup_and_resume_dedup passes x2 against real resonate 0.9.8 (kill/reboot mid-sleep, catchup:latest fires exactly ONE tick, resume dedup, call_workflow body executes probe/upgrade/verify); on-demand workflow invoke suite unaffected (no regression).

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
P12.2 verification (bd-25g7.2, ADR-0012 Phase 2) — evidence:

GATE: cargo build --workspace CLEAN; cargo test -p toron-workflow 157P/0F (twice, incl. live gate test cron_spec_loop_fires_tick_with_catchup_and_resume_dedup); clippy CLEAN.

Design (crates/toron-workflow/src/cron.rs):
- ONE loop, TWO input shapes: CronSpec -> spec_tick_workflow (steps/graph/policy mapped; NO trigger — the loop synthesizes the schedule trigger) + catchup from spec.policy; legacy workflow-binding unchanged. Shared engine runs both (cron-spec:{name} run-id namespace).
- Replay-deterministic loop: per-iteration terminal-ops are (decide_tick -> ctx.sleep -> run_cron_tick), all positionally recorded, so a restart mid-sleep resumes at the RECORDED decision/timer/tick-result: the catch-up decision is a recorded child result (never a re-derived wall-clock one), and the tick body + policy side effects live in the run_cron_tick child (replay resolves the recorded child — no phantom events, no double-fire). Fixes the burst bug found in the first live run (replay's sleep re-matched the stale expired promise).

title: FIX: pre-commit sweep guard — strict staged-paths check + install in flywheel repo (P0)
description:
Sweep incidents (2026-08-15/16, both rounds): crew A commits with git add -A / git add . / commit -a and sweeps crew B's in-flight edits into A's commit; B's work is mis-attributed, forgotten, or redone. Happened >=3 times (wave-1 main.rs sweep, wave-2 constructor cross-commits, MCP-round near-miss).

ROOT CAUSES (verified in code):
1. ~/workspace/FLYWHEEL repo's .git/hooks/pre-commit is the legacy mcp-agent-mail chain-runner — NO reservation check at all. Every sweep happened in the flywheel repo.
2. toron repo HAS `toron guard check` but guard_check_blocked (crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/guard.rs:42) FAILS OPEN when the agent is unattributed (env TORON_AGENT/FLYWHEEL_MAIL_AS missing) — crews forget AGENT_NAME constantly.
3. The guard only blocks paths reserved by OTHERS — a lapsed reservation (4-min TTL vs 4+ min cargo runs) leaves B's files unprotected at sweep time.
4. No enforcement that staged paths are within the committer's OWN reservations.

## Work (repo: ~/workspace/toron — guard.rs + cli + robot; plus install in flywheel repo)
- Strict mode `toron guard check --strict`: when an agent IS attributed, every staged path must match (a) the agent's own active reservation, OR (b) the shared-safe list (.beads/issues.jsonl, .beads/beads.base.jsonl — tracker bookkeeping), else BLOCK with an actionable message naming the offending paths + their holders if any. Env TORON_GUARD_STRICT=0 disables for a session (operator escape hatch, logged).
- Fail-closed attribution in strict mode: agent env MISSING -> block with 'set AGENT_NAME=<pin>' message (no silent pass-through).
- `toron slot acquire` renews the agent's existing file reservations (or guard accepts a held slot as liveness proof) — kills the TTL lapse window during long cargo runs.
- Update the guard-installed hook script: same as today, plus strict env default ON for swarm projects (TORON_GUARD_STRICT=1 exported by flywheel spawn peer/prime injection? minimal: document in hook comment).
- Install/replace the hook in ~/workspace/flywheel: `toron guard install` (replaces the legacy chain-runner by chaining it — keep the mcp-agent-mail plugins running via hooks.d if present; toron guard must NOT clobber user hooks, follow its own rule).
- Tests: strict blocks cross-agent staged path; allows own-reserved; allows .beads bookkeeping; blocks unattributed in strict; slot-acquire renews reservations; non-strict behavior byte-identical (existing tests stay green).

## Acceptance
- Live demo receipt: two agents, A holds src/foo.rs, B stages src/foo.rs + own file -> B's commit blocked naming A; with AGENT_NAME unset -> blocked with the env message. flywheel repo commits guarded.
- Full toron suite green.

## VERIFY
```
cd ~/workspace/toron && cargo test -p toron-core guard && cargo test -p toron-cli
```
close_reason: Completed: strict pre-commit sweep-guard. guard_check_strict (own-reservation OR shared-safe .beads coverage; fail-closed unattributed; blocks name path+holder); CLI --strict + TORON_GUARD_STRICT (0=escape hatch); AGENT_NAME in attribution chain; slot acquire renews holder reservations (1h cap); install preserves legacy hook as pre-commit.legacy + chains it, refuses clobber; hook installed in ~/workspace/flywheel (strict ON, chain-runner + hooks.d intact). VERIFY: cargo test -p toron-core guard = 38 passed; cargo test -p toron-cli = all green; live demo: GreenLake staging RedLake's src/foo.rs blocked 'held by RedLake' exit 1; unattributed blocked with set-AGENT_NAME message exit 1; own path + .beads pass exit 0; flywheel hook blocks unreserved scratch (exit 1), passes clean (exit 0). comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05) — CHANNEL CHOICE (aligns with the bd-led.3.2 lossless rule):

Presence (kind-20001) is ephemeral + loss-tolerant, so it is the CANONICAL consumer for the DROPPING `tokio::broadcast` channel. A missed heartbeat just means stale presence until the next one — no data loss, because presence is never projected to SQLite/Git by definition.

title: Loop --engine parity gate: run 6 e2e-hardened-loop scenarios bar-for-bar on --engine vs legacy
description: The deferred verification for bd-e0xk: run scripts/e2e-hardened-loop.sh (baseline drain, crash-resume+dedup, state-file respawn, blocked alert, frozen-agent escalation, unknown-agent repair) on flywheel loop run --engine vs the legacy imperative loop; all 6 must pass bar-for-bar IDENTICAL. Then legacy removal one phase after --engine proven. bd-e0xk's --engine coexistence path is implemented + runs; this bead is the parity proof + cutover.
close_reason:
PARITY GATE — honest finding, NOT forced. Two full live runs on the FIXED build (bd-bvwf.2-5 landed first, commit 14765aa; real swarms, herdr + Resonate live, scratch projects outside the repo).

RESULTS:
- LEGACY: PASS=4 FAIL=3 — S1 2/6 closed (loop alive full window — the pre-fix early-exit "complete at 3/6" is GONE; stall = environmental toron-mail key issue in the scratch project: renew_file_reservations fails "agent CoralFinch has no local key", every tick); S2 3/4 closed BUT same-invocation resume + zero-dup HELD; S3 PASS; S4 FAIL (agents drained by the mail-key stall); S5 PASS (3 respawns + FailStop hard-stop); S6 PASS (documented).
- ENGINE: PASS=4 FAIL=3 — S1 5/6 (stranded-reclaim re-dispatch worked); S2 PASS (same invocation, 4/4 closed exactly once); S3 PASS; S4 FAIL (documented: blocked not producible via __send on this build); S5 FAIL (1 respawn — CONFOUNDED: S1/S2 drained the ready queue so no further sends to freeze); S6 PASS (documented).

LOOP-FIX VERIFICATION (bd-bvwf.2-5 landed): no early-complete exit on either path; crash-resume reuses the SAME invocation + no duplicate dispatch after kill -9; context respawn fresh/stale byte-identical; legacy S5 hard-stop works. No regression from the reliability set.

PARITY VERDICT: bar-for-bar identical NOT met; direction unchanged (engine >= legacy on S1/S2). Divergences: (1) toron-mail-key env issue in scratch projects (both paths; legacy worse because churn drains its fewer agents) — scratch projects must register a toron agent identity before the loop lease-renew/mail leaves work; (2) engine S5 escalation deferral (documented bd-e0xk later slice); (3) S4 blocked-drive build limitation. Legacy removal NOT authorized. Follow-ups: register a mail identity in gate scratch projects (or make renew_leases skip when the orchestrator identity is unregistered), engine S5 escalation slice.

comments.author: DustySparrow
comments.text:
# bd-3aen parity gate run — 2026-08-11 (DustySparrow)

Ran scripts/e2e-hardened-loop.sh twice against the installed binary (~/.local/bin/flywheel 0.2.0, built 2026-08-11 15:42, includes --engine path commit 168cd8b):
- legacy arm: `LOOP_EXTRA=""` (imperative swarm-loop)
- engine arm: `LOOP_EXTRA="--engine"` (WorkflowEngine loop-dispatch)

Logs: /tmp/bd-3aen/legacy.log, /tmp/bd-3aen/engine.log

## Bar-for-bar matrix

| Scenario | Legacy | Engine |
|---|---|---|
| 1 baseline drain | FAIL (3/6 closed) | FAIL (5/6 closed) |
| 2 crash-resume+dedup | PASS (same invocation resumed, 4/4 closed once) | PASS (same invocation resumed, 4/4 closed once) |
| 3 state-file respawn | PASS | PASS |
| 4 blocked fast-alert | FAIL (no agent) | FAIL (no agent) |
| 5 frozen escalation | PASS (3 respawns + hard-stop) | FAIL (0 respawns) |
| 6 unknown repair | PASS (doc'd limitation) | PASS (doc'd limitation) |
| **Total** | **PASS=5 FAIL=2** | **PASS=4 FAIL=3** |

Gate exit: legacy 1227s, engine 1244s. NOT green on either arm; NOT bar-for-bar identical.

## Root causes

1. Scenario 1 (both arms): loop1.log full of `reclaimed stranded bead X (re-dispatching)` churn; agents polled working but beads not closing within the 10-min budget. This is the bd-bvwf.2/.5 defect class (first-poll-beats-detection -> unknown -> dispatch refusal -> strand reclaim storm). Engine closed 5/6 (better) but still fails the 6-closed gate.
2. Scenario 4 (both arms): after scenario 3's respawn, no agent reaches idle/done within 90s -> `no agent for scenario 4`. Same detection-latency root cause.
3. Scenario 5 (ENGINE ONLY, real divergence): freeze watcher froze opencode pids 52282/9701, but the engine loop produced ZERO respawn events and all loop-dispatch promise rows resolved. Legacy produced 3 respawns + hard-stop ("failed to accept 4 prompts"). The engine path does NOT implement send-failure escalation -> frozen agent never respawned. This is a genuine engine-vs-legacy behavioral gap, not a harness artifact.
4. Environmental noise (both arms): `lease renew failed ... agent CoralFinch has no local key` spam (scratch projects have no CoralFinch key) — known pre-existing issue, non-fatal ("continuing").

## Verdict

`--engine` is NOT proven equivalent. Legacy removal is NOT justified. bd-3aen acceptance (all 6 pass bar-for-bar identical) NOT met.
Blocked on: bd-bvwf.2 (first-poll unknown stall), bd-bvwf.5 (unknown-agent dispatch refusal), plus new discovery for scenario-5 engine escalation gap.

description: Residual of bd-py9o (sampled post-fix, daemon pid 47129): gift-wrap unwrap crypto eliminated, but BusEventStore::replay remains hottest — every subscribe runs the phase-1 id-scan (bus_event_tags joins + ORDER BY + newest-tail LIMIT) even when the identical filter was replayed milliseconds earlier and nothing changed. title: OPS: update existing templates/skills to ADR-0019 vocabulary
description:
Templates predate ADR-0019. The flywheel SKILL.md Fleet-lifecycle section still tells crews 'each lane works in its own worktree (herdr worktree)' — DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS ADR-0019 Spec 3 (worktrees forbidden; serialize/split). A captain following the skill would violate the ADR.

## Work
- integrations/beads-body.md.tpl + beads-execute/review/commit templates: add the ADR-0019 crew contract — ## VERIFY fence requirement on beads, reserve-before-edit + renew, build slot before cargo, stage ONLY reserved paths (never git add -A; cross-sweep = flag on channel), commit-before-close with bead id, close reason carries VERIFY tail, PRINCIPLES citation (name — decision), NO worktree ever, conflict ladder (hard=serialize+channel, soft=freeze+propose, design fork=collab/interrogate, blocked>10min=mail captain), AGENT_NAME for repo hooks.
- beads-review: reviewer verifies at CLEAN HEAD (git stash or /tmp clone), rejects PRINCIPLES-without-decision (cargo-cult), checks no *V2*/*_improved*/*_enhanced* new files.
- ~/.agents/skills/flywheel/SKILL.md: (1) DELETE the multi-lane worktree default paragraph, replace with ADR-0019 Spec 3 serialize/split rule + pointer; (2) add /swarm + /loop to Commands; (3) add 'loop run from PARENT cwd' note already present — keep; (4) captain addressing: captains register a routable adj+noun pin and crews address THAT (bare 'flywheel' name is unroutable in swarm projects); (5) sync ~/.grok mirror if present.

title: Mail read-state never applied to inbox projection: mark-read does not stop re-notification loops
description:
# Gap (TanFern session 2026-08-21, flywheel x toron collab)

`toron mail read` / `mark_message_read` return success and set read receipts, but the inbox projection keeps re-serving the same messages: the orchestrator mail-wake refired '1 urgent' across 5+ turns in one session after the cited messages were marked read. Gotcha #8 already notes 'the projection does not apply read state' — this makes it a live loop, not a cosmetic gap.

## Evidence
- dba9557af070… / b8be54a3eeeb… / d9a310f93f10… marked read via `toron mail read --project toron --agent TanFern` → {"acknowledged":false,"read":…} receipts returned; wake kept firing on the same batch.
- Wake cited id 9150144f2e8c… which is the SENDER npub of a reservation-release notification (importance=normal) — no message with that id exists in any project inbox (toron/flywheel/demo checked).

## Consequence
Agents burn turns chasing phantom urgent mail; wake loops never terminate; urgent signal becomes noise.

## Work
Apply read_ts_us in the inbox projection (fetch_inbox + CLI inbox), so once-only delivery semantics hold for wake drivers; add regression test: mark-read then fetch excludes/flags the message.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p toron-core
```
close_reason:
Premise misdiagnosed — toron-core projection applies read state correctly; closed with end-to-end evidence, no code change warranted.
mark-read writes the projection: toron mail read set read_ts_us on dba9557/b8be54a3/d9a310f9 (values visible on subsequent fetch).
fetch_inbox applies it: messaging.rs joins message_reads (~396-425), unread_only retains unread (~458), shared filters run post-projection for MailSurface + MCP paths.
Wake drivers skip read assigns: flywheel wake_urgent pass-2 checks read_ts_us absent; regression test wake_urgent_skips_read_assign exists.
Session banner decomposed: last-id = sender npub not message id (bd-kryk); the 1 urgent count is REAL and belongs to herdr-name identity flywheel-toron-oc3 (unread high [assign] bd-hkw5.x never seen from pin TanFern) — per-recipient read state working as designed.
Stale docs flagged in thread: flywheel main.rs:7238/:11475 + toron skill gotchas #4/#8 claim no read-state — false since bd-5icg.

toron-core pins `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18` (crates/toron-core/src/backend/herdr.rs:29) while the live herdr daemon reports protocol 19 (`herdr api schema --json` → `protocol: 19`). flywheel's verify-0001.sh gate greps toron-core's pin and FAILS until it is >= 19 (escalated from flywheel bd-8vg; the toron-side tracker never picked it up — this bead closes that gap). flywheel itself already consumes v19 (bd-protocol-v19-bump-dy4).

## What to do

1. Verify toron-core's herdr wire structs against the live v19 schema (`herdr api schema --json`). The v19 deltas (from flywheel's own bump bead) are:
   - AgentInfo.agent_status is NON-Option in v19 (toron already matches)
   - WorkspaceInfo +number, +focused, +active_tab_id (toron already has these)
   - PaneInfo +terminal_id, +focused (toron's PaneInfo at herdr.rs:108 has ONLY pane_id/title/cwd/agent_status — MISSING)
   - WorktreeInfo: workspace_id → open_workspace_id + 4 worktree bools (toron's WorktreeInfo at herdr.rs:117 has worktree_id/workspace_id/branch/label — MISMATCH)
2. Fix the structs that do not conform (PaneInfo terminal_id/focused; WorktreeInfo open_workspace_id + booleans per live schema).
3. Bump `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL` 18 → 19.
4. Update module doc + any protocol-comment references (18 → 19).
5. Verify: a live round-trip against the running herdr daemon (agent.list / workspace.list / pane.list) parses; `cargo test` green; the flywheel verify-0001.sh gate goes GREEN (flywheel path-depends on this repo: ~/workspace/toron).

## Success criteria

- `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 19` in toron-core.
- PaneInfo/WorktreeInfo conform to live v19 schema (field-for-field).
- Live herdr round-trip parses (herdr up, agent.list etc).
- toron `cargo test` passes.
- flywheel `bash docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-0001.sh` passes after this lands.

## Considerations

- The herdr client is the SHARED client across flywheel + toron (ADR-0003 Decision 3A) — sc-fw test asserts exactly one `fn agent_prompt`. Do not duplicate client logic; only fix the structs + pin here.
- Backwards compat: v19 adds fields; existing v18 consumers are unaffected. Wire structs are Deserialize-only here.
- TDD: write/extend a fixture-based parse test (live schema trimmed fixture like flywheel's tests/fixtures/herdr-schema-v19.json) before/with the struct changes.
close_reason: v19 conformed: PaneInfo field-for-field (+terminal_id/workspace_id/tab_id/focused/agent_status non-Option/revision + agent_session/scroll/etc), WorktreeInfo -> open_workspace_id + 4 worktree bools (path/is_bare/is_detached/is_prunable/is_linked_worktree/label/branch); HDR_PROTOCOL 18->19; fixture tests (crates/toron-core/tests/fixtures/herdr-schema-v19.json) green (17 backend tests); full toron-core suite 323 passed (3 bd-5icg in-flight failures = Crew 2's, not mine); flywheel verify-0001.sh PASSED; live round-trip (agent.list/workspace.list/pane.list via typed client) passed against running daemon; clippy -D warnings: 2 pre-existing errors in untouched mailbox files (surface.rs:324, mod.rs:177), zero from this change

title: toron read-state: read_ts projection + honest unread_only filtering
description:
# toron read-state (read receipts in the projection)

## Problem

toron's `fetch_inbox` treats `unread_only` as a documented NO-OP (`messages` branch in messaging.rs:271-278: "Unread-only filtering needs the projection read-state; the pipeline-level dedup treats everything as fresh on first read"). There is no per-recipient read_ts anywhere in the projection, so:
- callers cannot query "what's new since I last looked"
- the AM-parity `mark_message_read` MCP tool exists but writes nothing the projection reads
- flywheel's mail digest/wake uses the `recent` proxy (importance high|urgent) instead of true unread

## What to do

1. Add a per-recipient read-state: a `read_ts` (or per-(message,agent) read receipt) that `mark_message_read`/acknowledge paths WRITE and `fetch_inbox(unread_only: true)` FILTERS on.
   - Where: the SQLite index (`messages` table + a recipient-reads table, or a read_ts column per recipient row in the projection), consistent with the SqliteProjectionSink model (unwrap.rs:413+).
   - The bus/replay path has no read state by nature (events are immutable) — read state is a PROJECTION concern; must be rebuilt/derived deterministically.
2. Wire `mark_message_read` (and the fetch path, per AM parity "fetch marks read") to write the state.
3. Make `unread_only: true` actually filter (fetch_inbox + the surface InboxQuery path + the MCP layer).
4. Expose unread count where useful (e.g. the existing tool response or a small addition) — do not break the existing response shapes.

## Success criteria

- `fetch_inbox(unread_only: true)` returns only messages not yet read by the requesting agent (was: everything).
- `mark_message_read` on a message makes it disappear from the unread-only view.
- Read state survives process restart (persisted, not in-memory-only).
- AM-parity tests (live or unit) cover: mark-read → unread-only fetch excludes it.
- `cargo test` green; no regression in the non-unread path.

## Considerations

- Determinism: read state is projection state, NOT event state — do not write it into Nostr events. The bus replay must converge (read state is a local projection; deleting the index and rebuilding must not re-derive read state from events — document this: read receipts are lost on index rebuild, acceptable for now, or persist alongside the archive).
- Match AM-Rust semantics: AM's fetch_inbox marks returned messages read by default (that is what flywheel's digest historically collided with). Decide + document: does `fetch_inbox` (no args) mark read, or only `mark_message_read`? Prefer explicit `mark_message_read` only (fetch stays read-only) — this is the safer default and keeps the flywheel digest honest.
- Surface consistency: MailSurface `InboxQuery` already carries `unread_only` — the leaf/facade plumbing is done; only the projection needs the real behavior.
- TDD: unit test the projection filter + mark-read round trip before wiring the MCP surface.
close_reason: read-state projection: message_reads table (migration 0002), mark_message_read/acknowledge_message write read_ts, fetch_inbox(unread_only:true) filters, read_ts_us exposed on MCP inbox rows (additive). fetch_inbox stays read-only (design decision). Unit tests: mark-read->unread-only excludes, survives restart, ack implies read, no-pool degrade. cargo test toron-core 326P + toron-mcp 28P, clippy -D warnings green (--no-deps --lib), conformance 5P.

title: Loop completion scoping + stranded-bead reclaim + close-evidence (loop-enforced)
description:
# Dispatch-lesson fix: loop completion + stranded-bead reclaim (scoped)

# Failure
The durable loop resolved EARLY (exit 0, state Resolved) while 5 beads were ready + one was stranded in_progress (assignee=bangedorrunt, not a live agent). The swarm stalled until the captain un-stuck the bead + restarted the loop. Root cause: the completion condition misfired on state churn + had no scope.

# Fix (loop-enforced, code not prose)
1. SESSION SCOPE: the loop records the beads it dispatches (or is assigned via flywheel assign) as its session scope. It completes ONLY when, WITHIN SCOPE: (a) no ready beads, (b) no in_progress bead assigned to a NON-live-agent (stranded), (c) agents settled. Ready beads OUTSIDE scope (other epics, the deferred backlog) never block completion.
2. STRANDED RECLAIM: on each poll, an in_progress bead whose assignee is not a live swarm agent (captain, dead agent, unknown identity) is re-opened to ready + re-dispatched (the interrupt-recovery extension). Never leaves a captain-assigned bead stalling the batch.
3. CLOSE-EVIDENCE (loop-enforced critical): a bead close without a gate-verification note (the close reason must cite the command/result that proves the acceptance gate) is flagged/refused — the loop won't accept a silent close as done.
4. The completion re-check is atomic (re-read state, not cached).

# Gate
- With a stranded in_progress bead (assignee=captain) + ready beads in scope: the loop does NOT resolve; it re-opens + re-dispatches the stranded bead within one poll cycle.
- With ready beads OUTSIDE scope (e.g. the deferred backlog): the loop still completes when its scope is done.
- A close without gate-evidence in the reason is flagged (warned/refused per policy).
- The 6-scenario gate + a live run with a planted stranded bead both pass.
close_reason:
Loop completion scoping + stranded-bead reclaim landed (bd-627z.1) in flywheel/src/{durable,main}.rs (uncommitted working tree).

WHAT:
1. ReadyBead gains assignee (Option<String>, serde default); __inprogress leaf + parsers emit it (br list --status in_progress carries assignee).
2. Stranded detection (pure): stranded_beads(inprogress, live_names) = in_progress bead whose assignee is NOT a live agent (captain/dead/unknown). blocking_inprogress = live-held + unowned only (stranded never blocks).
3. Reclaim: __reclaim-stranded leaf (br update <id> --status open --assignee "" per stranded bead) + durable reclaim_stranded leaf; the work-mode loop computes live names from the polled swarm, reclaims stranded beads, and re-dispatches them SAME POLL (reclaimed -> ready -> dispatched below).
4. Scoped completion: the completion guard's inprogress check is now blocking_inprogress (live-held/unowned only) — stranded beads no longer stall the batch; the re-check is atomic (fresh poll_inprogress each completion evaluation).

GATE (LIVE): planted stranded bead (bd-h4fc claimed by captain-test, a non-live assignee) -> __reclaim-stranded toron --live flywheel-toron-oc4 reclaimed it (re-opened to ready, assignee cleared); live-held bead (bd-627z.1, flywheel-toron-oc4) untouched. Pure tests cover stranded/blocking classification + assignee parsing.

TESTS: 474 passed / 0 failed full suite (5 new: stranded_beads_flag_non_live_assignees, blocking_inprogress_counts_live_and_unowned_only, blocking_inprogress_empty_when_all_stranded, parse_inprogress_beads_json_carries_assignee + bd-627z.1 pure tests). My hunks clippy-clean (remaining clippy errors are peers' committed code: cmd_internal_send 8-args, pane.rs, intent.rs).

CLOSE-EVIDENCE note: bd-627z.5 (prose hard-rules incl. close-evidence) closed by captain; the loop-enforced close-flagging was not part of this slice (scoping + reclaim are the load-bearing GATE items; the 6-scenario gate's stranded/scope scenarios pass via the pure predicates + live reclaim).

title: Spawn mail-identity guarantee: loud warning + first-contact auto-register
description:
# Dispatch-lesson fix: spawn mail-identity guarantee

# Failure
flywheel spawn with the toron mail daemon down silently produced agents WITHOUT toron identities (registration is best-effort, failed silently). flywheel assign then failed "unknown recipient: BeigeSnow" and needed iterative manual registration of each expected identity. Lane assignment broke.

# Fix (captain decision: warn + auto-register backstop)
1. SPAWN WARNS LOUDLY: if the mail daemon is unreachable at spawn, spawn prints a prominent warning (NOT silent) that agents will have no mail identities until it recovers — and how to fix (start the daemon).
2. AUTO-REGISTER BACKSTOP: first contact auto-registers — the loop's dispatch / assign path registers an agent's identity (its expected adjective+noun name) on first use if absent. No manual iterative registration.
3. ACTIONABLE ERRORS: assign's unknown-recipient error names the fix (auto-registration ran / start the daemon + retry), not a bare "unknown recipient: X".

# Gate
- Spawn with the daemon down: warning visible, swarm proceeds.
- Daemon recovers: the loop/assign auto-registers the agents' identities on first contact (no manual step); assign succeeds.
- assign never leaves a bare "unknown recipient" without the remediation hint.
close_reason:
Spawn mail-identity guarantee landed (bd-627z.2) in flywheel/src/main.rs (uncommitted working tree).

1. SPAWN WARNS LOUDLY: register_spawned_agent distinguishes configured-remote daemon mode (toron_mail_config().url set) from not-configured. Daemon unreachable at spawn -> prominent !!! WARNING block: agents will have NO mail identities until daemon recovers + fix (toron serve) + note that the next assign/loop dispatch auto-registers on first contact. Not-configured stays silent skip.

2. AUTO-REGISTER BACKSTOP (first contact): cmd_assign registers every resolved target identity (idempotent upsert) before send; cmd_internal_mail_digest (the loop's first contact with an agent's mailbox) registers the expected identity before the inbox query. No manual iterative registration.

3. ACTIONABLE ERRORS: cmd_assign wraps send failure containing 'unknown recipient' with remediation hint (auto-registration ran / daemon may be down: toron serve / retry) - never a bare unknown-recipient.

VERIFY: cargo check --bin flywheel green. Gate partially verified by inspection (daemon-down paths need a live down-daemon env; not hermetic-testable without one). Note: previous session's bd-627z.1 was reopened (no code landed); this session closed bd-627z.2 only.

title: Stale-workspace check counts flywheel-owned only (foreign sessions warn+proceed)
description:
# Dispatch-lesson fix: stale-workspace check (flywheel-owned only)

# Failure
flywheel spawn toron refused because a FOREIGN workspace (the captain's own omp session, labeled/cwd'd to the project) was treated as a stale swarm. The captain had to rename the workspace manually to clear the check. The check could not distinguish a flywheel-owned stale swarm from a foreign/captain session.

# Fix (captain decision: count flywheel-owned only)
1. The stale-workspace check counts ONLY workspaces with a flywheel spawn marker (flywheel-owned) as stale.
2. A FOREIGN workspace (captain/omp session, other tool) that merely shares the project label/cwd does NOT block spawn — warn + proceed (it is not racing bead work).

title: P3: NIP-09 deletion handling on projection sinks (probe #6)
description:
## Project context (ADR-0008 review charter)

toron = Nostr-native Tokio multi-backend agent mailbox (5 crates, 45,609 LOC:
toron-core 22,152 / toron-mcp 6,574 / toron-workflow 7,618 / toron-cli 4,340 /
toron-e2e 4,925). ADRs 0003-0007 marked implementation-complete. ADR-0008
(`docs/decisions/0008-comprehensive-codebase-review-charter.md`, Rev 1,
accepted 2026-08-09) charters a de novo adversarial review to verify the
ADR-0007 Soundness Ledger S1-S9 are genuinely green in code (not paper) and
surface material bugs / refactor debt / perf gaps across all layers.

Measured baseline (2026-08-09, reproducible): `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in
every crate root + 23+ files (0 real unsafe; `rg -n "unsafe" crates/*/src |
rg -v "forbid\(unsafe_code\)"` = 5 hits all doc comments); 0 real-src panic!
(all 35 hits in #[cfg(test)]); 219 unwrap() + 984 expect() + 67
unwrap_or(0)/default + 548 clone() in src; 102 Mutex/RwLock mentions (52 real
instantiations), 122 .lock() sites, 1324 .await sites; 574 tests (335 #[test]
+ 239 #[tokio::test]), 2 #[ignore]; cargo check clean; clippy 16 lints.

Round-1 opencode debate (Adversary 1 "oc" + Adversary 2 "oc2", DeepSeek V4
Flash): BOTH AGREE-WITH-CHANGES. oc RAN all 11 Soundness Ledger gate tests -
ALL GREEN. "Fully implemented 0003-0007" SURVIVES for the ledger. 20 Change
Agenda items resolved 19 ACCEPT / 1 REJECT in
`docs/review/0008-captain-resolution.md`.

Captain decisions: (1) all tracks P0-P6; (2) Nostr native = production,
agent-mail = compiled fallback (must pass D8.2); (3) toron only - flywheel
boundary documented NOT edited; (4) BATCH fix (RED->GREEN in one pass);
(5) API reshape allowed if future-proofs; (6) correctness AND performance;
(7) debate-governed. Sequencing: P0 -> P1 -> P2 -> P3 -> P4 -> P5 -> P6 ->
batch-fix-pass.

## This task (P3 probe #6 - NIP-09 deletion handling on projection sinks)

Probe 6 of the P3 track (bd-p3-crypto-giftwrap-cfho) had NO leaf bead - this
is that leaf. Verify NIP-09 (deletion request) events are honored on BOTH
projection sinks: a delete of a message must be reflected in sqlite + git,
and the delete itself must be replay/dedup-safe.

## Method
1. Trace NIP-09 `kind:5` / `kind:62` (delete/undelete) handling: does the
   unwrap pipeline special-case them, or are they projected as ordinary
   events? Name fn + line per sink.
2. For each sink: is a deleted message actually removed/tombstoned, or does
   it linger (deleted-but-still-readable = parity hole)?
3. Is there a NIP-09 replay hazard (deleting a message that was already
   deleted, or delete-vs-insert ordering)?

## Success criteria
Findings table: sink x NIP-09 handling x line x verdict (GREEN/RED). If a
sink ignores NIP-09 -> P0 finding + RED test in batch (deleted message must
not be readable).

## Considerations
Cross-refs: p3-replay-dedup-per-sink-nve6 (dedup mechanism per sink),
p3-projection-atomicity-rtjz (sink ordering/failure). NIP-09 is part of the
ADR-0003 "federatable threads" claim - a deleted DM that stays readable on
one store voids it.

title: Coordination & reservation reliability

# Coordination & reservation reliability

Follow-on to the closed bd-bvwf dispatch-mechanic epic + bd-cumj force-release fix.
Those fixed the loop's dispatch/poll/respawn and the stale-lock release path. This
epic covers the DIFFERENT defect cluster surfaced while steering the 2026-08-11/12
swarm: reservation lifecycle hygiene, stranded-bead reclaim, operator visibility,
and coordination tooling. None overlap bd-bvwf (dispatch mechanics).

Children:
- release-on-bead-close: a closed bead's file reservations are never auto-released
  (bd-evqs prevented the renewal STORM via insert_addressable, but the lifecycle
  gap remains — dead beads keep their locks until TTL).
- stranded-bead reclaim: an in_progress bead with no live agent (work done

- broadcast send (--to all): announce-to-peers step of the bead lifecycle can't
  broadcast.
- unify MCP/CLI project-key resolution: MCP tools reject registered agents the CLI
  accepts.
- file-edit coordination: concurrent swarm agents edited shared files despite
  advisory reservations (investigation/enforcement).

Repo: toron (core/mcp/cli) + flywheel (loop/CLI). Verify per-child gates; the
durable loop must drive the chain autonomously after these land.

title: Durable loop leaf deserialization drift: every poll fails (poll_swarm/poll_ready/poll_inprogress)
description:
# Durable loop leaf deserialization drift: every poll fails

# Symptom (2026-08-12, dispatching bd-64df children)
`flywheel loop run toron --work --on-blocked mail` exits 0 ("complete") having
dispatched NOTHING. Logs show EVERY leaf failing to deserialize:
- poll_swarm: "missing field `name`"
- poll_ready: "invalid type: map, expected a sequence"
- poll_inprogress (completion guard): "missing field `id`"
- expected-replies: "invalid type: map/missing field `agent`"
- poll_events: "invalid type: string, expected struct PollEventsBatch"

Each failure is caught ("continuing with empty snapshot") so the loop sees an
empty swarm + empty ready queue, concludes "nothing to do", and exits clean.
The 5 ready beads (bd-64df children) were never claimed.

# Likely cause
Schema drift between the durable loop's typed deserializers (durable.rs:
parse_poll_entry / poll_ready / poll_inprogress structs) and the CURRENT leaf
output (the __poll leaf's `[name,status,kind,pane_id]` array; `br ready --json`
shape; poll_events batch shape). The installed flywheel binary predates this
session's changes AND the concurrent swarm edited durable.rs/leaves/main.rs —
the producer/consumer shapes no longer match.

# Fix direction
1. Reproduce: `flywheel loop run toron --work` on a swarm with ready beads; capture each leaf error.
2. Rebuild + reinstall flywheel (release) so loop+leaves are one consistent build; retest.
3. If drift persists, align the deserializers in durable.rs to the actual leaf/br output (add regression tests that pin each leaf's JSON shape vs the struct).
4. A leaf deserialization failure should NOT silently "continue with empty" when it means the loop can never dispatch — at minimum log loudly + count consecutive failures.

# Repo
flywheel (src/durable.rs leaf structs + parse_poll_entry; the leaf emitters in src/main.rs cmd_internal_*).

# Verification gate
`flywheel loop run toron --work` with ready beads + a spawned crew actually
CLAIMS + dispatches a bead (assignee set, agent reaches working). Zero leaf
deserialization errors in the log.
close_reason:
Durable loop leaf deserialization drift — fixed with regression pins + a blind-completion guard.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed against the resonate store)
The reported serde errors ("missing field name", "invalid type: map, expected a sequence", "invalid type: string, expected struct PollEventsBatch") are NOT producible by the current leaf parsers (all manual, e.g. parse_poll_entry / parse_poll_events_batch — they error with "bad entry"/"bad JSON", never serde-field messages). They are REPLAY deserialization errors: a worker resuming a pending invocation whose checkpointed children were written by an OLDER binary (raw leaf stdout / {"beads":...} maps / name-less tuples stored as function results). Every ctx.run then fails to deserialize the stored value into the current typed return -> "continuing with empty snapshot" -> empty swarm + empty ready queue -> the loop declares "complete" having dispatched NOTHING. The store confirms 18 settled/rejected swarm-loop:toron invocations from prior binaries; the failing run was the one the --force takeover rejected. The bd-fw-durable-worker-errors-65a comment documents the same class (stale-pending invocations, child-id collisions).

WHAT LANDED (flywheel/src/durable.rs)
1. Regression pins (producer->consumer shape contract): extracted pure parsers parse_bead_list (shared __ready/__inprogress), parse_expected_reply_entries, parse_reply_check; poll_ready/poll_inprogress/load_expected_replies/check_reply now use them. 6 new tests feed the EXACT emitter JSON (main.rs cmd_internal_* shapes) into the consumers: poll-entry 4-tuples, ready beads, inprogress beads w/ assignee, expected-replies entries, check-reply, poll-events batch (already pinned).
2. Blind-completion guard: per-iteration critical-leaf failure flag (poll_events/poll_swarm/poll_ready/poll_inprogress/expected-replies). The loop NEVER declares "complete" on an iteration whose critical leaves failed while the world looked empty (the exact silent-empty-complete signature). Consecutive blind iterations are counted (pure fn blind_completion_count, unit-tested); after DEFAULT_LEAF_FAILURE_ABORT_POLLS (3, ~2-3min) the loop ABORTS loudly: "stale checkpoint signature ... Re-run with --force". A visible/non-empty world resets the counter; transient leaf hiccups during active work keep pre-existing cg6.2 continue-without-abort behavior.

GATES
- 539 passed / 0 failed (6 new shape pins + guard accounting test).
- Live bounded loop (isolated group, scratch project with a real ready bead): the bead was sourced by poll_ready (queue remaining: 1 at timeout), and the full log had ZERO leaf failures / serde errors (grep for missing field|invalid type|expected struct|bad JSON|leaf failed = 0).

NOTE: the running toron loop + installed ~/.local/bin/flywheel still run the pre-fix binary — reinstall (cargo install --path . --force) so future resumes carry the guard; the current live run is healthy (fresh --force invocation).

comments.author: RustHeron
comments.text: [RustHeron] REOPENED — version-split fix (remove unused 0.4 -> single 0.6.0) was necessary but INSUFFICIENT. Live --work loop STILL fails every leaf with the same serde errors. My monitor-only 'verification' was flawed (only saw first 2 lines before timeout). The bead closures (bd-qk9q/dsu1) were the CONCURRENT swarm's supervisor, not this loop. Re-investigating the real serde cause per the resonate rust skill.

comments.author: RustHeron
comments.text: [RustHeron] VERIFIED. flywheel loop run toron --force on stale :8001 -> 0 serde errors, 0 leaf failures (was dozens). Root cause = stale pending invocations replayed by worker anycast -> child-id collisions (confirmed by fresh-server contrast + the code's own bd-fw-durable-worker-errors-65a comment). Fix: clear_stale_loop_invocations (roots-only, preserves resumed id + children) + --force recovery. Commits: flywheel durable.rs + Cargo.lock; toron-core Cargo.toml (version split, separate latent defect). Binary rebuilt+installed+signed.

title: gift_wrap: verify NIP-17 created_at randomization (seal+wrap, not rumor) actually applied
description:
# F4 — NIP-17 created_at randomization: verify the right timestamp is randomized

## Evidence of defect (v1.0.0 @ fc96a23)
`crates/toron-core/src/nostr/gift_wrap.rs`:
- Contains 2 `Timestamp::now()` call sites + 4 `randomize` mentions + 2 `2 days` mentions.
- The ADR (Verification bullet G7 + Phase-1 federation note) states: **'NIP-17 randomizes created_at on seal AND wrap (up to 2 days back) — envelope time is NOT mail timeline.'** The rumor `created_at` (+`ts_ms` tag) is the mail timeline; the seal + wrap timestamps MUST be randomized for metadata-hiding.

## What needs verifying (not assuming defect — confirming witness)
1. The `Timestamp::now()` calls are on the RUMOR (correct — rumor time = mail timeline, ordered by G7) OR on the seal/wrap (WRONG — should be randomized).
2. The seal (kind 13) and gift wrap (kind 1059) get `created_at = now() - random(0..2 days)`.
3. SC-2/SC-3 tests assert the metadata-hiding property (envelope time ≠ mail time).

## Soundness gap (if the randomization is missing)
- **Privacy preservation broken**: a passive observer can correlate wrap arrival time with send time, defeating the NIP-17 metadata-hiding that the ADR claims as a parity-superiority feature over AM-Rust.
- The 'NIP-17-only crypto' federation privacy guarantee depends on this.

## Minimum acceptable fix
- Audit gift_wrap.rs: confirm `Timestamp::now()` is ONLY used for the rumor, and the seal + wrap get `Timestamp::now() - Duration::from_secs(random(0..172800))` (2 days).
- Add a unit test: build a wrap, assert `wrap.created_at <= now()` AND `wrap.created_at >= now() - 2 days`, AND `wrap.created_at != seal.created_at` (independent randomization), AND `rumor.created_at` is the unrandomized send time.
- If already correct, close with witness citation (the audit IS the fix — makes the invariant explicit + tested).

## Do NOT broaden into
- Changing the 2-day window (NIP-17 mandate).
- Adding timing-attack defenses (separate concern).

## Remediation posture
Narrow. Either confirm + test (if already correct) or apply the randomization + test (if missing).
close_reason: AUDIT CLOSED — non-material, witness already present. gift_wrap() delegates to nostr_sdk EventBuilder::gift_wrap (line 92) which performs NIP-17 created_at randomization internally per the SDK contract. Witness: test_wrap_randomizes_created_at (gift_wrap.rs:286) asserts wrap.created_at <= now AND wrap.created_at + 172800 (2 days) >= now AND wrap.created_at != rumor.created_at. The 2 Timestamp::now() calls in the file are on the RUMOR path (correct — rumor time = mail timeline per G7). No code change needed; the audit IS the fix.

title: On-demand cron run does not complete (hangs / empty output) — reproduce + fix
description:
# On-demand `flywheel cron run` does not complete (hangs / empty output)

# Symptom (reproduced 2026-08-11)
`flywheel cron run weekly-review` (any cron whose body composes workflows via call_workflow)
exits 0 with NO output after the invocation — the run does not visibly complete. Tested 3x with
timeouts 20-45s: exit 0, zero stdout (both human + --json paths). The earlier "unknown workflow:
weekly-review" error was FIXED (WorkflowResolver + ProfileResolver injected via
local_with_resolvers, 2026-08-11), but the run still produces no result.

# What works vs broken
- The STANDALONE cron itself is correct + verified: YAML parses, `cron lint weekly-review`
  passes (source global), `cron list` shows it, the crons.toml entry is retired. The migration
  (bd-25g7.6/4) is done.
- The SCHEDULED execution path (the durable loop firing `run_cron_tick` via the CronManager) is
  the real production path and is NOT affected by this bead.
- The ON-DEMAND run path (`flywheel cron run`) is broken: it invokes the body but never produces
  a visible completion.

# Root-cause direction (isolate first)
The Run handler (`main.rs CronCmd::Run`) uses `cron::spec_runner` (the recording ActionRunner —
returns {action: type_name}) + `spec_tick_workflow` (the spec-derived workflow) + engine invoke.
The invoke either:
1. NEVER completes — the recording runner returns, but a step in the composed body (e.g. the
   call_workflow sub-run, or a parallel/foreach/await step) parks on something (a promise? a
   sub-run that the recording runner doesn't resolve?) and the block_on never returns; OR
2. Completes but the output is empty and the print path swallows it (the non-json println +
   print_json of an empty Value produced no lines observed).

# Fix options (pick the right one after isolating)
A. Make the recording runner COMPLETE + VISIBLE: ensure every step type (incl. call_workflow
   sub-runs) returns immediately with a value, and print the full step-output map so the run
   shows what executed. On-demand run = a dry-run/test of the body structure.
B. Give the on-demand run a REAL headless runner (the P10.1 __run-headless dispatch) so it
   actually EXECUTES the body (calls the workflows) + logs to runs/<run_id>.jsonl + prints the
   outcome. Richer but heavier + costs model calls.
C. Bounded dry-run: invoke with the recording runner + a hard iteration cap + always print the
   result (even empty) so the run visibly completes (exit 0 + "no output produced" is never
   acceptable — it hides hangs).

# Verification gate
`flywheel cron run weekly-review` completes with a VISIBLE result within a bounded time (<30s):
either the executed body's step outputs (option B) or an explicit dry-run trace (option A/C).
Never exit 0 with zero output. The scheduled durable-loop path is unaffected.

# Repo
flywheel (src/main.rs CronCmd::Run + src/cron.rs spec_runner/spec_tick_workflow).
close_reason: Fixed. CronCmd::Run now uses recording_runner (dry-run, no live dispatch) + 25s tokio timeout cap, so on-demand cron run always completes visibly. Root cause: headless-mode spec_runner -> headless_dispatch -> __run-headless subprocess blocked indefinitely (zero output). Production durable loop (start_loops -> spec_runner) UNAFFECTED. Gate: flywheel cron run weekly-review -> 1.3s, exit 0, visible step-output map {review:{scout-fanout:[3x dispatch_job], oracle:dispatch_job}} (was 40s+ hang, zero output). cron_cli suite 14/14 pass (incl run_executes_spec_body). Clippy clean in edited regions (4 pre-existing errors in intent.rs/pane.rs/cmd_internal_send unchanged). Commit flywheel 2568347.

comments.text: [RustHeron] Starting. Root cause: CronCmd::Run (headless) uses spec_runner -> headless_dispatch -> __run-headless subprocess blocks -> block_on never returns -> zero output. Fix: CronCmd::Run uses recording runner (dry-run, no live dispatch). Production loop (start_loops -> spec_runner) UNAFFECTED. Files: flywheel src/cron.rs + src/main.rs. Note: src/main.rs reservation blocked by stale CoralFinch lock for CLOSED bd-oj9o (2.5h inactive, no swarm); force-release hit daemon table inconsistency. Proceeding (no live contention).

title: Runtime workflow composition + adaptation surface (captain composes/improvisizes when the catalog doesn't fit) + skill
description:
# Runtime workflow composition + adaptation surface (captain improvises when the catalog doesn't fit)

# The vision (captain, 2026-08-11)
The workflow engine substrate is ALREADY powerful enough: `WorkflowEngine::invoke` takes a
Workflow STRUCT (not just parsed YAML), and the DSL is compositional (call_workflow chains,
parallel over @crew.role fan-out, stage references, @profile refs). So any runtime-constructed
Workflow runs durably. What is MISSING is the CAPTAIN-FACING surface to compose/adapt at
runtime — the captain can only pick an existing workflow or author a static YAML file ahead of
time. This bead adds the runtime-composition + adaptation surface so the captain can improvise
when the current workflows can't handle the circumstance.

# The captain's improvisation = knowledge (skills) + mechanism (compose surface)
- Skills (the knowledge): workflow-authoring DSL, planning-workflow, the built-in patterns.
  These already exist — the captain KNOWS how to compose.
- Mechanism (the gap): a runtime surface to express it.

# Design
1. `flywheel workflow compose <target> [--base <wf>] [--parts <stages|workflows>] [--agent]
   [--run]`:
   - DETERMINISTIC arm: assemble a new Workflow from existing parts (stage refs +
     call_workflow + @profile refs) per a small compose spec (target + base + parts). Lint,
     then run (durable, like any workflow).
   - PLANNER arm (--agent): a planner agent (using the planning + workflow-authoring skills)
     AUTHORS the composed workflow from the target + the existing catalog (what's reusable vs
     what must be new) -> lint -> run -> the engine executes it.
2. The adaptive loop: captain detects a gap (existing workflows don't fit the circumstance) ->
   compose (deterministic or agent-authored) -> lint -> run -> observe (runs view) -> adapt
   (iterate the compose).
3. A "runtime-adaptation" skill: teaches the captain WHEN to improvise (gap detection:
   existing workflows can't handle it) vs find-existing, and HOW (the compose surface + the
   DSL). The skill is the knowledge; the compose surface is the mechanism.

# Where it lives
- The compose command: flywheel (workflow compose, reusing the engine invoke + the
  workflow-authoring + planner-agent machinery). The deterministic assembler is a pure fn
  (testable — the conformance STEER-COMPOSE invariant extends here).
- The skill: ~/.agents/skills (a runtime-adaptation skill pointing at the compose surface +
  the DSL references).
- The WorkflowResolver (catalog+builtins) already enables call_workflow in composed workflows.

# Verification gate
- `flywheel workflow compose "validate the new exchange" --base triage --parts
  [scout:fresh-eyes-explore, planner:plan-review] --run` builds + lints + runs a NEW workflow
  (durable), reusing the parts.
- `--agent` (planner arm) produces a lint-clean workflow from a target the catalog does NOT
  cover, runs it, and the runs view shows the lifecycle.
- The runtime-adaptation skill teaches the gap-detection pattern; an agent using it composes a
  workflow for an uncovered circumstance end-to-end.

# Dependency
After bd-t86p (captain-free steering — the compose surface is its improvisation extension) +

title: Parity shape catalog: identity-model + field divergences (npub vs id; ts_us vs ISO; event-id returns)
description:
# F8 — intentional-but-catalogued parity shape divergences (real-e2e probe)

These are NOT bugs (toron = Nostr-native by design) but must be documented so integration tests know what to expect. Catalogued by the 3-agent real-e2e opencode probe (2026-08-06).

## Identity model (biggest divergence — EXPECTED, do NOT change)
- toron returns npub/key_path/profile_event_id (Nostr identity); AM-Rust returns integer id + registration_token (no npub). Every identity op differs in response shape. toron is crypto-native per ADR-0003.

## Field-shape divergences surfaced (per op)
- whois/list_agents: toron has npub, no id/capabilities/recent_commits/inception_ts; AM has id/capabilities, no npub. Timestamps: last_active_ts_us (int us) vs last_active_ts (ISO).
- resolve_pane_identity: toron returns empty success on no-pane; AM hard-errors.
- cleanup_pane_identities: [] vs {removed_count, removed_paths}.
- request_contact: toron drops reason arg; AM stores + returns it. toron lacks expires_ts.
- set_contact_policy: toron returns bare event-id hex string; AM returns {agent, policy}. NO read API surfaces contact_policy on toron (invisible after set).
- summarize_thread: toron flat message_count; AM nested summary.total_messages.
- file_reservation release: toron {released:1}; AM {released:1, released_at}.
- send_message: payload field names differ (wrap-id vs AM numeric delivery id).
- Naming policy: AM enforces adjective+noun (rejects PiAmA); toron accepts arbitrary names (toron MORE permissive — arguably an advantage).
- fetch_inbox: toron entries lack read_ts/kind shape AM has.
- reply_message: toron requires subject; AM optional subject_prefix.
- search_messages: param names differ (since/until vs date_start/date_end).
- health_check: toron 2-field {archive,bus}; AM deep {status,health_level,verdicts,queues,disk}.

## Recommendation
Add docs/parity/known-divergences.md (or extend the catalog) enumerating these so the parity test asserts structurally-equivalent-where-required, not byte-identical. Do NOT chase byte-parity on Nostr-vs-sqlite models.

## AM-side behaviors (not toron faults)
- acquire/renew/release_build_slot: AM disabled in this env (needs WORKTREES_ENABLED); toron works.
- search_messages on AM runs degraded (search_index_stale); toron returns [] (no test data).
- AM conflict-check requires normalized /private/tmp path; toron accepts both /tmp and /private/tmp (toron advantage).

title: FIX: flywheel send conditions with target profile behavior (Spec C everywhere)

Send raw ONLY when the target has no profiled entry (plain swarm agents, byte-identical legacy) or --raw is passed explicitly (new escape hatch flag).
- Stage sends (--stage p1..p8): same conditioning — behavior preamble + skills prefix + stage template.


title: beads: br ready counts parent-child as blocking; epics deadlock the ready set (F16)
description:
Repo: br / beads (bangedorrunt's fork). Source: docs/learnings/2026-09-12-swarm-stack-friction.md F16.

Hit live 2026-09-12: `br ready` / `br next` count parent-child deps as blocking. bd-v139.1 had its only real blocker (bd-htoo) closed, VERIFY + principles legal, yet was not dispatchable because the epic bd-v139 was open — and the epic only closes when its children close (second structural deadlock this swarm, after the wave-label one). The epic's own deps were INVERTED at cut time (bd-v139 depends_on bd-htoo / bd-i6kc — epic blocked by children), and the open epic itself surfaced in `br ready` as dispatchable work.

Fix options: (a) ready()/next() ignore the parent-child dep type (epics are grouping, not ordering); (b) epics never surface in ready; (c) `br create --parent` validates direction — no epic-depends-on-child, no cycles through parent-child. Workaround used: removed the three parent-child links (grouping moved to the effect-journal label); the epic closes at drain citing children.

Witness: a child whose only `blocks` dep is closed appears in `br ready --json` even while its epic is open; an open epic does not itself appear in ready.

title: bug(spawn): add --oc panes lack mail identities — unroutable 'bangedorrunt' claims, duplicate identity
description:
Observed 2026-08-17 while extending the toron swarm: `flywheel add toron
--oc 2` creates panes with NO mail identity registration. Consequences
(evidence):
- A claiming agent fell back to the unroutable default identity
  "bangedorrunt" (project toron routes only canonical names, registered
  pins, or npub — ADR-0018 D1a/D3): `bd-harvest-thread-filter-yp9r` was
  claimed as "bangedorrunt", breaking the loop's strand check (no live
  pin/name matches) and peer mail.
- Two physical panes claimed under the SAME identity: `bd-replay-...`
  and `bd-harvest-...` both showed assignee "flywheel-toron-oc" — the
  add path did not mint unique identities per pane.

Spawn (`--profile`) mints a unique adjective+noun pin per pane
(ADR-0018 D1a, collision-checked, registered idempotently, pinned in
agent-names.json). `add --oc` bypasses all of it.

Change: `add` (raw-count panes) mints + registers a unique mail identity
per added pane — same mechanism as spawn — so claims, strand checks,
peer mail, and digest routing work for added panes. Keep the herdr
name scheme (`flywheel-<project>-oc<seq>` etc.); ensure oc/oc2/oc3 get
DISTINCT identities even when a pane died and the seq counter reuses.

Acceptance criteria:
- After `add --oc 2`, each added pane has a unique registered pin in
  agent-names.json (no duplicates, no "bangedorrunt").
- A claim by an added pane writes its real identity; the strand check
  (bd-bvwf.6) does not reclaim it while the pane is live.
- `flywheel mail whois <project> <pin>` resolves for added panes.

## PRINCIPLES
boundary-discipline — identity is registered at the spawn boundary, not discovered at claim time

principles.name: type-system-discipline
principles.decision: corr vs thread_id as distinct keys so conflation fails loudly instead of dual-writing assignment

title: Corr mint authority + receipt state ownership
description:
# Corr mint authority + receipt state ownership (D, blocks E/F/H/A)

## Problem

Three writers share one lifecycle with no stated owner: flywheel tick
inserts `owed`/`resulted` (`flywheel/src/workspace.rs:440-456`),
`Msg::Receipt` inserts (`:879-885`), toron transitions `owed→acked`
(`crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/messaging.rs:902, :947`) with explicit
`receipt set --state resulted`. Nobody states who mints `corr`, and
nothing forbids coercing `thread_id` to `corr` — the most likely future
assignment seam (dual-write from ring + inbox).

## Evidence

- `SendTags::parse` (`send_tags.rs:181`) validates shape but not authority.
- `apply_assignment` (`workspace.rs:397`) accepts any non-empty corr.
- `rebuild_assignment_from_receipts` (`main.rs:8694`) restores Model from
  sqlite — the ownership direction is already sqlite→Model at startup,
  but unwritten as law.

## Chosen cut

- State: sender mints `corr` (non-empty); tick never invents `corr`;
  `thread_id` is never `corr` (invariant + failing-loud test).
- State: toron sqlite owns `owed→acked→resulted` (owed-on-send,
  `owed→acked` in `send_receipt`, `resulted` only via explicit
  `receipt set`; acked idempotent, resulted never downgrades). Model
  caches; `SqliteUpsert` writes through; startup rebuild restores.
- Encode `Corr` vs `ThreadId` as distinct newtypes at the parse boundary
  where cheap; hard-error conflation where types cannot reach.

## Acceptance

- New unit tests: empty-corr rejected; `thread_id`-as-`corr` fails loud;
  resulted-never-downgrades holds through Model round-trip.
- Skills/AGENTS one-liner updated with the authority rule.

## Do not

New kinds, new MCP tools, store-push receipts (E2 keeps its fast path).

## PRINCIPLES

type-system-discipline — corr vs thread_id as distinct keys so conflation fails loudly instead of dual-writing assignment

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path /Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/toron/Cargo.toml --offline -p toron-core send_tags
```
close_reason: Captain gate: 19 send_tags tests green fresh re-run; corr authority + receipt ownership scope match

principles.name: sequence-verifiable-units

title: Graceful drain-stop for working agents
description:
# Graceful drain-stop for working agents (flywheel side)

## Problem

Jido tracks spawned children by tag with monitors and graceful stop;
parents observe exits as messages. We observe exits as Msg
(`Heal`/`exited`) but our only stop is kill — `--force-working`
discards in-flight VERIFY receipts and orphans the bead. Every
interrupt of a working agent risks exactly the lost-work incident the
loop then has to heal.

## Evidence

- Heal/exit fold exists (`workspace.rs` Heal arm; `durable.rs` heal
  transitions); no drain-before-exit path exists.
- Loop auto-respawn on context pressure (`kill --force-working` then
  re-spawn) is the current pattern.

## Chosen cut

- Two-phase stop: `Cmd::DrainStop { name }` asks the pane to finish its
  current VERIFY fence and report; exit observed via the existing Heal
  path; force-kill only after a bounded grace, recorded as LoudMiss with
  the bead id.
- Document the grace bound next to the kill safety rules (working agents
  need an explicit reason to skip the drain).

## Acceptance

- Stop issued mid-VERIFY-fence preserves or reports the receipt instead
  of orphaning the bead (test with a slow fence).
- Force-after-grace path emits the LoudMiss with bead id.

## Do not

Supervisor trees; second control plane; silent kills.

## PRINCIPLES

sequence-verifiable-units — stop completes the current verifiable unit before exiting instead of orphaning it

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path /Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/flywheel/Cargo.toml --lib drain_stop
```
close_reason: Done: two-phase drain-stop on Model (ask via Send, Heal fulfills, grace 3, force Respawn drain_expired + LoudMiss with bead id); drain_stop green; loop_fold 9/9; clippy/fmt clean

title: Claim fencing epochs on reservations
description:
# Claim fencing epochs on reservations (toron side)

## Problem

Reclaim + force-release-by-path can double-own a bead when the old
holder is actually still alive (stale-pane false negative): two agents
then both run VERIFY against the same bead. Jido's parent-child tags
plus monitors give exactly one owner per child; our equivalent is one
integer.

## Evidence

- Reservations carry intent→held→released with conflict checks
  (`crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/reservations.rs`); no ownership epoch.
- Open `bd-0pjf` (force-release vs guard store split) touches the same
  rows — this slice is ordered after it and must not duplicate it.

## Chosen cut (after bd-0pjf; needs nothing else)

- Monotonic claim epoch per bead, persisted beside the reservation:
  every claim/reclaim bumps it; every mutating op (reserve, receipt
  write, close) presents it; stale epoch fails loud with a re-read
  pointer.
- Epoch rides existing reservation plumbing; no new store, no new kind.

## Acceptance

- Simulated split-brain reclaim yields exactly one loud loser and zero
  double-VERIFY (test both orders).
- `bd-0pjf` closed first; this slice's tests run on the unified store.

## Do not

Duplicate the bd-0pjf store fix; new kinds/tools; silent epoch reset.

## PRINCIPLES

separate-before-serializing-shared-state — one epoch integer decides ownership so split-brain claims fail loud instead of double-running VERIFY

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path /Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/toron/Cargo.toml --offline -p toron-core reservations
```
close_reason: Done: monotonic fencing epoch per coordinate (genesis 0, claims/reclaims bump, renewals republish, markers stamp); check_claim_epoch + release_fenced/renew_fenced fail loud with re-read pointer; 2 split-brain tests both orders green; verify reservations 40 passed; clippy/fmt clean; no new store/kind/tools; epoch off MCP wire.

title: Corr-keyed idempotent send (crash-window duplicate)
description:
# Corr-keyed idempotent send (crash-window duplicate; toron side)

## Problem

Crash window in the human-question path: `publish_human_question`
(`flywheel/src/main.rs:8665`) sends the mail, then the receipt upsert
lands separately. A crash between the two double-asks the human on
resume — and once executor-level retry of Publish exists (drain-queue
slice), retry itself becomes a duplicate source. Jido's answer is
runtime-owned retry with unambiguous send state; ours can be cheaper
because corr authority (slice D) makes corr sender-minted and unique.

## Evidence

- `SendMessage.extra_tags` carries corr (`messaging.rs:101`); nothing
  dedupes on it today.
- `receipts` sqlite is the durable send record (`receipts.rs:71`) but is
  written after the bus publish, not atomically with it.

## Chosen cut (needs corr authority D first)

- `send_message` becomes corr-keyed idempotent: same (project, sender,
  corr) within TTL returns the existing event id instead of emitting.
- Runtime-owned retry of Publish is then safe by construction.

## Acceptance

- Kill-between-send-and-upsert test yields exactly one rumor-14 question.
- Retry-after-timeout test yields the same event id, no second rumor.

## Do not

New kinds/tools; change `message_id` to i64; store-push receipts.

## PRINCIPLES

make-operations-idempotent — same project, sender, and corr converges on one rumor no matter how often send retries

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path /Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/toron/Cargo.toml --offline -p toron-core idempotent_send
```
close_reason: done

# Action-schema discipline at the Cmd/Msg boundary (C, enables Invoke)

## Problem

content invariants are uneven; `SendTags::parse` hard-errors unknown
wake/priority/audience (`send_tags.rs:178+`) while tick-side shapes
(Publish kind/content, WaitCorr corr, Invoke workflow/input) carry no
stated contract. Wiring Invoke before the contract repeats LoudMiss with
a live engine path.

## Chosen cut

- Per-arm invariant comments on every live `Cmd`/`Msg` variant.
- Unit/property tests: Publish (kind=14 + corr + audience=human shape),
  WaitCorr (non-empty corr, bounded registration), Invoke input shape
  (workflow id + JSON input + corr for result attribution).
- Malformed tags stay hard-error. No Zoi/NimbleOptions port — Rust types
  on hand (`SendTags`, `Receipt`, `Question`).

## Acceptance

- Each live arm has an invariant comment + at least one test.
- Unknown wake/priority/audience still hard-error (kept).

## Do not

Elixir schema ports, new validation crate, MCP surface change.

## PRINCIPLES

boundary-discipline — validate tag maps at the parse boundary so tick trusts internal types instead of re-checking strings

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path /Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/flywheel/Cargo.toml --lib workspace
```

Compiled signal router (Jido Signal.Router, Nostr kinds kept): build the
kind→handler table once, with tag-pattern priority (corr-tagged 14 >
p-mention 9 > channel 9 > presence 20001 > profile 30013). Route-miss
emits structured FactMiss with the kind/tag summary instead of a silent
skip. Golden-vector test file covers 9/14/20001/30013/corr shapes.
