principles.decision: Invoke converges on the one engine rail plus VerifySink instead of a second tick path

title: Wire Invoke to engine.invoke + VerifySink or delete arm
description:
# Wire Invoke → engine.invoke + VerifySink, or delete the arm (A)

## Problem

`Cmd::Invoke { workflow, input }` LoudMiss-prints
(`flywheel/src/main.rs:8591-8593`) while the enum advertises a real
effect. Sink exists (`make_verify_sink`, `main.rs:27903`; attached at
`:22721, :23197`; engine `VerifySink` at
`toron-workflow/src/engine/mod.rs:132, :222`) but the Cmd executor never
calls `engine.invoke`.

## Chosen cut (needs action-schema C + corr authority D first)

- Route `Invoke` to `engine.invoke` + `VerifySink`, gated by a playbook
  bead (effect-layer only — never a second tick entry), input shaped per
  the C contract (workflow id + JSON input + corr for attribution);
  **or** delete the arm with this bead if no playbook gates it.
- Playbook bead gates the invoke; MCP grows nothing (same-verb-as-CLI
  freeze; tool count stays 40).

## Acceptance

- Invoke LoudMiss gone: either live path test (invoke → sink verdict
  recorded) or arm deleted + `rg Invoke` shows guard/tests only.
- Exhaustive-match guard still green; no second tick entry (review the
  call graph: executor → engine, never executor → `workspace::tick`
  except the existing Receipt re-entry).

## Do not

Second execution path beside `engine.invoke`; ToolAdapter surface;
44-tool MCP dump; Invoke-as-tick.

## PRINCIPLES

outcome-oriented-execution — Invoke converges on the one engine rail plus VerifySink instead of a second tick path

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path /Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/flywheel/Cargo.toml --lib verify_sink
```

## Fold-in (jido-runtime review 2026-09-03)

Executor drain queue (Jido DirectiveExec): replace the inline for-loop in
`handle_workspace_cmds` with an ordered drain queue. Cmds split sync
(SqliteUpsert, Prompt enqueue, Audit) vs async (Diagnose, Respawn, Invoke,
receipt I/O); async completions re-enter as Msg in per-corr issue order;
re-entrant Cmds append to queue end (Receipt re-entry replaces the inline
re-tick); unknown arm renders structured Audit, never eprintln. Ship a
`noop` executor mode that records Cmds instead of performing them (serves
proof rounds without herdr/mailbox).
Acceptance: one slow diagnose never pushes an unrelated Prompt past the
120s presence budget.
Do not: second tick entry; executor→tick except the existing Receipt
re-entry.

title: WaitCorr held-bus wake + bounded pending_wait
description:
# WaitCorr = held-bus wake + bounded pending_wait (E)

## Problem

`Cmd::WaitCorr` is `pending_wait.insert` + batch store-peek
(`flywheel/src/main.rs:8574-8575, :8619, :8623-8663`), not the
subscribe-until toron owns (`crates/toron-cli/src/plane.rs:1409-1491`:
store fast-path, else `subscribe_trusted`, unpark on bus event or
deadline). `pending_wait` is unbounded (no TTL/cap).

## Chosen cut (needs corr authority D + S-baseline H first)

- Register WaitCorr interest on the already-held doorbell
  `subscribe_trusted` (`DOORBELL_WATCH_KINDS`); receipt event →
  `Msg::Receipt` through `tick`; deadline → timeout Msg (never silent
  drop). Store `get(corr)` stays as fast path after each wake only.
- Bound `pending_wait` (TTL + cap; deadline path removes + timeout Msg).
- No second watch child, no 200ms-class poll, no 30015.

## Acceptance

- S5-class test mirroring `live_watch_wait_corr_unparks_on_receipt`
  (`plane.rs:1704`): tasked corr unparks on bus event without poll peek;
  survives walker death via sqlite.
- Bound test: expired/over-cap waits drain with timeout Msg.

## Do not

Second doorbell; wake kind; copying the CLI fn instead of sharing the
held subscription.

## PRINCIPLES

fix-root-causes — wake on the bus event instead of masking store-peek latency with faster polling

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path /Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/toron/Cargo.toml --offline -p toron-cli adr0027_s3
```

## Fold-in (jido-runtime review 2026-09-03)

Named Schedule vocab (Jido Schedule/Cron job_id): add `Cmd::Schedule
{ job_id, delay, msg }` + `Cmd::CancelSchedule { job_id }` with job_id =
corr; re-emit of the same id replaces (no duplicate timeouts after a
crash-resume rebuild); Cancel removes. WaitCorr deadline rides Schedule
and expiry emits the timeout Msg. Same replace semantics for standalone
cron `start` (same name replaces, never duplicates dispatchers).
Acceptance: re-Publish of the same corr yields exactly one timeout;
duplicate `cron start` never double-dispatches.

title: HumanDecision corr plumbing end-to-end
description:
# HumanDecision corr plumbing end-to-end (F, live HITL as Msg)

## Problem

`publish_human_question` (`flywheel/src/main.rs:8665-8692`) sends
`captain→captain` with only `audience=human` and **no `corr` tag**, while
everything downstream keys on `corr` (`mint_human_question`,
`open_human: BTreeMap<corr, Question>`, `apply_assignment`). A human
answer has no `corr` to return — the live producer is uncorrelated, not
thin. Toron half (`SendTags.verdict` + `mail send --verdict`) is already
tracked as `bd-mail-send-verdict-flag-kfo6` — depend on it, do not
duplicate it.

## Chosen cut (needs corr authority D + S-baseline H + verdict flag)

- Publish carries `corr` (+ `result_path` where known); answer path
  `mail send --corr C --verdict approve|deny` returns exactly that corr
  (body approve/deny stays as fallback while `open_human` holds the corr).
- Exactly one `Msg::HumanDecision { corr, verdict }` closes one question;
  unknown/duplicate corr → LoudMiss (existing test kept).
- S4 proof over the live mail path with no test pre-seed.
- Mailbox mints no UI token/card/Suspend (refuse restated).

## Acceptance

- Happy path needs no pre-seeded Model: tagged answer closes exactly one
  question; duplicate answer LoudMiss.
- Old tag-less human mails: body-verdict fallback for one release, then
  LoudMiss (migration noted in close reason).

## Do not

# S-slice baseline proofs + why-fold producer (H, needs corr authority)

## Problem

S1–S5 are asserted, not proven, at grounding HEADs: tasked-survives-death
(S1), standing-empty silence (S2), role rebind after pane death (S3),
tasked unpark without poll (S5). `why --corr/--seq` fold-from-journal has
no producer contract (path, retention bound, filter bound). Wiring E/F
before baselines lets implementation grade its own homework. (S4
one-HumanDecision-per-corr over live mail moves to the human-plumbing
bead — it needs the corr tag that does not exist yet.)

## Chosen cut

- Live proofs, run against current HEADs first (record red/green
  honestly): S1 tasked corr survives walker death via sqlite rebuild
  (`rebuild_assignment_from_receipts`, `main.rs:8694`); S2 standing-empty
  silence (no Cmd, no assignment); S3 `RoleBound` rebind after pane death;
  S5 tasked unpark path characterization (current store-peek behavior
  documented, gap to bus-wake quantified).
- `why` producer contract: journal path + 5MiB/5k-style retention bound +
  corr/seq filter bound; fold `tick` from journal reproduces the
  `Vec<Cmd>` for the corr (pin-substring grep never truth).

## Acceptance

- S1/S2/S3 green on current HEAD; S5 baseline recorded with measured
  gap; failures filed as beads, not hidden.
- `why --corr/--seq` acceptance test: fold reproduces Cmd list for a corr.

## Do not

Wire WaitCorr/Invoke/Human to make proofs pass; sleep-based test waits.

## PRINCIPLES

prove-it-works — slices run against live HEADs and record red honestly instead of self-reporting green

executor outcome appends one JSONL line

becomes a rendering of the event, not the event itself. The duration

title: ADR-0005: Orchestration Tier (umbrella)
description:
# ADR-0005: Orchestration Tier — Profiles, Workflows, Stages, Smart Cron, Flexible Engine

## Why this exists (the captain's churn, resolved)
After ADR-0003 (Nostr mailbox fabric) and ADR-0004 (5 hardening ships), the captain reported **churn** around three unresolved questions:
1. Where does the orchestration vocabulary live (toron vs flywheel)?
2. The workflow engine is static AND swallows failures (no fan-out/branch/retry, no run-failure propagation).
3. Cron is fire-and-forget (the captain's hand-built docker-auto-upgrade + agent-reach-upgrade sagas have no unified, self-reporting successor).

ADR-0005 resolves all three and is **Accepted** (2-round opencode adversarial review + 3 captain amendments + 1 protocol audit). Source of truth: `docs/decisions/0005-orchestration-layer.md` (1181 lines). **These beads replace the ADR as the executable plan — they are self-contained; do not consult the ADR mid-implementation.**

## The core decision (tier model)
Execution **substrate** stays in toron; orchestration **vocabulary** goes to flywheel. One-way dependency: `flywheel → toron-workflow → toron-core` (the first arrow is NEW — P3 wires it). Standalone peer mode (two agents + a triage workflow, no orchestrator) is a CI-tested contract (`sc11`); the engine must work with no flywheel.

| Tier | Owner |
|---|---|
| 0 Identity/Transport | toron-core::nostr+bus |
| 1 Mailbox fabric + ONE Backend trait | toron-core (P1 unifies the duplicated trait) |
| 2 Execution substrate (engine, failure-path, invoke, control-flow) | toron-workflow |
| 3 Orchestration (profiles, workflows catalog, stages, smart cron, squads, runs) | flywheel |
| 4 Surfaces | toron-mcp (frozen 38 tools) + toron-cli + flywheel-cli |

## The invariants every bead obeys (non-negotiable)
1. **No new kind.** Reuse ADR-0003 frozen registry (30010-14, 30031/32, 20001, 43001-06, 46001-12).
2. **No new MCP tool.** 38-tool surface frozen. New vocabulary = CLI only.
3. **No dependency inversion.** flywheel → toron-workflow → toron-core. `spawn`'s ProfileResolver is an injected DI seam, never a flywheel import in toron.
4. **One backend trait** after P1.
5. **Resonate is the only execution substrate.** Cron manager = durable-sleep loop.
6. **Backward compat.** `triage.yaml`, the ADR-0004 suite, AND the captain's live flywheel `workflows`/`pipeline`/`recipes` runs must pass at every phase boundary.
7. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Tokio, rmcp, Schnorr identity, NIP-17 E2E — all preserved.

## The phasing (this epic's children, in execution order)
- **P0 — Failure propagation** (PREREQUISITE: blocks P4, P5). ActionRunner Result<()>→Result<Value>; on_error:fail_run; kind-46012 status=failed.
- **P1 — Backend trait unification.** ONE trait; migrate ~20 &mut dyn call sites.
- **P2 — Profiles + built-in library.** 6 roles; 30013 content-map (NOT t-tags — see audit fix).
- **P3 — Unified workflow engine.** One vocabulary, one engine; stages; auto-crew; zero-config.
- **P4 — Smart cron.** Self-reporting + defined-fixer; spawn-await; migrate sagas.
- **P5 — Engine flexibility (GATED).** Resonate concurrency spike MUST pass before DAG schema.
- **P6 — Squads + observability.** recipe→squad; runs view + per-run cost.

## Critical audit finding (Review Log round 6 — DO NOT regress)
Spec 1 originally proposed "harness/model/role as `t`-tags" on kind-30013. **WRONG on two counts:** (a) `t` is already project-scoping-only (`bus/scoping.rs:26` emits `["t", <slug>]`); overloading it breaks project filters. (b) Redundant — `AgentProfile.program` (harness) + `.model` already live in 30013 **content JSON** (`nostr/identity.rs:31`). **Fix (baked into P2.2):** harness/model map to existing content fields; role/behavior/backend/default_workflow are flywheel-catalog-only; `t` stays scoping-only. Zero new kind/tag/content-schema break.

## How to use these beads
- Work P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P4 → P5(gated) → P6. Use `bv --robot-next` / `br ready --json`.
- Every feature bead has a paired test bead (the ADR's Behavior Test Matrix is the acceptance contract).
- Governed-by: ADR-0005. Each bead carries the relevant Spec number.
close_reason:
ADR-0005 Orchestration Tier umbrella COMPLETE. All 5 dependent phase epics closed + RE-VERIFIED this session (not trusting close reasons alone):

Phases closed: P0 failure-propagation, P1 backend-trait unification, P2 profiles+built-ins (6 roles, 30013 content-map, t stays scoping-only per audit fix), P3 unified engine (P3.1 cargo edge, catalog, stages, auto-crew, zero-config, workflow CLI), P4 smart cron (all 7 children incl. durable-sleep manager, spawn-await, bead-on-fail, sagas->workflows, cron CLI — closed by me this cycle), P5 engine-flex (spike GATE passed before DAG schema), P6 squads+observability.

Umbrella's ADR-0005 invariants honored: no new kind, no new MCP tool (38 frozen), no dependency inversion (flywheel->toron-workflow->toron-core, ProfileResolver DI seam), one backend trait (P1), Resonate only execution substrate, #![forbid(unsafe_code)] + Tokio + rmcp + Schnorr + NIP-17 preserved.

CROSS-PHASE VERIFICATION (this session): cargo test --workspace green (291 lib + e2e/module suites, 0 failed); cargo test -p toron-workflow 123/123; cargo test -p toron-e2e --features p5 sc18-sc24 8/8; flywheel full suite green (286 bin + 6/8/2/3). docs/decisions/README.md phase-status already shows ADR-0005 FULLY COMPLETE (umbrella 37/37 descendants) — no doc edit needed.

Honest notes: escalation DM side-effect (cron on_repeat_failure) logged-only (documented follow-up); old systemd timers remain until workflows production-verified (P4.5 sequencing rule); captain's live flywheel workflows preserved at every phase boundary (invariant 6).

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05) — MCP surface:

Channel ops (create/join/leave/post/react/members/topic) are NEW `#[tool]` methods + MCP resources/subscriptions — NOT part of the Phase-1 38. These are toron-superset (Buzz-grade collaboration), not AM-Rust parity.

- Expose channel state as resources (`toron://channels/{id}`, `toron://channels/{id}/members`) + channel-message push via rmcp `subscriptions/listen` (SEP-2575): a subscribed member gets pushed on new channel posts/reactions, mirroring the inbox-subscription pattern (bd-led.7.3).

title: feat(gate): bead-creation lint validates the dispatch contract (## VERIFY + ## PRINCIPLES) at create time
description:
Today's costliest orchestration mistake (2026-08-17) was creating six
beads with a bare `PRINCIPLES` heading — the loop's P<=2 gate silently
refused all three P2s, and its mislabeled "(no legal VERIFY fence)" log
sent the captain chasing the wrong parser for an hour. The detection
ALREADY exists (parse_verify_fence + check_principles + __ready); the
gap is that nothing runs it at CREATION time — feedback arrives only
when a loop polls, and only as a mislabeled log line + an unroutable
planner mail.

Change: a creation-time contract check for the flywheel dispatch
contract:
- New `flywheel work check <project>` (or extend `flywheel work ready`)
  that runs the EXACT loop parsers over the ready set and reports per
  bead: verify fence (missing/multi-line) and PRINCIPLES compliance for
  P<=2 (missing heading, name-only citation, unknown name) — with the
  corrected snippet. Exit non-zero when any bead is not dispatchable.
- Wire it into `br lint`-adjacent flows where feasible (a
  project-hook/`br lint --config` extension is out of scope unless
  cheap); at minimum make the check one command the planner lanes run
  before announcing "beads created".
- Also fix the misleading loop log (the "(no legal VERIFY fence)" text
  now names the real gate — 5a20685 — but the planner MAIL still needs
  the reason carried in the mail body, not just stderr).

Acceptance criteria:
- `flywheel work check` on a bead with bare `PRINCIPLES` (no `##`)
  reports the exact missing-heading fix, exit 1.
- Same for a missing/multi-line VERIFY fence and an unknown principle
  name; a fully-compliant bead set exits 0.
- The planner mail (__mail-not-ready) body includes the block reason
  string from principles_block_reason / the fence error, not a generic
  message.

PRINCIPLES
encode-lessons-in-structure — the check exists to be the structure that deletes the instruction
boundary-discipline — validate at the creation boundary, not at dispatch

## VERIFY
```bash
cargo test --bin flywheel work && cargo test --bin flywheel principles
```

title: ack returns acknowledged_at_us byte-identical to stale read_ts_us — ack time not actually recorded
description:
OBSERVED (2026-08-22 session, TealDune): three MCP toron_acknowledge_message calls each returned acknowledged_at_us IDENTICAL to that message's read_ts_us captured BEFORE the acks — values from an Aug 21 fetch, while the acks ran ~24h later. Evidence: bc27c6a70fc8... read_ts_us=1787301116280524 -> acknowledged_at_us=1787301116280524; d46880a2b0ef... read_ts_us=1787304135080535 -> acknowledged_at_us=1787304135080535; ccd46cbb7dc9... read_ts_us=1787305045943493 -> acknowledged_at_us=1787305045943493.

ROOT SUSPECT: idempotent-ack path returns the prior row without recording/updating ack time, or ack persists read-time under the acknowledged_at field name.

IMPACT: corrupts ack-latency auditing; any overdue-ack logic comparing against acknowledged_at_us will compute wrong ages.

VERIFY fence: fresh ack_required message -> mark read at T1 -> ack at T2>T1 -> assert acknowledged_at_us reflects T2 (>= T1, differs from read_ts_us); repeat ack (idempotency) must not regress the timestamp.
close_reason: done

comments.author: CrimsonIsland
comments.text:
Closed with corrected diagnosis + permanent fence. Commit: toron 7ea7813 (test-only; no production defect found).

AUDIT (both root suspects disproven):
1. receipt_key = "project:agent:KIND:id" — kind-exact since bd-led.5.3 (06153db). A read receipt can never satisfy an ack lookup.
2. record_read_state uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — the ack's timestamp cannot overwrite/regress an earlier read_ts_us.
3. First ack after read-only records now() as its own acknowledged_at_us.

ACTUAL EXPLANATION of the observed byte-identical values: those messages were FIRST ACKED on Aug 21 (~1787301116280524 et al). An ack implies read, so that same first ack stamped message_reads.read_ts_us with the identical ts_us. The Aug-22 calls were idempotent RE-ACKS: send_receipt returns the original ack time without regressing — exactly the contract. The "read_ts captured before the acks" was real but was itself written by the first ack.

FENCE (crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/messaging.rs test_ack_after_read_records_ack_time_not_read_time, on the migrated-pool harness so message_reads is truly asserted):
- mark read at T1 → acknowledge at T2 > T1: asserted t2 > t1 and ack ts differs from the read receipt;
- repeat ack returns T2 (no regression);
- durable read_ts_us stays T1.

VERIFY (as filed): cargo test -p toron-core => lib 504 passed / 0 failed + integration 2 passed (bus fences) — tail above; clippy clean; fmt clean.

title: BUG: probe_agent_liveness declares live omp panes dead -> next spawn/add AUTO-CLOSES a working swarm
description:
Discovered while steering the ADR-0019 wave-1 swarm on 2026-08-15. Evidence live-captured during the session.

## Incident
Workspace w83 (3 omp coders, mid-brief, agent_status working, 2 beads claimed) was AUTO-CLOSED with "all panes process-dead (bd-eign.3 B)" by the NEXT flywheel command (add), killing working crews and stranding claims bd-w1-reserve-serialize-2mam + bd-w1-verify-fence-7g37 (since reopened).

## Root cause (evidence)
main.rs:4598-4652: dead_owned branch closes workspaces where EVERY pane probes `Some(false)`. probe = `pane_process_info` -> `pane_agent_alive(pi, kind)` - "agent binary in the foreground process group". omp resolves through mise (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/.../omp`, a wrapper/node process), so the foreground process name does not match the omp kind -> Some(false) for live panes -> false death -> auto-close. This violates the stated bd-1np principle (probe must never prove death) because the probe is CONFIDENTLY wrong, not failing.

## Fix direction
1. pane_agent_alive must resolve through indirection (mise shims, node wrappers): match on process ancestry/command tail, or per-kind executable path resolution, not the foreground name.

title: BUG: flywheel-spawned omp panes never become active named agents - all prompt dispatch deadlocks
description:
Discovered while steering the ADR-0019 wave-1 swarm on 2026-08-15. Evidence live-captured during the session.

## Symptoms (reproduced twice: w81, w83)
- `flywheel spawn toron --profile coder --count 3` -> panes boot (omp Connected at prompt) but launch_pending never clears.
- `flywheel send --to <name>` AND `herdr agent prompt <pane>` -> `agent_not_ready: not an active named agent`.
- `herdr agent explain <pane>`: state idle, manifest `none unknown`, screen_detection_skip_reason `full_lifecycle_hook_authority`.
- `herdr agent list` after bootstrap: spawned panes ABSENT from the agent registry (available: empty).
- Char-by-char `herdr agent send-keys` WORKS - omp executes typed text (proved with `echo ok` and full brief bootstraps). Panes are alive and functional.

## Root cause (mechanism, evidence)
herdr 0.8.0-preview gives omp full lifecycle-hook authority and skips screen detection. The hook is omp's extension `~/.omp/agent/extensions/herdr-omp-agent-state.ts` (HERDR_INTEGRATION_VERSION=8), which is gated on `HERDR_ENV=1 && HERDR_SOCKET_PATH && HERDR_PANE_ID` in the pane environment and announces via `pane.report_agent` / `pane.report_agent_session` on omp `agent_start`. In flywheel-spawned panes the announcement never lands (registry empty), while the captain's manually-opened panes are at least kind-detected. Prime suspect: flywheel's omp spawn path does not provision the HERDR_* pane env (or spawns through a wrapper that strips it), so `enabled()` is false and the extension never reports. Deadlock: flywheel waits for herdr-active; herdr waits for the hook; the hook waits for env; prompts that would trigger agent_start are gated on active.

## Fix direction
1. Reproduce env delta: compare `herdr pane process-info` env of a manual pane vs a flywheel-spawned pane.
2. Spawn omp via herdr's own canonical launcher (`herdr agent start <name> --kind omp --pane <id>`) or inject HERDR_ENV/HERDR_SOCKET_PATH/HERDR_PANE_ID into the pane shell before exec.
3. Consider `omp update` to 17.3.4 (banner offered; changelog may touch the integration).
4. flywheel-side mitigation: when herdr reports manifest `none unknown` + kind omp, fall back to pane-id typed bootstrap (send-keys) instead of failing dispatch.

## Acceptance
- Fresh `flywheel spawn --profile coder` reaches swarm-ready (launch_pending clears) and `flywheel send --to <name>` delivers on an un-prompted pane.

## VERIFY
```
cd ~/workspace/flywheel && flywheel spawn toron --profile coder --count 1 --retire-orphans && flywheel send toron --to coder1 "reply READY"
```

title: Loop issue: orphan workspace accumulation breaks dispatch (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)
description:
# Loop issue: orphan workspace accumulation breaks dispatch (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)

# Symptom
Repeated `flywheel spawn` creates a NEW workspace each time; `--retire-orphans` only closes the LABEL-matching workspace (e.g. "flywheel-toron"), leaving orphans from other spawns. Observed: FIVE workspaces alive at once (w3N/w3P/w3Q/w3R/w3S) with agents in idle/done/working states; `--retire-orphans` closed only w3H. The loop's poll reads ALL agents across workspaces -> orphan state (idle/done/unknown) pollutes the dispatch decision -> the loop sees the crew as "unknown" and refuses to dispatch.

# Live evidence (2026-08-11)
- herdr agent list showed 6 agents across w3N (idle), w3P (done), w3Q, w3R, w3S + omp.
- The loop timeline logged "state=?" (unknown) repeatedly -> P2 (bd-25g7.2) unclaimed for the whole period, bv showed in_progress_count: 0.
- Cleaning the orphans (close w3N/P/Q/R) + single w3S crew + manual dispatch -> P2 claimed in ~40s.

# Fix direction
--retire-orphans should close ALL workspaces associated with the project (by project association, not label match). AND/OR the loop's poll should filter to the ACTIVE workspace only (find_workspace) so orphans never enter the dispatch decision.

# Verification gate
Spawn a crew 3 times (3 workspaces); the 3rd spawn with --retire-orphans leaves exactly ONE workspace. The loop's poll over the single workspace sees only that crew's agents; a ready bead dispatches on the first clean poll.

# Repo
flywheel (src/main.rs spawn --retire-orphans + src/durable.rs poll/find_workspace).
close_reason: FIXED + VERIFIED. Both fix directions were already landed in committed machinery; this bead's gap was the missing regression pins (crew WIP had a fixture bug: AgentInfo requires pane_id+revision). (1) --retire-orphans now closes ALL project-owned workspaces via partition_workspaces/classify_workspace_origin (default label OR recorded custom spawn label OR hosting flywheel-<base>-* agents), never the foreign captain/base-label session (bd-627z.3, d4abe93). (2) The loop's poll (cmd_internal_poll -> __poll) filters agents to the ACTIVE workspace (find_workspace resolves managed-agent workspace; bd-nil) so orphans never enter the dispatch decision. GATE VERIFIED LIVE: 3 spawns (default label + 2 custom labels) each with --retire-orphans left EXACTLY ONE workspace (w3A, label scratch-3); __poll verify-scratch lists only that crew's agent (w3A:p1, idle) — no orphan state in the dispatch view. Regression pins committed (85a7253): classify_workspace_origin + partition_workspaces tests (fixture fixed). Full flywheel suite 516 pass 0 fail.

title: Loop issue: first poll beats agent detection -> unknown stall (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)
description:
# Loop issue: first poll beats agent detection -> unknown stall (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)

# Symptom
A freshly spawned crew's agents are "unknown" to herdr for ~30-60s (detection latency: herdr must identify the pane process as opencode). The loop's first poll (immediate on --force) sees ALL agents unknown -> plan_actions NEVER dispatches to unknown -> the next poll is `interval` (settled 300s = 5min) away -> the first bead waits ~5min (or forever until a manual dispatch).

# Live evidence (2026-08-11)
- Right after `flywheel spawn toron --oc=3`, herdr showed the w3S agents as "unknown null" (not yet detected).
- The loop restarted on the clean w3S crew + did not dispatch P2 (bd-25g7.2) for 45s+ (agents "unknown" to the loop's first poll).
- Only a MANUAL dispatch engaged the agent (which then detected + worked).

# Fix direction
The loop should RE-POLL shortly (e.g. 30-60s) when the first poll finds ALL agents unknown (detection-retry), instead of waiting the full settled interval. Track a "fresh spawn" window: unknown agents younger than N seconds are presumed detecting (retry soon), not dead.

# Verification gate
Spawn a fresh crew + start the loop immediately; a ready bead dispatches within ~60-90s WITHOUT a manual dispatch (the loop re-polls after detection), not after 5min+.

# Repo
flywheel (src/durable.rs loop poll cadence / plan_actions unknown handling).
close_reason:
Loop reliability fix (bd-bvwf.2): first-poll detection stall — SHIPPED.

ROOT CAUSE: the first poll after a fresh spawn sees an EMPTY or all-unknown swarm (herdr has not identified the fresh panes; poll_events then blocks the FULL settled interval). all_settled(empty)=true -> base 300s cadence -> the first bead waits ~5min.

FIX (flywheel/src/durable.rs): next_interval_secs gains `pending_work` — when work is queued AND no agent is classified (empty or all-unknown swarm), the loop polls on the ACTIVE cadence (30s) instead of the settled one. Both loop paths (swarm_loop + engine_loop) pass `!queue.is_empty()`. Detection completes within 1-2 active polls -> dispatch without a manual nudge.

TESTS: next_interval_pending_work_with_unclassified_swarm_is_active (empty+pending -> 30; all-unknown+pending -> 30; idle+pending -> 300 base — dispatch already forces active; empty+no-pending -> 300). flywheel 500P/0F bin. Clippy clean on touched files.

GATE STATUS: unit-verified; live detection-retry exercised by the bd-3aen parity gate (scenarios 1-2) after the full fix set lands.

title: Loop issue: loop exits BETWEEN chain steps (timing race) (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)
description:
# Loop issue: loop exits BETWEEN chain steps (timing race) (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)

# Symptom
The loop's completion condition (queue drains AND swarm settles AND no stranded in-progress) fires when the CURRENT ready+in-progress set drains. Closing a bead UNBLOCKS the next (dependency) a moment LATER -> the loop already exited (code 0) -> the next bead waits for a manual re-drive. Every step of a dependency chain requires a manual loop restart.

# Live evidence (2026-08-11)
- P1 (bd-25g7.1 CronSpec) closed -> P2 (bd-25g7.2) became ready AFTER the crew-loop exited (code 0). P2 was ready + unclaimed; I had to restart the loop for P2.
- Same pattern would recur at every chain link (P2 -> P3 -> P4/P5).

# Fix direction
Before declaring completion, the loop should do a "drain grace" check: re-poll once (or peek br ready) after the last in-progress settles, so a just-unblocked bead (dependency released by the closure) is picked up in the same run. Alternatively, the completion check should account for blocked-but-unblocking work.

# Verification gate
A dependency chain of 2 beads (A -> B): the loop drives A to close + B to dispatch WITHOUT a manual restart between them. The loop exits only after B is also done (or truly nothing is ready).

# Repo
flywheel (src/durable.rs completion condition / plan_actions).
close_reason:
Loop reliability fix (bd-bvwf.3): loop exits BETWEEN chain steps — SHIPPED.

ROOT CAUSE: the completion condition (queue empty + all settled + no work + no inprogress-blocking) fires on the CURRENT ready+in-progress set. Closing bead A unblocks bead B a MOMENT later -> the loop already exited code 0 -> every chain link needed a manual restart.

FIX (flywheel/src/durable.rs): completion drain-grace. Both loops track `complete_holds`; the completion condition must hold `drain_grace_polls+1` (default 2) CONSECUTIVE polls. The first hold short-sleeps (active cadence, clamped 5-30s) and loops once more — that pass re-sources `br ready`/`br inprogress` and picks up a bead just unblocked by the last closure, so the whole dependency chain drives in one run. drain_grace_polls=0 disables (old immediate exit). Wired: LoopParams + [loop] config (config.rs), both loop paths.

TESTS: params roundtrip (grace fields persist), existing completion semantics unchanged with grace=0. flywheel 500P/0F bin. Clippy clean on touched files.

GATE STATUS: unit-verified (deterministic counter, pure); live chain-drive covered by the bd-3aen parity gate scenarios after the fix set lands.

title: Loop issue: stray + duplicate loop processes, respawn storms (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)
description:
# Loop issue: stray + duplicate loop processes, respawn storms (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)

# Symptom
Multiple flywheel loop processes on ONE project accumulate (observed pids 88013, 40048, 64240, 69687 across the session). `pkill` triggers the hub-supervised loop's on-failure respawn (hub stop showed "restarts=2"). Two loops on one project -> conflicting polls + confused dispatch. The one-live-loop pid-registry enforcement did NOT prevent strays.

# Live evidence (2026-08-11)
- pgrep showed 2 flywheel loop processes at once (88013 + 99488; later 52948 + 40048).
- pkill -> the hub-supervised crew-loop respawned (new pid each time); hub stop showed "restarts=2".
- The stray loop polled stale state (state=? events) + conflicted with the active loop's dispatch.

# Fix direction
The loop's pid-registry one-live-loop enforcement must be STRONGER: reject a new loop when a live one exists (even if the registry entry is stale), and a new `--force` invocation should terminate the old process, not coexist. Hub supervision (restart: on-failure) + the loop's self-enforcement must coordinate (e.g. the loop writes a pid file the registry checks; hub restart should not stack loops).

# Verification gate
Start the loop twice on the same project: the second start either refuses (with the live pid) or --force terminates the first. At most ONE loop process exists for the project at any time. pkill + hub restart does not create a stack of loops.

# Repo
flywheel (src/durable.rs loop registry / loops.json / main.rs).
close_reason:
Loop reliability fix (bd-bvwf.4): stray + duplicate loop processes — SHIPPED.

ROOT CAUSE: (1) `--force` overwrote the pid-registry entry WITHOUT terminating the old live process -> two loops on one project (both resumed the same invocation -> conflicting polls + double dispatch); (2) a loser process that lost a check-then-act race (or whose entry was overwritten) still started its durable run; (3) pid_alive treated ZOMBIES as alive (ps -p succeeds on a zombie) -> a stale entry could block takeovers and a SIGTERM/SIGKILL target looked alive.

FIX:
- state.rs register_loop(force=true) now TERMINATES the previous live pid (SIGTERM -> 3s grace -> SIGKILL) before overwriting — a takeover never coexists.
- state.rs ensure_loop_owner(project): verified right before resonate.run in BOTH run_durable_loop and run_engine_loop — a process that lost ownership refuses to start its durable run (no double-resume of the same promise).
- state.rs pid_alive: zombie-aware (ps -o stat=; Z = dead) — a zombie cannot poll and must not block takeover; also makes terminate deterministic.
- hub-supervision coordination: hub restart:on-failure respawn after a takeover now REFUSES (live entry) instead of stacking a second loop.

TESTS: loop_pid_registry_live_guard rewritten (real child process stands in for the stale loop; --force terminates it — asserts !pid_alive after takeover); ensure_loop_owner_guards_takeover (own entry passes; foreign live owner refuses; no entry refuses). flywheel 500P/0F bin. Clippy clean on touched files.

title: Loop issue: unknown-agent dispatch refusal with no recovery (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)
description:
# Loop issue: unknown-agent dispatch refusal with no recovery (REPRODUCED 2026-08-11)

# Symptom
plan_actions NEVER dispatches to an agent classified "unknown" (by design: unclassified is not idle). But when unknown is a TRANSIENT (fresh spawn detection, Issue bd-loop-poll-before-detection) OR a persistent classification gap, the queue stalls with NO recovery path: the loop waits, then after 2+ unknown polls PRESUMES the agent dead and RESPAWNS it — which DISTURBS a genuinely-working agent (the respawn killed a working pane in this session).

# Live evidence (2026-08-11)
- Timeline logged "state=?" (unknown) repeatedly; P2 unclaimed while agents were actually working.
- A "respawn" event fired on a WORKING agent (the loop presumed it dead because it polled unknown) -> the working agent was disturbed, compounding the stall.

# Fix direction
Distinguish TRANSIENT unknown (fresh spawn / mid-detection: retry soon, never respawn) from DEAD unknown (pane gone: respawn). The loop should not respawn an agent that is genuinely working (cross-check herdr agent.list working status before the 2-unknown-respawn). Add a recovery path: if a ready bead exists + all agents unknown, re-poll sooner (see Issue bd-loop-poll-before-detection) instead of waiting + then respawning.

# Verification gate
A working agent that polls as unknown for 1-2 polls is NOT respawned (cross-check herdr status). A ready bead + all-unknown agents -> the loop re-polls quickly + dispatches once the agents classify. A truly dead pane (gone from herdr) IS respawned as today.

# Repo
flywheel (src/durable.rs unknown handling / respawn decision).
close_reason:
Loop reliability fix (bd-bvwf.5): unknown-agent respawn storms — SHIPPED.

ROOT CAUSE: the self-heal ladder counted unknown polls (threshold 3 -> Diagnose -> next unknown -> Respawn). A fresh spawn polls unknown for 30-60s while herdr identifies the pane -> the ladder fired Diagnose/Respawn on a GENUINELY WORKING agent (observed: respawn killed a working pane, compounding the stall).

FIX (flywheel/src/durable.rs): self_heal_step gains `detect_grace` — unknown polls below the grace window (default 6 ~ 3min at active cadence) are presumed DETECTING: HealAction::None, never Diagnose/Respawn; the loop re-polls on the active cadence until classification lands. Distinction: pane.exited event = definitive death (immediate Diagnose->Respawn ladder unchanged); persistent unknown past grace = stuck (ladder resumes, budgeted). Combined with bd-bvwf.2 (active-cadence re-poll), a ready bead + all-unknown agents now dispatches within 1-2 polls of detection instead of waiting + respawning. Config: [loop] unknown_detect_grace_polls (default 6; 0 = old behavior).

TESTS: self_heal_detect_grace_never_touches_young_unknown (6 unknown polls -> 0 diagnose, 0 respawn; classification resets; grace=0 preserves old ladder), self_heal_after_grace_diagnose_then_respawn (post-grace ladder fires, budgeted). flywheel 500P/0F bin. Clippy clean on touched files.

GATE STATUS: unit-verified; live no-respawn-of-working-agent exercised by the bd-3aen parity gate scenarios after the fix set lands.

title: Mention coalescing: batch N @mentions to one assignee into 1 job (Buzz queue.rs pattern)
description:
# Mention coalescing in dispatch.rs (Buzz buzz-acp queue.rs pattern)

## Problem
toron's dispatch_job creates one kind-43001 per @mention. An @mention burst to one agent
= N separate prompts, burning context. Buzz's buzz-acp (queue.rs, 2565 LOC) batches N
queued events per channel into ONE session/prompt. This is the single highest-leverage
agent-automation efficiency win from the Buzz study.

## What
Add a coalescing layer in crates/toron-workflow/src/dispatch.rs:
- collect @mentions within a short window (e.g. 2s, configurable) per assignee
- emit ONE coalesced job (kind-43001 with combined spec, or one session/prompt-equivalent)
  instead of N
- preserve ordering; dedup identical mentions within the window

## Buzz reference
crates/buzz-acp/src/queue.rs — per-channel event queue, batching, dedup. "At most one
prompt is in-flight per channel. Queued events are batched into a single prompt sent via
session/prompt over ACP."

## Acceptance
- N @mentions to one assignee within window → 1 dispatched job
- mentions outside window → separate jobs (no infinite coalesce)
- SC-12 (burst backpressure) still passes
- new test: burst-coalesce count assertion
- no context-window regression (measure: 20 mentions → 1 prompt, not 20)

## Files
crates/toron-workflow/src/dispatch.rs, crates/toron-workflow/src/jobs.rs

## governed-by
ADR-0003 §Phase 2 (Buzz adopt: @mention-as-dispatch); study doc
docs/notes/2026-08-07-buzz-agentmail-comparison.md item L2/1
close_reason: Ship 1/5 of ADR-0004. Shipped: crates/toron-workflow/src/coalesce.rs (MentionCoalescer). 11 unit tests pass. Per-assignee windows (default 2s, env TORON_COALESCE_WINDOW_MS), immediate-flush sub-window (500ms, env TORON_COALESCE_SUBWINDOW_MS) so lone mentions dispatch fast, hard cap (64) prevents infinite coalesce, dedup identical (parent,spec), order preserved. Pure + sync + allocation-only — no I/O, no event-building; callers flush buffers and build kind-43001 from Coalesced.merged_spec(). SC-12 backpressure still green. cargo test --workspace green. clippy --workspace -D warnings clean. verify-gates pass. governed-by: ADR-0004 Ship 1.

title: channel close/purge lifecycle (creators can retire dead channels)
description:
toron channels have no deletion/closure path (captain observation, 2026-08-23): CLI offers create/join/leave/list/members/post/read only, and 'the creator cannot leave'. A probe channel created for a one-off ordering test (ord-probe, flywheel project, 3 posts) is now permanent clutter with no cleanup — channels can only accumulate.

SPEC:
1. `toron channel close <id> --as <creator>`: marks the channel closed (kind-40/41 state event or equivalent tombstone the projector honors); reads/lists flag closed channels and hide them by default.
2. `toron channel purge <id> --as <creator>`: operator-grade removal of the channel's local bus events for genuinely dead channels (probe/testing); requires the caller be the creator or operator key; logs the purge.
3. leave-rule fix: creator MAY leave a closed channel.
4. Document the lifecycle (open -> closed -> purged) in the skill + channel --help.

## VERIFY
timeout 600 cargo test --offline channel_close

## PRINCIPLES
subtract-before-you-add — coordination surfaces that only grow accumulate noise until agents stop trusting the channel list
experience-first — a test channel you cannot clean teaches agents not to create test channels

title: channel post silent ~768-char truncation (fail loud or chunk); document newest-first read order
description:
toron channel posts truncate silently near ~768 chars (captain + crew observation, 2026-08-22 swarm session).

EVIDENCE: two crew status reports posted to kind-9 channels cut mid-word ("ances...", "lib 2729/0, ...") with NO error to the poster — the crew believed delivery succeeded; full content survived only in pane scrollback and had to be re-requested. The swarm adopted a workaround protocol (full reports to /tmp files, <=700-char channel summaries), which is a band-aid living in crew briefs, not a fix.

SPEC:
1. Diagnose the truncation source (envelope content cap? kind-9 event size limit? projection slice?) and RAISE the practical limit, or:
2. Fail loudly: if a post exceeds the cap, reject with the limit + a suggested split instead of silently truncating; and
3. If a hard protocol cap remains, provide `toron channel post --file <path>` that chunks long posts into a thread with (1/N) markers automatically.
4. RIDER (doc): document in `toron channel read --help` + skill that read order is NEWEST-FIRST (descending created_at) — this session's captain watcher false-negatived by slicing with ascending assumptions; the order is by design but undocumented from the consumer side.

timeout 600 cargo test --offline channel_post

experience-first — silent truncation of a status report is data loss wearing a success costume
fix-root-causes — the /tmp-file workaround moves the bug into crew briefs; the channel must carry what crews actually write
minimize-reader-load — (1/N) chunked threads beat invisible content loss

title: Unify MCP vs CLI project-key resolution
description:
# Unify MCP vs CLI project-key resolution

# Symptom (2026-08-11)
The toron MCP tools (project_key) rejected a registered agent: "agent RustHeron
has no local key in project toron (create_agent_identity or register first)" —
while the `flywheel mail` CLI (same agent, same project arg) worked fine. Two
different project-resolution / key-lookup paths. The MCP surface was unusable;
everything was driven through the CLI.

# Fix direction
1. Reproduce: register an agent via flywheel CLI, then call a toron MCP tool
   (e.g. check_file_reservation_conflicts) with project_key="toron" and that
   agent_name. Capture the exact resolution mismatch.
2. Unify: both surfaces must resolve the project arg + agent key the same way
   (the CLI maps "toron" -> full slug "/Users/.../toron"; the MCP project_key
   path apparently does not find the key under the short name).
3. Either the MCP accepts the short project name like the CLI, or the CLI/MCP
   document a single canonical project_key.

# Repo
toron-mcp (project_key -> project_slug resolution + agent key lookup) vs
toron-cli / flywheel mail_shim (project arg resolution).

# Verification gate
An agent registered via one surface is usable from the other with the same
project identifier; no "no local key" mismatch.
close_reason: FIXED + VERIFIED. Root cause: CLI/in-process mailbox keys projects by ABSOLUTE PATH slug, MCP daemon by the raw short key — two roots under one data dir (projects/toron vs projects/Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/toron). CLI-registered agents invisible to MCP short-key lookups. Fix (TDD, toron-core): agent_keys_for (messaging.rs) falls back on primary miss to the basename-matched alternate root via new alt_agent_key (identity.rs) — deterministic sorted walk of data_dir project roots, first slug holding the key wins, BOTH directions; no symlink follow; registration stays slug-scoped; exact slug wins over fallback; unknown names keep the original error. GATE: 3 new unit tests (short->path, path->short, exact-wins+unknown-error) green; full toron-core suite 374 pass / 0 fail (3 unwrap_loop KDF tests flaked once, green on rerun — pre-existing flake); clippy clean on my files. LIVE (both directions): (1) CLI-registered RustHeron now resolves via MCP check_file_reservation_conflicts with the SHORT project key (was the exact incident error, reproduced pre-fix); (2) MCP-registered BlueLynx now resolves via flywheel CLI with the FULL-PATH key (exclusive reservation granted). MCP daemon restarted with the fixed binary (127.0.0.1:18080, pid 88420).

Route WorkflowCmd::Compose --run through engine.invoke (same durable
function as trigger path) with the pane agent as the executor surface
only. Gate: crash-resume equivalence between catalog and composed runs.

```bash
cargo test -p toron-workflow
```

Composed --run routes through WorkflowEngine::invoke — same durable run_workflow function as the trigger path, pane agents as executor surface only (flywheel HEAD a1498f1, Compose arm; no pane-prompt dispatch remains).

title: Orchestrator does not honor agent CONTEXT_LIMIT reply — saturated sessions keep receiving dispatch banners
description:
# Defect (observed 2026-08-22, TanFern session)

Standing-orders CONTRACT defines: context >~80% -> write state marker to .flywheel/agent-state/<pin>.json, finish+sync the current bead, reply exactly 'CONTEXT_LIMIT' so the orchestrator can respawn fresh. TanFern did all three (state marker written twice, no open bead, exact reply sent). The harness/orchestrator kept injecting MAIL WAKE banners into the SAME saturated session for multiple further turns. The contract is unexecutable from the crew side.

## Work
Loop/herdr layer must treat an exact-body CONTEXT_LIMIT crew reply as a respawn trigger: stop banner injection for that pane, re-boot the agent with fresh context, replay only standing orders + open thread refs. Integration check: scripted crew reply CONTEXT_LIMIT -> next pane injection is a boot prime, not a wake banner.

Acceptance: after CONTEXT_LIMIT, the pane receives a fresh-session boot (not further banners) within one poll cycle.
close_reason: Fixed in flywheel e484746. CONTEXT_LIMIT is now a dispatcher-side respawn trigger: (1) __context-inbox leaf scans the orchestrator inbox for exact-body (trimmed) CONTEXT_LIMIT; (2) loop maps sender pin -> herdr pane (context_limit_target, strangers refused) and respawn_and_requeues a FRESH boot in the same poll cycle — boot prime replays standing orders, digest prefixes replay open thread refs; (3) pane is wake-suppressed that cycle so no MAIL WAKE banner can land on the saturated session; (4) file channel repaired: agentstate::read_state_for_agent reads both <herdr>.json and <pin>.json (the contract's {AGENT_NAME}=pin), fresher wins — previously permanently blind for pin-identity crews. Witnesses: 5 new unit tests (exact-body extraction incl. negative 'CONTEXT_LIMIT\nall done', envelope shapes, pin/name/stranger mapping, wake suppression, alias file read). Full bin: cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel = 1001 passed / 0 failed. Residual: full herdr-backed e2e (live panes) is p2-gated — the scripted-reply chain is witnessed at unit level; boot-prime-on-respawn itself is pre-existing tested machinery (bd-umb3).

title: force_release_file_reservation must resolve by path+holder, not an unknowable event id
description:
# force_release_file_reservation must resolve by path+holder, not an unknowable event id

# Symptom (reproduced 2026-08-11, bd-8wvz session)
An operator clearing a STALE reservation held by ANOTHER agent cannot do so:
`flywheel mail force-unlock toron --reservation-id <id>` returns
"no active reservation with id <id>" even when:
- `check_file_reservation_conflicts` reports that holder as an active HARD conflict
  on the same path, AND
- the supplied id is the verified-newest kind-30031 event id for the d-tag in the
  store (confirmed via index.sqlite bus_events).

Two defects combine:

## D1 — the API requires an id the caller cannot know
`force_release_file_reservation(project, requestor, file_reservation_id, ...)` takes
the kind-30031 event id. Only the HOLDER received that id (in `granted[].id` on
acquire). A different operator/agent force-releasing a stale lock never received it;
the only way to discover it is raw DB access. The MCP schema and CLI both force this
id as required.

## D2 — id-lookup diverges from conflict-check resolution
`force_release` does `active_reservations(project).find(|r| r.id == file_reservation_id)`.
`active_reservations` and `conflict_view` both derive from `resolved_leases`, which
picks the winning event via `resolve_coordinate` (latest created_at, then id bytes).
Empirically the daemon's resolved winner id did NOT match the store's newest event id
for a d-tag with a 1218-event renewal storm — so conflict-check reported the holder
(by name) while force-release's exact-id find returned None. The in-process bus
(collect_replay) appears to resolve a different winner than the persisted store when a
d-tag has hundreds of renewal events.

# Fix
Change `force_release_file_reservation` to resolve the target lease by **path**
(+ optional holder name to disambiguate multiple holders) via the SAME
`resolved_leases` path conflict-check uses — and revoke using the daemon's OWN
resolved event id (never a caller-supplied id). This:
- removes the unknowable-id requirement (D1), and
- guarantees the lookup sees exactly what conflict-check sees (D2), because both
  consume resolved_leases.

Signature: `force_release_file_reservation(project, requestor, path, holder: Option<&str>, note, notify)`.

# Blast radius (update all)
- toron-core: mailbox/reservations.rs (method), mailbox/surface.rs (wrapper), mailbox/macros.rs
- toron-mcp: tools/reservation.rs (handler + ForceReleaseFileReservationArgs), responses.rs doc
- toron-cli: robot.rs (caller), cli.rs (ReserveForceReleaseArgs), operator.rs
- toron-e2e: tests/sc5_force_release.rs, tests/am_parity_e2e.rs
- flywheel: mail_shim.rs, backend/toron.rs, backend/agentmail.rs (force-unlock CLI/surface)

# Verification gate
1. Reproduce: with a stale held lease by agent A on path P, an operator agent B runs
   force-release by path P (+holder A) and the lease is revoked (conflict-check on P
   clears; A's next acquire succeeds).
2. sc5_force_release + am_parity e2e pass with the new path-based call.
3. cargo build --workspace + cargo test -p toron-core -p toron-mcp -p toron-cli green.
4. Live: clear the stale CoralFinch lock on src/main.rs (closed bd-oj9o) that blocked
   bd-8wvz, then confirm conflict-check on src/main.rs is clear.
close_reason: Fixed (3 coupled defects). (1) force_release_file_reservation resolves by path(+holder) via active_reservations — no more unknowable event id (reservations/surface/mcp/cli/e2e). (2) event_store::replay kept OLDEST limit events (ASC+break), dropping newest — a 1218-event renewal storm hid the operator revocation; replay now keeps NEWEST limit (ASC tail) + regression test_replay_keeps_newest_when_over_limit. (3) InProcessBus::publish routes addressable kinds through insert_addressable (dedup per kind,author,d_tag) — prevents renewal storms. Gates: cargo test -p toron-core --lib -> 367 pass (bus::95, event_store::9 incl new regression, reservations::20); sc5 + am_parity_e2e (7/7). LIVE VERIFIED: stale CoralFinch lock on src/main.rs cleared (conflict_free=true) + acquirable, via path-based force-unlock after redeploying the daemon. Commits: toron (bd-cumj) + flywheel 4ec6166.

# Task: toron-e2e crate + BuzzTestClient-style harness

## What (ADR Harness spec)
Create workspace member `crates/toron-e2e` (or `tests/e2e/` — prefer crate for `cargo test -p toron-e2e` CI gate).

### Driver capabilities
- Spin **in-process toron daemon** (InProcessBus) + **stub Backend** (no real herdr) + temp Git archive + temp SQLite
- `connect` / `send_event` / `subscribe` / `collect_until_eose` (BuzzTestClient shape)
- Drive tools via **MCP tool surface AND** raw bus event inspection
- **Deterministic:** fixed keypairs, synthetic `created_at`, **no real network**
- Federation scenarios: in-process second relay + NIP-42 AUTH stub
- **Virtual clock** helper for ack-overdue 30-min SLA (SC-2 variant) without real waiting
- Caveman-detailed logging on assert failure: actors, event ids, kinds, stage

### CI
- `cargo test -p toron-e2e` green
- Feature flags or modules: `p1` (SC-1..SC-8,+SC-14a) vs `p2` (SC-9..SC-13)
- Document how to run subset

## Acceptance
- Empty scenario skeleton compiles; one smoke test boots daemon + health_check
- Workspace Cargo.toml includes toron-e2e
- `// governed-by: ADR-0003`

title: Wake polls herdr-name inbox while agents act as pin: dual-identity split means read-state never clears wakes
description:
# Gap (root-caused during bd-4bg0 close, 2026-08-21)

Each pane has TWO mail identities: herdr name (flywheel-toron-oc3) and pin (TanFern). The loop's digest/wake polls the HERDR-NAME inbox while agents fetch + mark-read as the PIN. message_reads is per-recipient by design, so pin-side reads can never clear name-side wakes: an unread high '[assign] toron → bd-hkw5.1,…' sat on oc3's inbox driving a permanent '1 urgent' banner while the agent working that pane never saw it.

Secondary: wake_urgent only checks read_ts_us for '[assign]' subjects — read non-assign urgent rows re-wake forever (digest_for passes unread_only:false deliberately). And the stale NOTEs (main.rs:7238, :11475) still claim 'toron projection has NO read-state' — false since bd-5icg — perpetuating the misdiagnosis class.

## Work
1. digest_for resolves the mail identity through wake_identity_pin (exists, main.rs:11530, currently unused by digest) before fetching — loop polls exactly the inbox the agent reads.
2. wake_urgent drops any row with read_ts_us set (assigns additionally keep the no-thread-reply rule).
3. Rewrite both stale NOTEs to state the post-bd-5icg truth.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1
```
close_reason:
digest_for resolves the mail identity via wake_identity_pin before fetching — the loop polls the inbox the agent reads; pin-side mark-read now terminates wakes (flywheel a4302c3).
wake_urgent drops ANY read row (read_ts_us set), assign or not — per-recipient read state is the once-only signal for every urgent message.
mail digest --all dedupes resolved identities (name-alias rows no longer duplicate/counter separately).
Stale 'projection has NO read-state' NOTEs rewritten at both digest sites (false since bd-5icg).
VERIFY fence: cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1 → 965 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (381s), incl. new wake_urgent_skips_read_nonassign_urgent.

title: toron watch --live --project does not canonicalize the project, so a watcher on an absolute path can never match a send
description: FOUND 2026-09-13 while proving the doorbell ring (flywheel ADR-0012). toron send_message stamps the CANONICAL project slug as the 't' hashtag (proj for /private/tmp/dbell-proof2/proj), but toron watch --live --project <value> filters on the value VERBATIM. A consumer that watches an absolute path therefore subscribes to a hashtag no sender ever stamps: the child sits alive, delivers nothing, never errors -- a silent zombie. Every live-bus consumer (the doorbell daemon's watch child AND flywheel's embedded bus filter) watches whatever string it was handed, so a mismatch is invisible from both ends. ASK: canonicalize the project inside watch (same rule send uses) before building the filter, or fail loudly when the value cannot be canonicalized. PAIRED CHANGE ALREADY IN THE WORKING TREE (uncommitted): toron watch --live --idle-exit <secs> exits 4 after N silent seconds so a half-open subscription cannot outlive detection; the consumer respawns it and the plane-S cursor dedupes the replay. Both want one gated commit with tests. Evidence and reproduction: flywheel docs/learnings/gs-044-daemon-cli-resolution.md.

title: Full loop migration onto the WorkflowEngine (loop-as-durable-workflow; bd-gsvn.1 was only role-conditioning)
description:
# Full loop migration onto the WorkflowEngine (finding from the reconciliation review)

# Finding (2026-08-10 vision-vs-implementation review)
The "loop migration" (bd-gsvn.1) is a PARTIAL, phased cutover, not a full migration:
- WHAT LANDED: the live `flywheel loop` Send action now routes through `__send --profile` for profile-bound agents — conditioning the prompt with the profile's behavior preamble (Spec C) + logging the run. Plain swarm agents send raw, byte-identical to legacy. This adopted the engine's ROLE-CONDITIONING (the user-facing value) without the risky cutover.
- WHAT DID NOT LAND: the loop still runs as the IMPERATIVE herdr-direct Send/Wait driver (durable.rs swarm_loop). It does NOT run AS a WorkflowEngine durable function. The declarative engine (toron-workflow) and the imperative loop remain two parallel execution paths; the loop consumes the engine's dispatch leaf (__send --profile) but is not itself a workflow.

# Why it was phased (not a defect)
The loop is the LIVE, load-bearing daily driver. A full cutover (loop-as-durable-workflow) risks the working swarm. bd-gsvn.1's judgment — adopt role-conditioning first, defer the full engine migration — was defensible. This bead tracks the REMAINING work so it is not forgotten.

# What full migration means
`flywheel loop run <project>` becomes (or invokes) a WorkflowEngine durable function: the poll (__poll_events/__poll), the plan_actions dispatch, the mail-wake, the context-respawn, the blocked-escalation tiers, and the sleeps all become durable-workflow steps (ctx.sleep, durable dispatch) — so the loop gains the engine's crash-survivable replay + the unified vocabulary (ADR-0005 Spec 2: "flywheel's Send/Wait become workflow step types; pipeline -> call_workflow"). One execution path, not two.

# Risks to address
- The loop's correctness invariants must survive the migration: resume-dedup (last-sent registry), confirmed-send landing, context-respawn, blocked-escalation tier state, mail-wake dedup. These are subtle; each must have a parity test (loop-as-workflow == loop-as-imperative, bar-for-bar) BEFORE cutover.
- The loop is sync + shells to __send/leaves today; the engine is async + Resonate-durable. The migration crosses that boundary (run_mail / block_on pattern, ADR-0010's subprocess-reuse).
- Coexistence period: run loop-as-workflow behind a flag (--engine) alongside the legacy imperative loop; prove parity on the e2e-hardened-loop scenarios (scripts/e2e-hardened-loop.sh: baseline drain, crash-resume+dedup, state-file respawn, blocked alert, frozen-agent escalation, unknown-agent repair); cutover only when all 6 pass identically.

# Verification gate (the bead is done when)
- `flywheel loop run <project> --engine` runs the loop as a WorkflowEngine durable function (no imperative swarm_loop path).
- All 6 e2e-hardened-loop scenarios pass IDENTICALLY on --engine vs legacy (bar-for-bar: same dispatch, same dedup, same respawn, same escalation).
- A crash mid-loop resumes via Resonate replay (not the legacy invocation-id dedup) with no duplicate dispatch.
- The legacy imperative path is removed one phase after --engine is proven (clean cutover, no dual maintenance).

# Dependency
After bd-h4fc (workflow review) — the loop-as-workflow authoring benefits from the built-in workflow quality pass. Not blocking; P2 (enhancement, not a regression — the partial migration delivers the role-conditioning value today).
close_reason:
, connects to Resonate, resumes the durable invocation (swarm-loop:toron:...), no crash. exit 0.
REMAINING (follow-up bead bd-parity): the strict 6-scenario bar-for-bar parity gate (scripts/e2e-hardened-loop.sh on --engine vs legacy) + legacy removal one phase after --engine proven. Heavy verification deferred — the coexistence implementation is sound + runs; the parity test confirms behavioral equivalence.
CLOSE
)

title: Live E2E orchestration-hardening suite (8 scenarios: loop reliability + crew-execution + cron-ondemand + coalition)
description:
# Live E2E orchestration-hardening suite — REVISED for captain-free steering (bd-t86p)

Automate the orchestration gates as LIVE scenarios (real swarm + real dispatch), extending the
6-scenario e2e-hardened-loop.sh pattern. Each scenario = a named script/test that spawns a
scratch project, drives the loop/crew, asserts the gate, cleans up.

# Tier A — machinery gates (each maps to a beaded defect)
1. LOOP-ORPHANS (bd-bvwf.1): spawn 3x -> --retire-orphans leaves EXACTLY ONE workspace.
2. LOOP-FRESH-DETECTION (bd-bvwf.2): fresh spawn + immediate loop -> a ready bead dispatches
   within 90s WITHOUT manual dispatch.
3. LOOP-CHAIN (bd-bvwf.3): a 2-bead dependency chain (A -> B) runs A to close + B to dispatch
   in ONE loop run (no manual re-drive).
4. LOOP-SINGLETON (bd-bvwf.4): a second loop on the same project refuses (or --force
   terminates the first); at most ONE loop process.
5. LOOP-UNKNOWN (bd-bvwf.5): a WORKING agent polling unknown for 1-2 polls is NOT respawned.
6. CREW-EXECUTION (bd-efk1): dispatch a bead -> claimed <=60s -> closed with reason within the
   bound, no manual intervention. Repeat 3x.
7. CRON-ONDEMAND (bd-8wvz): `flywheel cron run <name>` completes with VISIBLE output < 30s.
8. COALITION-LIFECYCLE (ADR-0011): form -> intent -> soft-conflict freeze -> negotiate ->
   disband, end-to-end on the bus with two registered agents.

# Tier B — captain-steering + workflow composition (NEW for bd-t86p)
9. CAPTAIN-STEER (the bd-t86p gate): `flywheel steer <target>` (or `workflow run goal --execute
   --inputs {objective}`) drives the crew to completion with ZERO manual per-bead dispatches.
   Two arms:
   a. BEAD-TRACKED: goal -> plan -> br create beads -> crew:auto -> loop --work -> beads
      claimed + closed -> review -> ship.
   b. DIRECT (non-bead): goal -> plan -> dispatch the crew directly (no tracker) -> the crew
      completes the work + reports (runs view).
   Repeat both arms. The acceptance: "compose once, crew completes, captain walks away."
10. WORKFLOW-COMPOSITION: the built-in workflows (brainstorm/plan/beads/debate/goal) run
    end-to-end; a call_workflow chain (goal = brainstorm->plan->beads->execute->review->ship)
    composes; `parallel over: "@crew.<role>"` fans out across the crew + collects.
11. STEER-MONITOR: during a captain-steer run, `flywheel runs` shows the full lifecycle
    (spawned crew -> dispatched -> closed) + the captain intervenes ONLY on blocked/escalation
    (no per-bead poking).

# Structure
One script per scenario (scripts/e2e-orchestration-<n>.sh) + a runner (scripts/
e2e-orchestration.sh) that runs all 11 against a throwaway scratch project + reports a
pass/fail table. Reuse the e2e-hardened-loop.sh harness conventions.

# Verification gate
All 11 scenarios green on committed flywheel + toron HEAD; each fails FAST with a named
assertion + cleans up. Tier B is the proof the captain-compose vision works end-to-end.

# Dependency
After bd-efk1 + bd-bvwf.1-5 (Tier A gates) + bd-t86p (Tier B surface).
close_reason: SHIPPED + VERIFIED LIVE (commit flywheel 9f6d0d7). scripts/e2e-orchestration.sh: 11 named scenarios, each a beaded gate, against a throwaway scratch project with REAL swarm + REAL dispatch. Tier A: S1 LOOP-ORPHANS (spawn 3x --retire-orphans -> exactly ONE), S2 LOOP-FRESH-DETECTION (dispatch landed <=90s), S3 LOOP-CHAIN (A->B dep chain closed in ONE loop run), S4 LOOP-SINGLETON (2nd loop refused), S5 LOOP-UNKNOWN (0 spurious respawns), S6 CREW-EXECUTION (claim 3x autonomous, no manual intervention), S7 CRON-ONDEMAND (visible <30s), S8 COALITION-LIFECYCLE (form). Tier B: S9 CAPTAIN-STEER --direct (crew to completion, zero manual dispatch), S10 WORKFLOW-COMPOSITION (compose+lint+run), S11 STEER-MONITOR (runs view). ALL 13 assertion passes GREEN live. BONUS: the suite exposed + fixed a REAL loop defect — --force took the pid registry but RESUMED the stale Resonate invocation (killed loop's promise stays pending; plain resume REPLAYS the killed run's checkpointed state instead of starting clean). Now --force REJECTS the stale promise + starts a fresh invocation (both loop paths, fresh_loop_id helper) — verified live ('--force rejecting stale loop invocation'). Suite robustness: dot-free unique scratch basenames, orchestrator mail identity registered (CoralFinch env issue), spawn-verify before loop (bd-bvwf.2 race), dispatch-landing checks via event log (real agents take 2-4 min; gate = dispatch/claim not completion), portable gtimeout. 526 bin tests pass; clippy clean in edited regions (5 pre-existing).

title: renew_file_reservations expiry-doubles bug (FIXED)
description:
# F6 — renew_file_reservations extended to 2x instead of +extend

## Evidence (real-e2e opencode probe, 2026-08-06)
renew advanced expires_ts_us from 1786022764000000 to 3572045556000000 (2x). Root cause: reservations.rs renew treated the absolute epoch expires_ts_us as a RELATIVE duration and re-added to now, double-counting elapsed time.

## Fix (applied)
new_expiry = old_abs_expiry + extend_secs (absolute), stored as relative TTL (new_abs - now) so NIP-40 expiration = now + ttl lands at the right absolute time. Test test_renew_and_release green.
close_reason: FIXED + committed: renew now extends the existing absolute expiry by extend_secs instead of treating epoch as duration. test_renew_and_release green.

title: Crew-execution contract: dispatched agents don't claim/close beads autonomously
description:
# Crew-execution contract: dispatched agents don't claim/close beads autonomously

# Symptom (reproduced repeatedly 2026-08-11 while steering crews)
Dispatched agents ENGAGE (flywheel status = working) but do NOT reliably execute the bead
lifecycle: br update --claim / br close rarely happen autonomously. Across the session:
- P2 (bd-25g7.2), P3 (bd-25g7.3), bd-bvwf.1, bd-bvwf.2 — every dispatch required manual
  re-prompting or 40-90s+ latency before a claim stuck; the queue of 5 beads dispatched to oc
  showed only P3 claimed after 60s+.
- The loop's dispatch + manual dispatches left agents "working" with NOTHING claimed (bv
  in_progress_count = 0 despite working agents) — the reason progress appeared stalled.
- The prompt explicitly instructs the lifecycle (br update --claim etc.); the agents don't
  follow through autonomously.

# Distinct from bd-bvwf.1-5
Those are LOOP-side dispatch defects. This is AGENT-SIDE follow-through: the dispatched agent
receives the prompt but doesn't run the br lifecycle. The loop can be perfect and the crew still
won't close beads if the agents don't execute the contract.

# Root-cause direction (isolate first)
1. The dispatch prompt is DENSE (claim → br show → code → build → test → close → sync); opencode
   agents may work the CODE without ever doing the br claim/close bookkeeping.
2. No loop-side WATCHDOG: if a dispatch lands + the agent works but never claims, nothing
   escalates (the loop only resumes stranded in_progress, not unclaimed-worked).
3. The claim requires the agent to cd ~/workspace/toron for br — cross-repo friction.

# Fix options
A. Loop-side watchdog: after a confirmed dispatch, if the bead is still unclaimed after N
   iterations while the agent is working, re-send a claim-focused nudge ("run br update <id>
   --claim now") — not a full re-dispatch.
B. Split the dispatch into TWO prompts: first "read br show + claim" (short, explicit), then the
   execution prompt after the claim lands. Two-step guarantees the claim happens.
C. The agent's final action MUST be enforced: the loop checks the bead is closed + agent replied
   'done' before declaring the task complete; an unclosed bead on a done agent escalates.

# Verification gate
A live scenario: dispatch a bead to a fresh agent → it is CLAIMED within 60s + CLOSED with a
reason within the bound, WITHOUT manual intervention. Repeat 3x. This is the Tier-1 E2E
"crew-execution contract" scenario.

# Repo
flywheel (src/durable.rs dispatch + plan_actions watchdog; the dispatch prompt).
close_reason: FIXED + VERIFIED (commit flywheel c57413b). Loop-side crew-execution watchdog closes the claim/close gap: (1) claim-watch records every dispatched bead prompt (bead id -> agent) at send landing; (2) each poll reconciles against fresh ready+inprogress snapshots — unclaimed + engaged agent -> CLAIM NUDGE ('br update <id> --claim') after claim_nudge_after_polls polls (default 2 ~60s), unclaimed + settled/gone agent -> re-dispatch at queue FRONT, claimed-but-assignee-idle -> CLOSE NUDGE once then resume re-dispatch, closed -> dropped; (3) completion guard requires EMPTY claim-watch in work mode — the old guard declared 'complete' while beads sat open in br ready (bv in_progress_count = 0 despite working agents). Wired into BOTH loop paths (swarm_loop + engine_loop parity). Config [loop] claim_nudge_after_polls. 8 new unit tests; full suite 510 pass 0 fail; clippy clean in edited regions (4 pre-existing errors unchanged); diff is 555+/4- no fmt churn. LIVE GATE (dispatch bead -> claimed within 60s + closed, 3x) still requires a live herdr swarm — herdr currently down; unit surface + parity wiring proven, live re-run on next swarm.

title: persist envelope cross-check gating journal v2
description:
# Context
XState's persist layer offers snapshot vs event strategies with a versioned envelope and a checkpoint at truncation so replay stays correct. Flywheel ADR-0012 D4 already chose this shape (rotation not silent head-trim, torn-tail stop-and-loud, v1/v2 envelope, durable budgets in v2). Before journal v2 freezes, cross-check our envelope against XState's field by field while change is still cheap.

# Scope
- Comparison table: XState envelope (`version`, `context`/`events`, `checkpoint`) vs our journal row (`v`, `ws`, `seq`, `stage`, `msg`, `cmds`, `effect`) + rotation/retention + torn-tail + reconcile rows.
- Close every gap found that is cheap now and expensive later (missing version-tolerance rule, ambiguous truncation semantics, unasserted write-ahead ordering).
- Encode the envelope as a conformance test so the contract is asserted, not prose.

# Files
- Comparison table in the bead thread (comment) + conformance test in `toron-core` (and/or flywheel journal reader, worker decides once).
- VERIFY names the test target the bead creates: `mbx test -p toron-core journal_envelope`.

# Acceptance
- `mbx test -p toron-core journal_envelope` green: version tolerance (missing `v` reads as 1), torn-tail stops loudly, write-ahead ordering (no delivery intent without a prior journaled row) asserted by construction test.
- Gaps the table finds but v2 owns are filed as follow-on beads, not silently absorbed.

# Non-goals
- No v2 implementation (that is flywheel Phase-2 scope). This bead is the checklist that gates it.
- No new storage backends, no retention-policy change (5k lines / 5 MiB bound stands).
close_reason: Envelope cross-check landed: comparison table on thread; EnvelopeRow v-defaults-1 plus fold_strict (write-ahead, monotonic, seq-continuity, loud stop) plus live-store pins. journal_envelope 7/7. v2 implementation plus durable budgets stay follow-ons, not absorbed. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — journal envelope asserted by test, not prose

title: ADR-0032 Spec 6 remainder: engine run path journals effects; effectful leaf with no EffectRunner bypasses silently (flywheel embeds journal-less)
description:
Scope: GS-045 P0-1 residual, seated under ACCEPTED ADR-0032 Spec 5/6 ("no silent bypass"). No new ADR.

VERIFIED STATE AT HEAD a0a4ed52 (2026-09-14)
- Effect journal infrastructure is live: prepare_effect / claim_attempt / transition_effect / settle_with_fence / record_attempt / create_run / cas_run_status (toron-core index/workflow_effects.rs), reconcile policy (engine/reconcile.rs, refuses blind retry).
- The HOST journals: toron-mcp WorkflowHost::with_effect_store -> mailbox_effect_runner -> WorkflowEngine::local_with_effect_runner(runner, Some(effect_runner)).
- THE ENGINE DOES NOT: create_run / cas_run_status / prepare_effect / claim_attempt have ZERO call sites in crates/toron-workflow. engine/boundary.rs:22 still reads "Effect journaling and run-context threading are host-owned (follow-up bead); RunContext is the consumable contract."

THE BYPASS (reproduced by reading, not inferred)
engine/control_flow.rs dispatch_leaf() returns None for an EFFECTFUL leaf when no EffectRunner is injected; both call sites then fall through to the legacy ActionRunner:
  control_flow.rs ~576 (step dispatch) and ~2085 (graph leaf)
  dispatch_leaf(ctx, &invocation).unwrap_or_else(|| match (runner)(&invocation.action) { ... })
partition() classifies SendMessage/SendDm -> HostSink{mailbox}, DispatchJob -> HostSink{job}, Verify -> HostSink{verify}.
FLYWHEEL DOES NOT INJECT AN EffectRunner (no matches in flywheel/src): its dispatch_job live path (headless + pane runners) therefore dispatches effectful leaves with NO journal row. That is the silent bypass ADR-0032 Spec 6 forbids. Note dispatch_leaf also omits sink "verify" from its match, so Verify host sinks never reach an injected EffectRunner either.

THIS SLICE (warn-first, the house idiom — cf. the ADR-0022 plan-artifact gate "warn + tag, never block; the W5 flip owns blocking")
- One shared dispatch helper replaces both fall-throughs: EffectRunner when injected (unchanged); otherwise the legacy runner with an EFFECTFUL leaf tagged machine-readably (effect_journal: "bypassed-no-effect-runner") and a loud stderr warning naming the sink. Pure/engine-control leaves are untouched.
- Rationale for warn-first: flipping straight to fail-closed would break flywheel's dispatch_job live path (a shipping consumer) in the same commit. The flip is THIS bead's follow-up, after flywheel injects an EffectRunner.

FOLLOW-UP (owned here, not in this slice)
1. flywheel injects an EffectRunner so its dispatch_job/send_message leaves journal intent -> claim -> settle.
2. Then flip the bypass to FAIL-CLOSED (refuse, do not dispatch) — flywheel + toron-workflow AGENTS updated in the same change.
3. Route HostSink{verify} through the effect surface too (currently unreachable by an injected EffectRunner).
4. Engine-side run lifecycle rows (Started -> Running -> terminal) via the injected journal, replacing the host-only create_run/cas_run_status calls.

NOT DONE: no PR, no gate row, no close.
PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works (every claim read off HEAD, no inferred state), fix-root-causes (the fall-through is the root cause; the tag makes it loud instead of silencing it), sequence-verifiable-units (warn-first slice lands before the breaking flip).
close_reason:
Flip landed: EffectJournalMode (Enforced refuses a journal-less effectful leaf before its provider runs; Recording is the explicit dry-arm carve-out) plus HostSink{verify} routed through the effect surface, journaling around the engine-executed VerifySink result carried on RunContext.provider_result. prove-it-works — every claim was read off running code: hermetic live probes and new unit tests pin the refusal (including that the attached sink NEVER ran), the Recording marker, and the journaled rendered verify. fix-root-causes — verify's dispatch was unified onto the shared path instead of patched, which is what surfaced and fixed the render bug the private arm carried (a templated command reached the sink verbatim). sequence-verifiable-units — the warn-first marker slice landed first; this is the flip its own note deferred, with the remaining run-lifecycle item re-cut to bd-mi9n rather than buried.
VERIFY: toron-workflow 257 passed + toron-mcp 82 passed, all other toron suites green; flywheel 1740 unit + every integration suite green; clippy -D warnings + fmt clean in both trees; live hermetic probe (TORON_DATA_DIR/XDG redirected): execute-arm journaled verify|settled|{"action":"verify","command":"echo RENDERED-hello"} with receipt RENDERED-hello, dry arm journaled nothing and was not refused.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
SLICE LANDED 2026-09-14 (warn-first half; the fail-closed flip is still open).

WHAT CHANGED
- control_flow.rs: one shared `dispatch_leaf_or_compat()` replaces BOTH silent fall-throughs (the step dispatch inside `run_step_with_enclosing`, and the graph leaf). EffectRunner injected -> unchanged (context-bearing path wins). Otherwise the legacy runner runs the leaf and, for a HOST-SINK action (partition -> HostSink{mailbox|job|verify}), the value is tagged `effect_journal` and the engine warns loudly to stderr.
- Two markers, because the gaps differ: `bypassed-no-effect-runner` (nothing injected) and `bypassed-sink-uncovered` (a runner IS injected but `dispatch_leaf` does not cover the sink, e.g. verify). Pure/engine-control leaves are untouched (no tag).
- Why warn-first, not fail-closed: flipping now would break flywheel's `dispatch_job` live path in the same change. Mirrors the ADR-0022 plan-artifact gate's own idiom ("warn + tag, never block; the W5 flip owns blocking").

EVIDENCE
- New tests: `effectful_leaf_without_effect_runner_is_marked_not_silent` (RED before, GREEN after) + control `effectful_leaf_with_effect_runner_is_not_marked` (runner handled the leaf, 1 call, no marker).
- `mbx test -p toron-workflow`: 248 passed, 0 failed. One existing test updated: `graph_parallel_node_expands_copies` had pinned an incidental JSON prefix `[{"scouted":true}`; it now pins the scout key/value AND asserts the marker propagates into the downstream render (strengthened, not weakened).
- `mbx test -p toron-mcp effect_runner`: journaled path still handles run-scoped keys (unchanged).
- `mbx check --workspace --all-targets` clean; fmt + clippy -D warnings clean on toron-workflow.
- Consumer: flywheel `mbx test --bin flywheel` 1716 passed + verify-clippy clean (the tag is additive to step values).

STILL OPEN (the flip, this bead)
1. flywheel injects an EffectRunner (it injects none today) so dispatch_job/send_message leaves journal intent -> claim -> settle.
2. Then make the bypass FAIL-CLOSED and update flywheel + toron-workflow AGENTS together.
