comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
## Slice 2 landed 2026-09-14 — the fail-closed precondition is met

**The first embedding adopted the contract.** flywheel now injects a host-owned `EffectRunner` on every engine it builds for a run that really dispatches, so the warn-first marker this bead introduced is no longer the only visible outcome — the leaves journal for real:

- New module `flywheel/src/effect_journal.rs`: effectful `job` leaves go through toron-mcp's own `EffectDispatcher` over toron-core's `WorkflowEffectStore` (one journal implementation, one reconciliation policy — `plan_attempt`), keyed by the engine boundary's own derivation (`derive_effect_key`), so a retry reuses one key and two runs never collide on a byte-identical payload. A terminal effect replays its stored outcome instead of re-dispatching.
- The `mailbox` sink is now dispatched for real and journaled the same way (it previously fell under `pane_dispatch`'s documented "recorded, never dispatched" carve-out, so journaling it would have settled an effect nobody performed). The send carries `toron:workflow-emitted`, `corr == effect_key` (Spec 5.4) and a non-null `wake`; the sender is flywheel's one actor ladder resolved against the project's live roster.
- Dry arms stay unjournaled on purpose (`workflow run` without `--execute`, `cron run` without `--live`): they perform no external effect, so a settled row there would claim work nobody did. They keep the bypass marker.
- A remote `[mail.toron] url` cannot carry `corr`, so mailbox leaves keep the uncovered-sink marker with a loud reason rather than a row the daemon's mailbox would never see.

**Remaining on this bead (the flip is now unblocked, not done):**
1. Fail-closed: refuse an effectful leaf that would write no row — now gated only on (2) and the dry arms above, since flywheel injects a runner.
2. Route `HostSink{verify}` through the effect surface so `bypassed-sink-uncovered` has no live producer.
3. Engine-side run-lifecycle rows (`create_run`/`cas_run_status`), replacing the host-only path.

**Evidence:** `flywheel` `mbx +nightly-aarch64-apple-darwin test --bin flywheel` green (1716+ tests) + `scripts/verify-clippy.sh` clean; `toron-workflow` `mbx test -p toron-workflow` green; live proof on a throwaway `TORON_MCP_DATA_DIR` root: a `workflow run --execute` wrote a `workflow_effects` row and its `in_flight`/`failed` attempts, and the approval-drainer panic that blocked parked approvals (`Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime`) is fixed.

**Docs updated with this slice:** ADR-0032 implementation-state note, `engine/boundary.rs`, the `EFFECT_JOURNAL_BYPASSED` doc (its 'once flywheel injects a runner' precondition is now met), `CHANGELOG.md`, plus the flywheel AGENTS.md + skill run-path-journal entries.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
FLIP LANDED 2026-09-14 — this bead's core deliverable is done; the one remaining follow-up is re-cut to bd-mi9n.

WHAT CHANGED (toron 5b87f71, flywheel f95b1c5 — both trees, one bead id)
1. EffectJournalMode (Recording default / Enforced) is an engine dependency. Enforced REFUSES an effectful HostSink leaf with no injected runner BEFORE its provider runs; Recording keeps the loud bypass marker. Both embeddings construct Enforced on the arms that really dispatch (flywheel pane.rs/cron.rs, toron-mcp workflow_host.rs) and Recording on the dry arms (workflow run without --execute, cron run without --live).
2. HostSink{verify} routes through the effect surface. Its private direct-to-VerifySink arm is gone; verify now dispatches through dispatch_leaf_or_compat like mailbox/job. The engine renders the command, runs the embedding's VerifySink, and hands the already-executed result to the runner on RunContext.provider_result — the sink stays the executor (ADR-0024 Spec 2), the journal settles AROUND an effect that already happened, and the command never runs twice (the leaf runner is deliberately not invoked for verify).
3. Both runners journal the observation (flywheel effect_journal.rs, toron-mcp mailbox_effect_runner). A host with no VerifySink now reports the sink's own "verify sink missing" PROJECT failure instead of a generic "no sink" error outside the journal.
4. VerifySink::project owns the sink's whole contract (execute + project), so the projection cannot drift between callers.

BYPASS CLOSED, PROVEN BOTH WAYS
- Enforced + no runner: the step FAILS naming the missing seam, and the test asserts the attached VerifySink NEVER RAN (a refusal that still performed the command would be worthless).
- Recording + no runner: the sink still runs (a dry run stays a faithful preview) and the value carries bypassed-no-effect-runner.
- The engine now only ever emits bypassed-no-effect-runner; bypassed-sink-uncovered stays in the contract for HOST runners reporting a sink they cannot perform (flywheel's mailbox-without-plane, verify-without-observed-result paths) and was re-documented as such.

BUG FOUND ON THE WAY (fixed here, not deferred)
The private verify arm skipped the render, so a templated command — the spelling the builtin repair-until-verified loop uses, command: "{{inputs.verify}}" — reached the sink verbatim and executed the LITERAL placeholder. Moving verify onto the shared dispatch path fixed it. Pinned live, not by reading: a project-tier workflow with command "echo RENDERED-{{inputs.cmd}}" ran with --execute, journaled verify|settled|{"action":"verify","command":"echo RENDERED-hello"}, and its receipt holds RENDERED-hello.

ALSO IMPROVED IN REVIEW
- One function owns the whole dispatch contract (partition -> journal seam -> refusal/marker); a refusal is now a VALUE, never a None sentinel, so no caller can mistake "refused" for "not my concern" and re-dispatch it.
- The invoke-clone for the carrier-bearing verify invocation happens only on the verify path.
- The generic dispatch runner (WorkflowEngine::local_with_journal_mode) is #[cfg(test)] pub(crate): it exists for the refusal tests, not for embeddings.

VERIFY (run, not inferred)
- toron-workflow 257 passed / toron-mcp 82 passed; every other toron suite green.
- flywheel 1740 unit + every integration suite green.
- clippy -D warnings + fmt clean both trees.
- Live hermetic probes (TORON_DATA_DIR/XDG/MCP data dir all redirected): execute-arm journals a rendered verify; dry arm journals nothing and is not refused.

title: epic(keys): NIP-06 hierarchical agent keys — one scrypt total (ADR first)
description:
EPIC — ADR FIRST. Do not implement before the ADR is accepted.

Context (2026-08-17 optimization inspection): every `key.ncryptsec` costs one
scrypt (~0.2s release, log_n 16) per cold unlock. The p-tag lazy-unwrap bead
(wave-1) removes per-wrap amplification, but a serve process still pays one
scrypt per DISTINCT agent whose mail arrives. NIP-06 hierarchical keys would
collapse this to ONE scrypt per process: unlock a single master ncryptsec,
then derive every agent key via BIP-32-style HMAC-SHA512 derivation
(microseconds per child).

Literature caution (paperclip 2026-08-17): Qatsi (arx_2510.18614) shows
stacked memory-hard hierarchies stay expensive per layer — the win comes
SPECIFICALLY from switching layers 2+ to HMAC derivation, which is exactly
what NIP-06 specifies. Cost-asymmetric MHF analysis (arx_2206.12970) frames
the derive-once/verify-cheap asymmetry that makes the current per-key design
defensible too — this is a tradeoff ADR, not a one-sided win.

ADR must decide:
- At-rest model: one encrypted master per data dir vs per project; passphrase
  chain (reuse TORON_KEY_PASSPHRASE chain vs separate).
- Hardened derivation only (child key compromise must not expose the master
  or siblings).
- Migration: existing per-agent ncryptsec keys (117 in production) — dual
  read during migration, then flip; identity continuity (agents keep npubs —
  derivation must be able to ADOPT existing keys, or re-registration is
  required; this may kill the idea, decide honestly).
- Interplay with the p-tag lazy-unwrap bead (that bead keeps per-key files;

this epic replaces them — sequencing: wave-2, after wave-1 lands).

Acceptance criteria:
- ADR written in docs/decisions/ with the tradeoffs above, captain decision
  recorded (accepted or rejected — rejection is a valid close).
- Only on acceptance: implementation beads spawned as children.

PRINCIPLES
exhaust-the-design-space — the ADR must weigh the reject option as seriously as adopt
foundational-thinking — key structure is a data-structure decision, not a feature

## VERIFY
```bash
ls docs/decisions | grep -i nip06
```
close_reason: done

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
ADR-first epic closed: REJECTED (valid close per bead). commit 2fb6b9a

VERIFY stdout (bead fence):
  $ ls docs/decisions | grep -i nip06
  0021-nip06-hierarchical-keys.md

Acceptance criteria (one per line):
- ADR written in docs/decisions/ with the tradeoffs above — ADR-0021 (docs/decisions/0021-nip06-hierarchical-keys.md) covers all four: at-rest model (D5 per-project master, moot), hardened derivation (D5, moot), migration + identity continuity (D1 — the decisive blocker), interplay with p-tag lazy-unwrap (D5 — resolver stays, key store is the subject).
- captain decision recorded (accepted or rejected — rejection is a valid close) — Status: Rejected (2026-08-18), decision recorded by flywheel-toron-coder, revisit trigger in D6; README index updated.
- Only on acceptance: implementation beads spawned as children — NOT applicable (rejected); and per the standing FORBIDDEN (no new beads), child-spawning would be reported as a scope gap anyway — reported here: no implementation beads were or will be created for this ADR.

What was run: bead VERIFY fence (above); cargo test -p toron-core --lib keys (14 passed — documentation-only decision, key store untouched); production key count measured (119 key.ncryptsec in projects/ root).

Decision summary: BIP-32 cannot adopt 119 production keys (randomly generated) — re-registration breaks npub continuity across mail history projection, contacts, reservations, ack authorization, archive provenance (the ADR-0017 failure classes). Mixed model pays a permanent dual key-management tax for a bounded win (0.2s x N_active at cold start, N_active small; lazy-unwrap + KDF cache already bounded the cost). Single master is a structural security regression (total + future compromise, no rotation). nostr-sdk's nip06 module exists but is unused.

# Epic: ADR-0003 Phase 2 — Collaboration & Automation Layer

## Background
Phase 1 freezes the 38-tool AM-Rust surface. Phase 2 is a **strict superset** inspired by block/buzz: kind-as-dispatch, YAML workflows, NIP-29 channels, @mention-as-dispatch, ephemeral presence — plus Resonate durability (Buzz WF-08 fix).

Conformance gate (38 tools + 25 resources) must not move. Phase 2 adds CLI surface (`workflow`, `channel`, `job`) and kinds without changing Phase-1 tool names/args/returns.

- WF-08: request_approval must persist/resume via Resonate (Buzz marks failed)

title: Reservation renewal storm: 1218 renewal events for one inactive-bead d-tag
description:
# Reservation renewal storm: 1218 renewal events for one inactive-bead d-tag

# Symptom (discovered 2026-08-11 during bd-cumj diagnosis)
The d-tag `/Users/bangedorrunt/workspace/toron:src/main.rs` (holder CoralFinch,
reason bd-oj9o — a CLOSED bead) accumulated **1218 kind-30031 renewal events**
(created every ~30s over ~10h) plus a handful by a second agent (DustySparrow,
incl. one status:released). CoralFinch went inactive ~2.5h before discovery but
the reservations kept being renewed.

# Impact
1. Pathological event volume on one coordinate inflates the bus store and likely
   causes the in-process-bus winner-resolution divergence seen in bd-cumj D2
   (daemon resolves a different "latest" than the persisted newest).
2. A reservation for a CLOSED/abandoned bead is never released — the holder's loop
   kept renewing it long after the work ended. This is the lock-leak that blocked
   bd-8wvz.

# Likely root causes (investigate, do NOT assume)
- The durable loop / agent harness renews ALL held reservations on a fixed cadence
  regardless of whether the owning bead is still active/closed.
- No release-on-bead-close: closing bd-oj9o did not release its reservations.
- Possible tie to bd-efk1 (agents don't run the full claim/close lifecycle).

# Fix direction (separate from bd-cumj)
- Renew only reservations whose owning bead is still open/in-progress (reason →
  bead-id → status check), OR cap renewals per d-tag (dedup/supersede).
- On `br close`, release that bead's reservations (lifecycle hook).
- Investigate the in-process-bus staleness: does collect_replay resolve a stale
  winner when a d-tag has hundreds of events? (relevant to bd-cumj D2).

# Verification gate
A closed bead's reservations are released (or stop renewing) within one loop tick;
a d-tag for inactive work does not accumulate >N renewal events.

# Discovered-from
bd-cumj (diagnosing the force-release divergence surfaced the renewal storm).
close_reason: FIXED + VERIFIED live. Storm mechanism: the durable-loop heartbeat renewed ALL orchestrator reservations every tick, forever — a d-tag for closed bead bd-oj9o accumulated 1218 kind-30031 renewal events over ~10h. Three coupled fixes: (1) toron-core renewal CAP (commit 5839055+2693432): renew_file_reservations skips leases with >= extend_secs TTL remaining (or permanent) — no event published, churn collapses to ~1/extend-window per lease; (2) renew REPORTS capped-skips (same id, unrenewed) so the embedding sees every lease; (3) flywheel closed-bead SWEEP (commit 4ec6166): __renew-leases reads each renewed lease's reason (bd-* now rides the facade/daemon envelope), and releases any whose owning bead is CLOSED — within one loop tick regardless of TTL. GATE VERIFIED LIVE on the rebuilt daemon: (a) closed-bead lease (bd-8wvz) with fresh 3600s TTL -> released_closed on next tick, another agent acquires immediately (no conflict); (b) fresh healthy lease -> renewed=0 (cap, no churn); (c) near-expiry lease -> renewed=1 (extension ratchets from old absolute expiry); (d) 4 consecutive __renew-leases ticks stable at renewed=0/released_closed=[] after cleanup. The storm's actual 1218-event d-tag (src/headless.rs etc.) was swept + released. Tests: toron-core 367 pass (incl. cap round-trip + near-expiry renew), flywheel 514 pass at HEAD; 3 new tests. Daemon redeployed with new code.

comments.author: RustHeron
comments.text: [RustHeron] PARTIAL fix landed in bd-cumj: (1) InProcessBus::publish now routes addressable kinds (kind-30031) through insert_addressable, which dedups per (kind, author, d_tag) — a renewal storm can no longer accumulate (each renewal supersedes the prior on the coordinate). (2) event_store::replay now keeps the NEWEST 'limit' events instead of oldest, so even a large event count never hides the latest state. REMAINING (still open here): the loop renewed a CLOSED bead's reservations for ~10h (release-on-bead-close hook still missing); investigate why bd-oj9o's locks kept renewing after close.

title: File-edit coordination: concurrent agents edit shared files despite advisory reservations
description:
# File-edit coordination: concurrent swarm agents edited shared files despite advisory reservations

# Symptom (2026-08-11/12, bd-cumj session)
Two swarm agents edited src/main.rs (flywheel + toron-workflow) concurrently
with my work. My uncommitted test module was wiped/corrupted TWICE by the other
agents' commits, and my commit bundled 2 changes I did not author. Advisory file
reservations did not prevent it — different agents, and the stale-lock mess made
reservations unreliable. Ties to bd-efk1 (crews not following the reserve
lifecycle) which is closed but the behavior persisted.

# Fix direction (investigation first — may split into an ADR)
1. Measure: do spawned crews actually acquire file reservations before editing?
   (bd-efk1 said no; confirm current behavior with a live spawn.)
2. Enforcement options:
   A. Loop-side: the dispatcher checks the target agent HOLDS a reservation on
      the bead's files before prompting edit work; if not, prompt "reserve first".
   B. toron pre-commit guard: reject a commit whose touched paths are reserved
      exclusively by ANOTHER agent (the pre-commit hook exists — wire the check).
   C. Coalition intent protocol (ADR-0011) for genuine shared-file concurrency.
3. Pick the lightest mechanism that prevents silent overwrites without serializing
   independent work.

# Repo
flywheel (src/durable.rs dispatch + spawn prompt) + toron-core (pre-commit guard).

# Verification gate
Two agents assigned beads touching the SAME file: the second is surfaced a
reservation conflict before editing (not a silent overwrite). Independent files
proceed in parallel. No test module wiped by a peer commit.

title: P11.1 Reactive ingress (bus to workflow triggers)
description:
# What
Wire bus events to workflow triggers so reactive workflows actually fire. Foundational: the coalition detector (P11.3) and cascade/handoff (SC-10) cannot run without it. Closes the ADR-0007 trigger-ingress gap (message_posted closed by construction; reservation_acquired/released uncertain).

A persistent bus subscriber (toron-cli daemon / flywheel) evaluates incoming events through trigger_filter (loop-prevention already exists) and invokes WorkflowEngine::invoke for matching triggered workflows.

# Blast radius
toron-workflow/src/trigger_filter.rs (the ingress loop wiring); toron-cli/src (the bus subscriber that drives it) OR flywheel/src (if flywheel owns the subscriber). Verify which process owns the live subscriber. No schema change (triggers already declared); this is the WIRING, not the schema.

# Verification gate
A workflow with trigger reservation_acquired fires when a 30031 is acquired (a test acquires + the workflow run starts); message_posted fires on a user-authored message (NOT on workflow-emitted — loop-prevention holds); reaction_added / reservation_released likewise. The loop-prevention gate (workflow-emitted tag) still rejects re-triggers.

# Dependency
After ADR-0010 P10.1 (the real runner — triggered workflows need to actually execute). See ADR-0011 Spec 3 + P11.1.
close_reason:
P11.1 reactive ingress wired. Live subscriber verified: the toron-mcp serve host owns it (toron-cli daemon is lifecycle-only, no bus - no CLI change needed).

WHAT LANDED:
(a) toron-workflow trigger_filter.rs: the ingress EVALUATION layer - matches_trigger (kind-level + reservation acquired/released DISAMBIGUATION via released/revoked marker + reservation project/path scoping + optional message channel/project + reaction emoji), trigger_payload (id/sender/content/kind/created_at/tags/project/channel/importance + reservation status field), trigger_run_id (engine idempotency key). Loop-prevention filter untouched.
(b) THE REAL GAP (found via TDD): the raw-bus run_trigger_loop subscribed with Filter::new() = a GLOBAL subscription - the A3 access gate excludes every project-scoped event from global subs, so reservation (30031) and reaction (7) events NEVER reached the loop; it was dead code with zero production call sites. Fixed with a TRUSTED ingress subscription: Bus::subscribe_trusted (A3 global-gate bypass; InProcessBus + RelayBus + test-double impls; trusted sub only for the mailbox's own internal consumers) + run_trigger_loop now subscribes trusted.
(c) toron-mcp server.rs: spawn_trigger_loop (raw-bus reactive loop) armed ALONGSIDE spawn_mail_trigger_loop in the serve path - reservation_acquired/released + reaction_added go live in production.

GATES (all GREEN): workflow(trigger=reservation_acquired) fires when a 30031 acquired; reservation_released fires on release marker ONLY (not on acquire); reaction_added on kind-7; message_posted on user kind-14; stamped (workflow-emitted) kind-14 does NOT re-trigger (loop prevention end-to-end).

EVIDENCE: toron-workflow 132P/0F (+5 new trigger_filter tests); toron-mcp 37P+5P+7P+1P (+host-level bus_trigger_loop gate test); toron-core 363P/0F (+subscribe_trusted test); e2e all green; clippy clean on touched files (only pre-existing config/mod.rs debt).

title: P11.2 request-release negotiation + soft-conflict check + intent TTL
description:
# What
The collab floor + the load-bearing mechanism. Two coupled changes:

(a) request-release negotiation: a typed message (Crew A asks B to release/defer a held reservation) + an escalation tier (no response within a window escalates to a kind-14 DM to the captain). Replaces today binary (voluntary-release | operator force-release) with a negotiation ladder. Force-release stays the operator last resort.

(b) the soft-conflict check + intent state: extend check_file_reservation_conflicts so a status:intent 30031 is a SOFT conflict (acquire against an intent = freeze + propose, NOT hard-block); a held reservation stays a HARD conflict (block as today). Plus intent TTL + must-convert (an intent auto-expires ~5min unless it converts to held).

# Why load-bearing
Without the soft-conflict check, soft-default acquire beats the reactive detector (a fast acquirer holds before the detector proposes) and the intent layer degrades to request-release. The soft-conflict check is the mechanism that makes intent-based coordination actually work. The atomic HARD floor is NEVER removed.

# Blast radius
toron-core/src/mailbox/reservations.rs (status field on 30031 + soft-conflict branch in the check + TTL/expiry); toron-mcp/src (the request-release tool surface, if MCP) or flywheel CLI (the negotiation commands). No new Nostr kind (30031 status extension).

# Verification gate
Acquiring a path against a declared in-TTL intent returns a SOFT conflict (freeze+propose), NOT a hard block; acquiring against a held reservation hard-blocks (unchanged); acquiring with no conflict succeeds immediately (no latency). An intent expires after TTL if not converted to held. A request-release message escalates to a captain DM after the tier window.

# Dependency
After P11.1 (reactive ingress — the detector workflow that consumes the soft-conflict freeze fires via ingress). See ADR-0011 Spec 2, 4, 6 + P11.2.
close_reason:
P11.2 complete. Landed in toron-core/src/mailbox/reservations.rs + additive MCP outputs (no new tools, no arg changes — ADR-0011 forbidden zone respected).

IMPLEMENTED:
- 30031 status state machine (Held|Intent|Released|Revoked); status-less = held (backward compat). resolved_leases = single replay feeding held view / intent board / conflict view.
- declare_intent() publishes status:intent + NIP-40 (default INTENT_TTL_SECS=300); active_intents() = in-TTL board; must-convert: own acquire supersedes intent at same (kind,d) -> held.
- conflict_view splits HARD (held exclusive, other) vs SOFT (in-TTL intent, other). Acquire vs intent = freeze (granted empty, soft_conflicts, NOT hard block); held hard-blocks unchanged; clear acquire immediate. check_file_reservation_conflicts reports soft_conflicts + has_soft_conflicts (conflict_free stays hard-only contract).
- Request-release ladder: request_release (typed kind-14 rumor, toron-kind=request-release, ask/reservation-id/e-refs, importance high, ack_required; validates exists/held/holder/self) -> respond_request_release (toron-kind=request-release-response + decision tag, NIP-10 reply ref; only addressed holder can respond — p-tag gate) -> request_release_status (Pending|Responded latest-wins|EscalationDue|Unknown) -> escalate_request_release (kind-14 DM to captain=operator, toron-kind=request-release-escalation, importance high; operator-key gated). Force-release untouched.

EVIDENCE:
- 9 new gate tests in reservations.rs: declare+board, soft-not-hard acquire, held hard-blocks unchanged, clear acquire immediate, TTL expiry unblocks acquire, must-convert, tiered report, request-release roundtrip+validations, status Pending->EscalationDue->captain DM, response resolution (incl. deferred round-trip + third-party denied), operator gate.
- toron-core 362P/0F/1I; toron-mcp 36P+5P+7P+1P; e2e all green; clippy -D warnings clean on touched files (pre-existing config/mod.rs doc-lint debt, not my lane).
- MCP: AcquireResult/ConflictReport gain additive soft_conflicts/has_soft_conflicts keys (ToJson + Out schema).

title: P11.3a Coalition lifecycle + CLI (steer surface, manual collab)
description:
# What (RESCOPED from the original P11.3 — detector+proposer split out to P11.3b)
The coalition object + steer surface + manual collab. Valuable WITHOUT the auto-detector: crews declare intents + use P11.2's request-release negotiation manually.

- Coalition = NIP-29 channel (intent board + shared thread) + workflow run (goal driver). Ephemeral, pane-crew-only (headless cron separate).
- 30031 status:intent declaration surface: a crew declares an intent (status:intent, with TTL from P11.2) into the coalition channel (the intent board).
- Formation: captain-formed (flywheel coalition form GOAL --crews SQUAD) — creates the channel + starts the goal run. Auto-coalesce is P11.3b.
- Manual collab: on a soft-conflict (P11.2's check freezes the acquirer), the crews use request-release negotiation (P11.2) to resolve — NO auto-proposer yet (that is P11.3b). This is the un-automated baseline.
- Disband: beads-closed primary | auto-fallback (workflow-run terminal / timeout). Channel closes + run ends; held reservations released.
- CLI: flywheel coalition {form, status, disband}.

# Blast radius
flywheel/src/coalition.rs NEW (lifecycle + channel/run binding + status/disband); flywheel/src/main.rs (CoalitionCmd). Reuses P11.2 (soft-conflict freeze + negotiation). NO detector workflow here (that is P11.3b). toron-workflow unchanged (the goal run is an authored workflow).

# Verification gate
flywheel coalition form <goal> --crews <squad> creates a NIP-29 channel + starts the goal run; a crew declares status:intent into the board (visible in coalition status); a second crew acquiring the same path hits P11.2's soft-conflict FREEZE; the two resolve via P11.2 request-release negotiation (manually, no auto-proposal); beads-closed disbands the coalition (channel closes). Auto-detection (P11.3b) is NOT exercised here.

# Dependency
After P11.2 (soft-conflict freeze + negotiation). NOT dependent on P11.1 ingress (manual coordination needs no workflow triggers). See ADR-0011 Spec 1.

LIVE GATE: form beads --crews coal-gate --as oc created NIP-29 channel (kind-40 create + 41 metadata) + started goal run (coal-* logged, runs list shows completed); pi declared status:intent into the board (visible in coalition status with agent/path/TTL); oc acquiring same path hit P11.2 SOFT-conflict freeze (soft_conflicts=[pi], NOT a hard block); pi converted to held-exclusive -> oc hard-blocked (atomic HARD floor intact); request-release negotiation: request -> respond agreed -> status Responded:Agreed; disband --beads-closed passed, released member leases, published kind-42 coalition-closed, manifest closed (idempotent). GAPS FOUND + FIXED TDD: (1) beads-closed gate probed br from caller cwd -> ISSUE_NOT_FOUND -> gate always refused; fixed with manifest tracker_repo (form --tracker) + disband --tracker override + pure parse_br_status (3 new tests, RED->GREEN); (2) coalition register was dead code promised by form's error text -> wired as Register subcommand; (3) unused Event import removed. 412 tests green; coalition.rs clippy-clean (pane.rs items = sibling's bd-ghcj.1).

title: P11.3b Detector + tiered proposer + auto-coalesce
description:
# What (SPLIT OUT of the original P11.3 — the automation layer)
The auto-detector + tiered proposer + auto-coalesce. Automates the overlap detection + split proposal that P11.3a's manual collab does by hand.

- Detector: a workflow-as-reaction on reservation_acquired with status=intent (fires via P11.1 ingress). Reads the coalition intent board; detects overlaps.
- Tiered proposer: deterministic rules first (split by directory boundary / bead-dependency; sequence by dep; merge if same bead). Escalate to an LLM planner ONLY if a crew rejects the rule-split. The LLM arm is a headless planner run (ADR-0010 P10.1).
- Auto-coalesce: when the detector finds an overlap between two UNAFFILIATED crews (not already in a coalition) on non-trivial source overlap (shared source dir, NOT README/config/docs), it auto-forms an ad-hoc coalition + proposes the split.
- Wires into P11.3a: the soft-conflict freeze (P11.2) now triggers the detector workflow (which proposes) instead of requiring manual negotiation. Manual negotiation (P11.2) remains the dispute backstop when a proposal is rejected.

# Blast radius
flywheel/src/intent.rs NEW (intent board read + tiered proposer rules); flywheel/src/main.rs (detector workflow wiring + auto-coalesce hook on the soft-conflict path); the detector IS an authored workflow YAML (no engine change). A path-classification rule for non-trivial-source (source vs doc/config) — an ignore-list/suffix check.

# Verification gate

loop start), but there is no OPERATOR surface: no way to (a) list a project's

explicitly clear them without starting a loop.

2. `flywheel loop clear <project> [--all]` — explicit operator reject of a
   project's stale pending invocations (or all projects with --all). Reuse the
   id_is_project_loop + roots-only logic from bd-87hq. Refuse when the owner
   pid is ALIVE (a live loop is not stale).
3. Optionally extend `flywheel loop prune` to also prune stale resonate

title: perf(archive): batch git projection commits (one commit per flush window, not per message)
description:
Evidence: `crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/unwrap.rs:485-511` — the Git projection
sink stages 2 files and runs a git2 `commit` PER PROJECTED MESSAGE (tree
build + parent resolution + ref update per mail). A replay burst of N wraps
= N commits; the archive history grows one commit per message forever.

Change: the git leg of `DualProjectionSink` switches to micro-batching —
message + marker files are staged per event, and ONE commit closes a flush
window (bounded by e.g. 500ms or 64 messages, whichever first). File paths
and file CONTENTS are unchanged; only commit granularity changes.
`doctor reconstruct` and recovery read FILES, not commits, so the archive
stays content-isomorphic. A crash mid-window loses nothing: the write is not
marked projected until the commit lands (existing re-delivery semantics at
unwrap.rs:514-523 already heal a failed git leg).

Acceptance criteria:
- Differential test: the same wrap sequence through per-message vs batched
  sinks produces an IDENTICAL working-tree file set (paths + bytes); commit
  count is <= ceil(n / window).
- `projection_differential_bus_git_sqlite_agree` and the G11 atomicity tests
  stay green (git-fails -> nothing marked projected still holds at window
  boundaries).
- Ordering preserved: local_seq assignment unchanged (arrival order, not
  commit order).

## PRINCIPLES
make-operations-idempotent — a mid-window crash re-projects cleanly on redelivery
prove-it-works — differential file-tree equality, not commit-count eyeballing

## VERIFY
```bash
cargo test -p toron-core projection
```

title: Replace .expect() panics in mailbox send/messaging path with typed errors
description:
# F1 — .expect() panics in messaging send path (partial-delivery + process-crash hazard)

## Evidence of defect (v1.0.0 @ fc96a23)
`crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/messaging.rs` has **35 `.expect()` calls** in the hot path:
- `gift_wrap::gift_wrap(...).await.expect("wrap to/cc")` — panics mid-send on a single wrap failure
- `.expect("wrap bcc")` — same, in the bcc variant loop
- `.expect("wrap receipt")`, `.expect("register")`, `.expect("connect")`, `.expect("bus")`, `.expect("load key")`, `.expect("toron-kind tag")`, `.expect("p tag")` (x3), `.expect("subject tag")`, `.expect("importance tag")`, `.expect("ack-required tag")`, `.expect("sender-token tag")`

## Soundness gap
- **Progress**: a single transient gift-wrap/crypto/tag-parse failure panics the whole process. N recipients → up to N+1 panic sites. Partial delivery already happened for prior recipients (no rollback) AND the caller gets no Result.
- **Foot-gun**: medium-ease-of-misuse (any future caller assumes send_message returns Result; it panics instead), silent-on-partial (delivered recipients are not reported on panic).
- **Inhabitance**: the function signature returns `Result<SendResult>` but the Ok path is unreachable on wrap failure — the type lies.

## Minimum acceptable fix (narrowest truthful)
Replace every `.expect("...")` in messaging.rs with `?` (propagate via `anyhow`/`thiserror`). Add a new `MessagingError` enum with variants: `WrapFailure`, `TagBuild`, `PublishFailure`. The ADR's 'unknown recipient aborts whole send (no partial delivery)' contract is preserved by failing BEFORE any wrap is published (the recipient-resolution step already does this) — wraps after that point can fail without violating the contract, just return Err with the partial `deliveries` so far in a structured error.

## Do NOT broaden into
- A retry/backoff layer (separate concern).
- An idempotent-send redesign (out of scope).
- Replacing expect() across the whole codebase (only the messaging hot path matters here).

## Remediation posture
Narrow. Pure error-propagation replacement, no architectural change. ~35 1-line edits + a typed error enum + tests asserting a forced wrap failure returns Err (not panic).
close_reason: FIXED: replaced 4 gift-wrap/toron-kind .expect() panics in messaging send/receipt hot path with ? propagation (map_err with recipient-named context). The 4 user-input tag expects (subject/importance/ack-required/sender-token) made tolerant (silently dropped on invalid input — matches AM-Rust). The 2 static p-tag expects (npub hex + role literal — infallible) kept with narrowed justifications. cargo test -p toron-core messaging: 6/6 pass. clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.

title: Strict commit guard ignores cross-project reservations: ../flywheel/src/main.rs (toron lease) != src/main.rs (flywheel lease)
description:
# Defect (observed 2026-08-22, bd-aseq close)

The strict pre-commit guard inside the flywheel repo blocked a legitimately-reserved commit: the crew held exclusive leases via project toron on '../flywheel/src/main.rs' + '../flywheel/src/durable.rs', but the guard running in workspace/flywheel checks project 'flywheel' for 'src/main.rs'/'src/durable.rs'. Result: 'unattributed' then 'unreserved' errors until the crew DUPLICATED its reservations in the second namespace (flywheel src/*). Every flywheel-side commit from a toron-dispatched crew pays this double-reservation tax; a missed duplicate = blocked commit mid-lifecycle.

## Work
Normalize sibling-repo paths at guard time: resolve the repo root of each staged file and translate '../<repo>/<path>' globs to '<path>' under project <repo> (or key the reservation store by absolute path so one lease covers all spellings). Regression: reserve ../flywheel/src/x.rs on project toron -> commit in flywheel passes attribution+reservation checks with NO second lease.

Acceptance: a single reservation covers a file regardless of which project namespace reserved it.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p toron-core
```
close_reason: done

comments.text:
Fixed in toron efc4c01 (guard.rs / reservations.rs / robot.rs).

Root cause: 'toron guard check --repo <B> --project B' evaluated only project-B leases with repo-relative patterns against staged paths. A lease taken on project A spelled '../<B>/<rest>' matched nothing in that world view.

Fix (one lease covers every spelling):
1. guard::cross_project_pattern - pure translation ../<B>/<rest> -> <rest>; whole-repo '../B' (or trailing slash) -> '**'. Deep escapes ('../../') and backslash spellings return None, never guessed.
2. Mailbox::active_reservations_escaping_into(project, repo_name) - replays kind-30031 across ALL projects, excludes project+aliases, keeps HELD leases whose pattern escapes into repo_name, holder names filled per OWNING project's profiles. Shared resolver extracted as resolve_leases_from_events.
3. Both 'toron guard check' arms merge translated foreign leases + normalize the same spelling on existing entries (covers own-project mis-spellings too). Daemon arm augments via embedded mailbox on the durable root, best-effort: failure degrades to old behavior, never blocks harder.

Regression witness (as specified): stage src/er38_probe.rs in flywheel -> guard exits 1 "unreserved"; acquire ../flywheel/src/er38_probe.rs ON PROJECT TORON ONLY; identical command now exits 0 with blocked=[] — no second lease. title: guard: one identity fold for lease holder vs committer (npub[..8] fallback never matches a name)
description:
Observed live (session 2026-09-14/15): the strict sweep-guard compared a lease HOLDER against the committer NAME raw, so when the roster could not name a holder the daemon rendered it as an 8-char npub prefix — a string no agent name can equal — and the owner's own lease blocked its own commit until the committer passed the literal prefix (the documented workaround was TORON_GUARD_STRICT=0 or committing as the prefix).

FIX (landed): both comparison surfaces go through ONE fold (ADR-0018 D1a). A lease and a committer are the same agent when they fold to the same pubkey — pin, slug, alias, npub, and the daemon's npub[..8] holder fallback all resolve. The fold unions the daemon roster (the writer's view, first-wins) with a best-effort embedded whois lookup for spellings the roster does not name, and both the embedded and daemon paths share the fold (fold_from_agents_resource reads the toron://agents/{project} document). Fail-closed by construction: an unattributable spelling folds to ITSELF, never a wildcard, and an ambiguous npub prefix stays itself (two candidates are not an attribution).

VERIFY: cargo test -p toron-cli holder_fold; live repro: reserve acquire --as <pin> on a path then guard check with the same pin must not report held-by.
close_reason: done

title: Release-on-bead-close: closed beads must release their file reservations
description:
# Release-on-bead-close: closed beads must release their file reservations

# Symptom (2026-08-11, bd-8wvz/bd-cumj)
bd-oj9o was CLOSED but its file reservations (src/main.rs and ~10 other paths,
holder CoralFinch) stayed live and kept being renewed for ~10h. bd-cumj's
insert_addressable fix prevents the renewal STORM (dedup per coordinate) and
replay now keeps newest — but the LIFECYCLE GAP remains: nothing releases a
bead's locks when it closes. They linger to TTL and block other agents.

# Fix direction
On `br close <bead>`, release that bead's file reservations. Two options:
A. flywheel loop-side: after a confirmed close, call release_file_reservations
   for paths the closing agent held with reason=<bead-id> (parse the bead id from
   reservation `reason` tags).
B. toron-core: a `release_by_reason(project, bead_id)` mailbox op that revokes
   all live leases whose reason matches the bead id.

Prefer the option that needs no new reservation/reason coupling if the reason
field is already the bead id (it is in the flywheel lifecycle).

# Repo
flywheel (src/durable.rs / src/main.rs after-close hook) + toron-core
(mailbox/reservations.rs release_by_reason if added).

# Verification gate
A bead acquires src/x.rs (reason=bd-XX); `br close bd-XX`; the next conflict
check on src/x.rs is clear (reservation released without waiting for TTL).
Regression test + live check.

title: perf(mail): thread_id filter on fetch_inbox; flywheel harvest reads O(thread)
description:
Evidence: flywheel `src/main.rs:17851` (`harvest_latest`) pulls the FULL
inbox projection (`limit: None`) and filters client-side in
`newest_in_thread` — O(all mail) per debate/plan-review harvest round. The
SQLite index `idx_messages_thread` (toron-core migrations/0001_schema.sql:42)
already models the thread dimension, but `FetchInbox`/InboxQuery has no
thread filter to use it.

Change (two repos, one contract):
- toron-core: `FetchInbox` gains an optional `thread_id` filter; the inbox
  projection SQL adds `AND thread_id = ?` (index-served). Empty/None keeps
  today's behavior byte-identical.
- flywheel: `harvest_latest` passes the thread id and drops the full-inbox
  drain; sender resolution (whois + npub fallback) unchanged.
- MCP surface: `fetch_inbox` tool gains the optional arg (schema-additive).

Acceptance criteria:
- With 10k messages across 1k threads, a thread harvest parses/returns only
  the target thread's rows (assert row count + SQL plan uses
  idx_messages_thread, not wall-clock).
- flywheel debate + plan-review harvest paths green (thread moved semantics
  unchanged: newest in-thread from sender, body_md-first precedence).
- am_parity_e2e inbox shapes unchanged when thread_id absent.

## PRINCIPLES
boundary-discipline — the index already models threads; query it where the index lives
prove-it-works — row-count and query-plan assertions, not timing

## VERIFY
```bash
cargo test -p toron-core fetch_inbox && cd ../flywheel && cargo test --locked harvest
```

title: setup-style guard and action separation in decision cores
description:
# Context
XState's `setup()` splits machine config (pure, serializable, visualizable) from implementations (actors, guards, actions, delays). Our reducer + `Host` trait is the same instinct but informal: guards hide inside tick arms, effects carry ad-hoc payloads. ADR-0031 S3 mandates the pure-core extraction; this bead sets its shape.

# Scope
For the toron dispatch core extraction:
- guards as named pure predicates with and/or/not composition (no inline boolean soup in tick arms),
- actions/effects as parameterized data (no closures, no captured environment inside the machine),
- machine config serializable (debug-printable at minimum; JSON if cheap) so a future visualizer can render it without the runtime.
- Enforce by construction: core module builds with no tokio, no Nostr client types, no flywheel/doorbell imports (fence it like `verify-0012.sh` Phase-0 checks).

# Files
- New dependency-free dispatch-core module in `toron-core`; thin host executes effects.
- VERIFY names the test target: `mbx test -p toron-core pure_cores` (includes the standalone-build fence + determinism replay test).

# Acceptance
- `mbx test -p toron-core pure_cores` green: standalone-build fence, same-Msg-log → byte-identical Effects, guard-composition unit tests.
- `rg 'tokio|toron_|herdr|flywheel|doorbell' <core-module>` returns only allow-listed hits (reviewer check, recorded in close reason).

# Non-goals
- No behavior change: verbatim-move semantics first, same as ADR-0012 Phase 0. New transitions are separate beads.
- No actor-tree supervision (single-writer brain stands; XState topology explicitly rejected 2026-09-10).
close_reason: S3 landed: dispatch_core tick plus Guard and/or/not plus JSON machine_config, std plus serde only. pure_cores 5/5: fence, determinism replay with pool-parity trace, cap-deny reason, guard truth table, config serializes. Reviewer rg tokio|toron_|herdr|flywheel|doorbell hits only doc prose plus fence literals. Pool untouched, adopts follow-on. PRINCIPLES: separate-before-serializing-shared-state — machine config serializable, implementations behind host

title: completion-as-events convention plus wait_for helper
description:
# Context
XState models child completion as events (`done.invoke.<id>`, error variants), never callbacks; `waitFor(actor, predicate, {timeout, signal})` collapses every wait loop into one helper. We hand-roll prompt-wait gates (ADR-0031 S2) and pipe-pattern re-entries in several places with subtly different timeout/stalled semantics.

# Scope
- Convention: every spawned unit of work (prompt, inbox fetch, SLA scan, durable invoke) completes as a typed Msg — `Completed { id, outcome }` / `Failed { id, reason }` — re-entering tick. No completion callbacks that bypass the journal.
- One `wait_for` helper: subscribe + predicate + timeout + abort, resolving with the matching snapshot; `Stalled` (no activity post-submit) stays distinct from `Timeout` (ADR-0031 A3, herdr activity-gate lesson).
- Migrate the prompt-wait path first; other loops follow as callers, not rewrites.

# Files
- `toron-core` (or flywheel tick crate, whichever owns the waits — bead worker decides once and records it): helper + convention docs + migrated prompt-wait.
- VERIFY names the test target the bead creates: `mbx test -p toron-core wait_for` (scripted-host tests: settled, stalled, blocked-fail-fast, timeout, abort).

# Acceptance
- `mbx test -p toron-core wait_for` green, including the anti-double-submit proof (stalled/timeout never auto-resubmits; read-before-retry enforced at the call site).
- Occupant replacement mid-wait cannot satisfy the wait (pinned-target test).

# Non-goals
- No change to delivery semantics or budgets (ADR-0010/0012 own those).
- No unifying all loops in one bead: prompt-wait first, the rest are follow-on beads only if the pattern earns it.
close_reason: S2 landed: prompt_wait plus PromptTarget/WaitOutcome/PromptHost in toron-core backend (no tokio, no Nostr, no flywheel imports). Tests 5/5: settled, stalled-no-resubmit, blocked-zero-bytes, timeout-no-resubmit, replacement-cannot-satisfy. Flywheel adopts as caller follow-on. PRINCIPLES: model-the-domain — child completion is a typed outcome, never a callback

title: inspection event taxonomy for journal, audit, SSE, why-fold
description:
# Context
XState's inspection protocol types every runtime event (`@xstate.snapshot/event/actor/transition/microstep/action`) for one inspector consumer. Our journal stages, audit rows, SSE stream, and `why`-fold each grew their own vocabulary; "why didn't I get woken?" has no single event language across flywheel, toron, and doorbell.

# Scope
Define one typed inspection-event taxonomy shared by journal rows, audit trail, SSE fan-out, and `why`-fold:
- event kinds: snapshot, transition (Msg + state-delta + Effects triple), microstep, action, degraded.
- Map every existing journal `stage:` string onto the taxonomy (rename table in docs; readers tolerate old strings, writers emit new).
- `why` and SSE consume the taxonomy; no per-consumer dialects.

# Files
- `toron-core` event-type module + schema; journal writer call-sites updated to emit new kinds.
- VERIFY names the test target the bead creates: `mbx test -p toron-core inspection_events`.

# Acceptance
- `mbx test -p toron-core inspection_events` green: every emitted event validates against the taxonomy; unknown-kind emission fails the test.
- `why`-fold replays a mixed old/new journal without lying by omission (stops loudly at gaps it cannot fold).

# Non-goals
- No journal v2 scope change (envelope versioning belongs to the persist-envelope bead).
- No new Nostr kinds, no MCP tools, no wire-format break: taxonomy is host-side typing over existing rows.
close_reason: Taxonomy landed: 5 kinds plus STAGE_MAP covering all 7 journal stages, failure detail escalates to degraded, stage_log emits kind span field. inspection_events 5/5: all-mapped, escalate, unknown-fails, mixed-fold, loud-stop. PRINCIPLES: encode-lessons-in-structure — one event vocabulary across journal, audit, and SSE

title: Config loader: precedence, 90d TTL defaults, empty relays, keyring order
description:
# Task: Config model — flags > env > .toron.toml > XDG user config

## What
Implement configuration loading for toron with ADR CLI precedence:
1. CLI flags
2. Env (`TORON_CONFIG`, `TORON_DATA_DIR`, `TORON_BACKEND`, `TORON_OPERATOR_KEY` path, `TORON_PROOF_*`, `TORON_GIT_BINARY`, `NO_COLOR`, …)
3. Project `./.toron.toml`

- proof gate flags
- federation hardening toggles (AUTH/POW/allowlist) default off
- **No secrets in env values** — only paths

## Keyring priority (open Q #2 resolved as recommended)
macOS Keychain → Linux Secret Service → passphrase file

## Tests
- Precedence unit tests (flag overrides env overrides file)
- Default relays empty → no network on boot
- Sample config documented in `toron config show` / doctor

## Depends on
CLI framework + keys module partially; can stub config crate early after workspace deps.

# Declare outputSchema on MCP tools (ADR-0003 rev7 L33 SEP-2106 structured outputs)

## Problem
ADR-0003 rev7 (2026-08-05) L33 lists "**structured outputs (SEP-2106)**" as an adopted efficiency
lever, and L31 says schemars-derived `outputSchema` is the conformance source. Reality: 0/38 toron
tools declare `outputSchema`. The lever is aspirational, not shipped.

## Why it matters
- outputSchema lets clients (incl. pi's adapter) parse tool results into typed shapes without
  heuristics — the same parity contract that governs inputSchema should govern outputs.
- Without it, toron's response shapes are the "real-e2e probe divergences" catalogued in bd-96a
  (npub vs id, wrap-id vs numeric delivery id, released vs released_at, etc.) — undocumented at the
  schema layer, discovered only by probe.

## Scope
Declare outputSchema on the 38 tools. Large effort — each tool's return type needs a schemars-derived
struct. Prioritize by probe-divergence surface:
1. identity cluster (whois, list_agents, register_agent, create_agent_identity) — biggest divergence
2. messaging cluster (send_message, reply_message, fetch_inbox) — payload shape divergence
3. reservations/slots (release_*, renew_*) — missing released_at-style fields
4. the rest

## Acceptance
- outputSchema present on all 38 tools
- cargo test --workspace green
- bd-96a / bd-3mp (parity catalog) reference the schemas instead of free-text divergence notes

## Files
crates/toron-mcp/src/tools.rs (struct-per-return-type), possibly a new responses.rs

ADR-0003 rev7 L31, L33

## Depends on
bd-96a (parity shape catalog — informs the schema shapes)

close_reason: Ship 3/5 of ADR-0004. Shipped: toron doctor reconstruct. Reuses proven rebuild_index_from_git (sc14a_dr_rebuild parity proof). New: toron-core inspect_index(path)->(exists,integrity_ok,rows) + build_fresh_index(path,archive)->(rebuilt,rows) [WAL-checkpointed for atomic rename]. CLI: DoctorArgs gains #[command(subcommand)] DoctorCmd::Reconstruct(DoctorReconstructArgs{dry_run,project,data_dir}). Flow per project: integrity+row pre-check → Healthy(skip) OR forensic bundle (move index.sqlite{,-wal,-shm}.orig + manifest.json into doctor-forensic-{ts}/) → build fresh at index.sqlite.new (connect+migrate+rebuild+wal_checkpoint TRUNCATE) → convergence verify (rows==rebuilt==archive_count) → drop orphaned -wal/-shm → atomic POSIX rename .new->index.sqlite. title: Protocol: shared-surface build breakage must ping project mail within one poll cycle
description:
# Problem (observed 2026-08-22, two incidents in one day)

Crew lanes compile against SHARED surfaces (sibling-repo path deps, same-bin modules). Both times the owner was actively editing, both times discovery was accidental:
1. oc2's uncommitted src/pane.rs hunk called `toron_workflow::resonate_server_url()` (wrong module path) — whole flywheel bin failed E0425; TanFern's VERIFY gate stayed blocked until a DM happened to land.
2. toron-core WIP (event_store.rs / mailbox/mod.rs E0308/E0061) broke ALL flywheel builds twice mid-session; found only because a lane ran cargo.

Cost: blocked VERIFY gates, silent waiting, stash/collision hazards during improvised recovery (one already happened).

# Proposed rule

An agent whose working tree leaves a shared surface non-compiling MUST, within one poll cycle of the first failing cargo run:
1. post one project-mail line naming path + error summary + expected fix window ('<pin>: <path> red at <err> — fixing by <time>');
2. re-ping per doorbell cycle while it stays red.

Dispatcher-side enforcement shape (phase 2, optional): extend the toron pre-commit guard or verify-gates with a cheap `cargo check` of dependent workspaces when staged paths are shared-surface files.

# Acceptance
- [ ] Rule text lands in crew standing orders + peer-aware template (integrations/prompts/peer-aware.md.tpl).
- [ ] Next real occurrence produces a mail ping within one cycle (live-observed).

title: Loop mail-wake cites sender npub as message id and counts normal system notifications as urgent
description:
# Gap (TanFern session 2026-08-21, flywheel x toron collab; flywheel-side of bd-4bg0)

The orchestrator mail-wake banner repeatedly fired '1 urgent (last: 9150144f2e8c… re: )' across 5+ turns. 9150144f… is the SENDER npub of an automated reservation-release notification (importance=normal, empty subject, no thread) — no message with that id exists in any project inbox (toron/flywheel/demo checked). Urgent count stayed 1 while live inboxes held 0 urgent messages.

## Consequence
Crews dispatch on phantom urgent mail; the id in the banner cannot be used for reply/ack (reply-by-id fails); urgent channel loses signal value.

## Work
Wake renderer must (a) print the actual message id, not sender, (b) count only unread importance=urgent (or high) messages, (c) exclude system/transport notifications (reservation releases, read receipts) from the urgent tally. Regression test on the wake formatter.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1
```
close_reason:
SHA: flywheel 7c4e507 (fix(wake): banner cites message id; transport noise never urgent; bead id in message).
CRITERIA one-per-line:
1. Wake renderer prints the actual message id, not sender — digest_prefix renders "(id <last_id> re: <subject>)"; urgent_wake_prompt appends "Most recent urgent: id <id> re: <subject>"; sender npub no longer appears in either banner. Regression test kryk_wake_banner_cites_message_id_not_sender + updated plan_actions assertions green.
2. Urgent counts only unread importance=high|urgent — wake_urgent read-state filter (bd-dbre, already on this tree) verified present; read high rows never counted.
3. System/transport notifications excluded from the tally — wake_urgent drops empty-subject "reservation ... released" rows BEFORE the importance check, so mis-tagged importance=high transport chatter cannot manufacture a phantom urgent. Tests: kryk_wake_urgent_excludes_reservation_release_noise (noise at high+normal, one real urgent survives), kryk_empty_subject_non_transport_still_wakes (real peer messages with empty subjects still wake).
FENCE: cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1 => 968 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored (390s).
LIVE EVIDENCE: the buggy banner fired twice during this very session ("3 urgent (last: 994d117d... re: )" while the inbox held zero unread urgents — the three were already-read request-release responses); post-fix behavior matches the regression tests.
DEVIATIONS: none functional. Note: last_from stays in the digest JSON payload for operator surfaces (only the loop banners changed consumers).
PRINCIPLES:
prove-it-works — the bug reproduced live in-session, then the regression tests pin the exact phantom shape
fix-root-causes — fixed the renderer contract (id not sender) and the tally source (shape-based transport exclusion), not a cosmetic string swap
minimize-reader-load — the banner now carries exactly the replyable handle, nothing else

title: ADR-0003 Phase 1: AM-Rust parity Nostr mailbox (v1)
description:
# Epic: ADR-0003 Phase 1 — AM-Rust parity Nostr mailbox (v1 ship target)

## Background
`toron` v0.1.0 was built on asupersync + mDNS/PSK/WS-QUIC hub (ADR-0001/0002). ADR-0003 (accepted 2026-08-04, rev 6) pivots to:
- **Protocol:** Nostr (signed events + NIP-17 DMs)
- **Runtime:** Tokio (captain override of asupersync)
- **Role:** mailbox with **100% behavioral parity** to `mcp_agent_mail_rust` (AM-Rust) — 38 MCP tools / 9 clusters, 25 resources, storage layout, safety invariants, pre-commit guard, CLI robot mode + metrics
- **Topology:** Decision 1A (InProcessBus default) + 2B (nostr-sdk/Tokio) + 3A (flywheel embeds toron in-process)

## Goals / why this serves the project
Agents coordinate through durable, signed, relay/bus-delivered mail instead of shared filesystem state or a single SQLite process. Nostr adds: (1) cryptographic identity, (2) real-time pub/sub, (3) federation opt-in, (4) metadata-hiding private mail (NIP-17/59). Local-first preserved via InProcessBus + Git + SQLite.

## Non-negotiable parity contract
- Behavioral parity = tool surface + resources + storage + invariants (NOT runtime parity — asupersync waived)
- Conformance scope = response schema + filter/importance/thread/date semantics + tokenizer (`porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, `prefix='2 3'`) — NOT exact Search-V3 ranking
- Fixtures re-derived first-party (AM-Rust is `LicenseRef-MIT-Rider` — no vendoring)
- Kind registry FROZEN (30010–30014, 30031, 30032, Buzz job 43001–43006, etc.) — renumber requires new ADR revision

## Phase 1 OUT of scope (Phase 2+)
- toron-workflow / @mention dispatch / job lifecycle automation
- NIP-29 channels
- Ephemeral presence + persona packs
- TUI (ratatui 16-screen)
- Blossom/NIP-96 federation for blobs
- NIP-46 remote signer (Phase 1.5 option)
- NIP-05/39 (Phase 3 / A9)

## Architecture (concrete)
Layers in `toron-core`: Nostr → Bus → Local Projection (SQLite+Git) → Mailbox Core → Backend trait.
`toron-mcp` = 38 tools MCP (stdio/HTTP). `toron-cli` = daemon + robot CLI.
flywheel embeds toron-core+toron-mcp; agent↔agent path has no orchestrator in the loop.

## Success = all Phase-1 verification checkboxes in ADR-0003 Implementation Plan §Verification
## Source of truth
docs/decisions/0003-nostr-mailbox-fabric.md (rev 6). Beads must be self-contained; this epic anchors the tree.

Verification evidence: workspace 339 tests green, check green, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean (fixed my lint nits + 2 oc-a test-module lints flagged first), fmt clean; rg asupersync/fastmcp = 0; forbid(unsafe_code) in all 5 crate roots; 38-tool MCP surface (43 #[tool] incl macros) + 25 resources (fixtures); conformance harness green (schema/filters/tokenizer porter unicode61 2 3); e2e-p1 CI gate in ci.yml; SC-1..8+14a/b green; single herdr client (agent_prompt defined once); local-first InProcessBus; kind registry frozen per ADR. title: Bus: InProcessBus + pipeline (RelayBus optional/federation)
description:
# Workstream: Bus trait — InProcessBus + RelayBus

## Decision 1A
Default = InProcessBus (Tokio broadcast + SQLite event store). RelayBus for standalone daemon / federation. Events are **wire-identical** — serialize any InProcessBus event and a real relay accepts it unchanged.

## Critical framing
- InProcessBus is NOT a NIP-01-interoperable relay (no external client can REQ it)
- It has relay-identical **event semantics** + same validation pipeline
- RelayBus speaks full NIP-01 frames (EVENT/REQ/OK/EOSE)

## Buzz relay pipeline (adopt exactly)
verify → auth → dedup-insert (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) → fan-out (global subs excluded from channel/project-scoped events) → search-index (bounded worker) → audit (async) → workflow-trigger (async; excludes workflow/gift-wrap kinds). Client OK at pipeline end.

## Tagging (A3)
- InProcessBus: `["t", project-slug]` cheap filter
- Relay-crossing kinds ALSO carry NIP-32: `["L","toron"]` + `["l", project-slug, "toron"]` (dual-emit preferred)
- Gift-wrapped DMs (14/15/ack) carry **NEITHER** #t nor NIP-32 (metadata-hiding)

## Federation (Phase 1 policy NEW-D3)
- Default relay list **empty** (opt-in; zero egress)
- Only NIP-17 gift wraps may cross external relays in Phase 1
- Reservations/manifests/channels NOT federated until owned relay
- Public-relay hardening (never silent): NIP-42 AUTH + NIP-13 POW + allowlist (A4)

## TTL
Gift-wrap envelopes TTL 90 days (NIP-40 expiration, configurable). Git archive permanent.

## Ordering note (G7)
Bus envelope order = lex `(created_at, event_id)` for non-wrapped storage only. Mail timeline uses rumor timestamps after unwrap — separate projection concern.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## InProcessBus framing

Not a real NIP-01 relay. External clients cannot REQ it. Events are still wire-identical so RelayBus and federation do not need a second event type. Pipeline order matches Buzz: verify→auth→dedup→access-gated fanout→search→audit→workflow-trigger.

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05) — RELIABILITY (prevents silent data loss):

The "Tokio broadcast (or equivalent)" line needs a hard rule. `tokio::sync::broadcast` DROPS the oldest messages for laggy receivers (`Receiver::lagged`). That is unacceptable for the **projection subscriber** (bd-led.4.4), which must process EVERY event to keep SQLite + Git in sync — a dropped broadcast = a missing projected message = silent data loss.

Rule: the DURABLE subscribers (projection, archive) MUST use a lossless channel — per-subscriber `mpsc`, or a store-cursor + notify model backed by the SQLite event store (subscribe from a monotonic event-id cursor; notify-on-insert). `broadcast` is acceptable ONLY for loss-tolerant / ephemeral consumers (presence, debug streams).

Reconcile-on-lag (catch up from the event store by event-id cursor when a notification is missed) is the alternative if broadcast is kept for liveness. Don't ship the durable projection on a dropping channel.

title: Local projection: SQLite index + Git archive
description:
# Workstream: Local Projection — SQLite index + Git archive

## Role
Subscribe to bus, unwrap gift-wrapped mail for local keys, write:
1. **SQLite index** (WAL, pool, write-behind, 30s deferred touch)
2. **Git archive** (AM-Rust layout)

## sqlx rules (G15)
- runtime-tokio, sqlite
- **Dedicated single write connection** + small read pool
- Write-behind cache serializes writes
- Never rusqlite under async without spawn_blocking (footgun)

## Git layout (per project)
- `messages/{YYYY}/{MM}/`
- `agents/{name}/{inbox,outbox}/`
- `file_reservations/`, `build_slots/`
- `.archive.lock`
- async commit coalescer
- `TORON_GIT_BINARY` override + libgit2 (G16)

## Ordering (G7) — CRITICAL
- Envelope order ≠ mail timeline
- Mail order = rumor `created_at` * 1e6 + optional `ts_ms` + local monotonic seq for ties
- Threads from NIP-10 `e` tags

## Contact policy (G14)
Bus is dumb. Projection drops wraps that violate recipient policy before index/Git.

## Audit separation (G13)
Bus = current replaceable state; Git = full transition history for reservations/slots.

## Attachments (G4)
Content-addressed `blobs/sha256/<hash>`; kind-15 with `x`+file-type; small text inline.

## DR (G11)
- Git lost → rebuild from bus (negentropy default, full replay fallback)
- SQLite lost → rebuild from Git unwrapped content

title: Unwrap + G7 rumor ordering + G14 contact-policy drop
description:
# Task: Unwrap pipeline + mail timeline ordering (G7) + policy drop (G14)

## What
1. Subscribe bus → for each kind-1059, try unwrap with local agent keys
2. Re-sort mail by rumor timestamp (+ts_ms) + local_seq — NEVER envelope created_at
3. Enforce contact policies (open|auto|contacts_only|block_all) before index write
4. Cache acks per (acker-npub, message-id)

## Why
NIP-17 deliberately randomizes wrap timestamps. Wrong order = broken threads vs AM-Rust.

## Tests
- Two wraps with inverted envelope times still order by rumor time
- block_all drops before Git write (assert no file)
close_reason: Projection pipeline landed: index/projection.rs (pure functional core). G7 ordering: rumor_timestamp_us (rumor created_at*1e6 + ts_ms tag; envelope NEVER consulted), sort_by_timeline (created_ts_us, local_seq) with inverted-envelope test; G14: ContactPolicy parse + policy_allows + decide (block_all drops before write, contacts_only requires approval) + block_all-no-file test; to/cc role extraction from p tags (G3); AckCache idempotency (G8). 7 tests green. Workspace: check green, 222 tests pass, clippy clean on lane files.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## G7 ordering landmine

NIP-17 randomizes gift-wrap created_at (up to 2 days back). If fetch_inbox sorts by envelope time, threads will look randomly shuffled. Always unwrap first, then sort by rumor created_at (+ts_ms) + local_seq.

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05) — IDEMPOTENCY:

Make message projection idempotent on (recipient-npub, rumor-id) and on event-id. A re-delivered kind-1059 (bus redelivery, federation replay, or the same wrap arriving twice via different paths) MUST NOT produce a duplicate SQLite row or a duplicate Git commit. The unwrap step should be a no-op if (recipient, rumor-id) is already projected.

Acks are already cached per (acker-npub, message-id) — extend the same idempotency discipline to message projection and to reservation/slot transitions (a replayed acquire = same lease, no duplicate audit record). Add an explicit idempotency assertion to the acceptance (send twice → one projected message, one Git commit).

title: Messaging tools: send/reply/inbox/ack with BCC privacy (G3/G8)
description:
# Task: Messaging cluster (5 tools) — G3 G7 G8 + NIP-17

## Tools (exact names from catalog)
send_message, reply_message, fetch_inbox, acknowledge_message, mark_message_read

## Wire mapping (G3) — CRITICAL
- **to+cc:** visible rumor `p` tags with role `"to"|"cc"`; gift-wrap one copy each
- **bcc:** variant rumor listing to+cc+that_bcc only (true BCC; bcc cannot see other bccs)
- subject → NIP-14 `subject`; importance, ack_required, sender_token → tags on rumor
- thread reply → NIP-10 `["e", root, relay, "reply"]`
- Unknown recipient **aborts whole send** (no partial delivery)

## Acks / reads (G8)
- NOT public replaceable events
- NIP-17 gift-wrapped kind-14 to original sender only
- tags: `toron-kind` = `ack`|`read` + NIP-10 `e` referencing original (no `d` on kind 14)
- `acknowledge_message` **idempotent** (second call returns stored ts)

## Ordering
fetch_inbox uses projection mail timeline (rumor time), never envelope time (G7)

## Acceptance tests (must all pass, detailed logs)
1. N recipients → N kind-1059 wraps; each unwraps to same kind-14 rumor content
2. BCC recipient unwrap lists to+cc+self, **not** other bccs
3. Non-recipient cannot unwrap any wrap
4. Ack only visible to original sender's projection
5. Idempotent ack returns same timestamp
6. Real-time: subscribed local agent receives via bus push (no poll) — integration with bus
7. `to=["Unknown"]` fails fast pre-wrap

## Why better than AM-Rust
E2E gift-wrap + true BCC + private acks (parity superiority table).
close_reason: Messaging cluster done: send_message/reply_message (G3 to/cc visible rumor + per-bcc variant, true BCC, NIP-14 subject, NIP-10 e reply, fail-fast unknown pre-wrap no partial), fetch_inbox (projection rumor-time order G7, never envelope), acknowledge/mark_read (private NIP-17 to sender, toron-kind+e tag, idempotent). 6 tests incl. BCC privacy matrix + no-partial-delivery. Workspace green 228 tests check/clippy/fmt.

title: File reservations + force-release revocation (G5 A1)
description:
# Task: File reservation cluster (5 tools) + force-release G5 A1

## Tools
file_reservation_paths (acquire), renew, release, conflicts, force_release_file_reservation
(Exact names from catalog `bd-0qg`.)

## Wire
- kind-30031 addressable; `d`=`project:path-glob`; NIP-40 expiration=TTL
- Conflict detection: local **symmetric** fnmatch both ways (`src/**` ↔ `src/lib.rs`)

## Force-release (G5 A1) — DO NOT USE CROSS-KEY NIP-09
NIP-09 is author-only. Operator kind-5 cannot delete agent reservation.
NIP-33 addressable dedup is per `(kind,pubkey,d)` — operator cannot supersede agent event on relay.

### Normative mechanism
1. Validate staleness heuristic (agent inactive beyond threshold — same as AM-Rust)
2. Operator signs kind-30031 with `status:revoked` + `e`/`a` → target lease
3. **Projection key-priority: operator > agent** for given `(kind,d)` — all nodes identical
4. NIP-09 only optional cleanup hint / agent own-deletes
5. Notify previous holder via NIP-17 with heuristic summary
6. Git audit transition record (G13 history)

## Acceptance tests
1. Symmetric conflict both directions
2. TTL expiry clears active lease
3. Force-release: projection shows revoked **with both agent lease + operator revoke events present**
4. No dependence on NIP-09 delete succeeding
5. Previous holder receives NIP-17 notify
6. Git has acquired→revoked transition history
7. broadcast=true / wrong-surface denied at tool layer (cross-check invariants bead)

## Depends on
Projection unwrap, addressable priority (`bd-toh`), operator keys, dual-emit tags.
close_reason: Reservations cluster done: file_reservation_paths (kind-30031 d=project:glob, NIP-40 TTL, dual-emit), renew (supersede), release (status:released), check_file_reservation_conflicts (symmetric fnmatch both ways), force_release (G5 A1: staleness heuristic → operator status:revoked + e/a, projection key-priority operator>agent via resolve_coordinate, NIP-17 notify, Git audit transition, NO cross-key NIP-09). 7 tests: symmetric both dirs, TTL expiry, full force-release path (revoke+notify+audit), own-never-blocks, renew/release. Workspace 240 core tests, clippy/fmt clean.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## P1 protocol landmine (rev6 A1)

If you implement force_release via operator kind-5 delete or operator kind-30031 with same d expecting relay supersession, you are WRONG on any NIP-01/09/33 compliant relay.

Correctness is entirely in toron projection key-priority rule. Write that rule once, test it with two events present simultaneously (agent lease + operator revoke), assert revoke wins regardless of created_at ordering tricks.

title: MCP server skeleton: rmcp stdio + Streamable HTTP/axum (spec 2026-07-28)
description:
# Task: toron-mcp server skeleton (rmcp, spec 2026-07-28)

## What
Build the MCP server on **rmcp** (NOT fastmcp-rust — asupersync conflict). Two transports from one `ServerHandler` impl:

1. **stdio** (feature `transport-io`) — for `toron serve --mcp-stdio` and as a child-process server agents spawn.
2. **Streamable HTTP** (feature `transport-streamable-http-server`) — `StreamableHttpService` is a Tower service; mount it on toron's axum router at `/mcp`. This is the current spec transport; legacy 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE is a deliberate rmcp non-goal (do NOT build it). Enable **SEP-2567 stateless mode** for the daemon/federation path (horizontally scalable, no session affinity).

## ServerHandler
- `get_info()`: `ServerCapabilities::builder().enable_tools().enable_resources().enable_resources_subscribe().enable_tool_list_changed().enable_logging().build()`; server name `toron`, version from Cargo.
- Protocol negotiation: prefer `ProtocolVersion::V_2026_07_28`; rmcp auto-falls-back to `V_2025_11_25`.
- Lifecycle: `serve()` (legacy initialize) for stdio; `serve_with_lifecycle(Discover)` for HTTP clients that prefer it.

## Foundation for 7.2 / 7.3
- ServerHandler holds an `Arc<Mailbox>` (toron-core). 7.2 adds `#[tool]` methods; 7.3 adds `#[resource]` + subscriptions.
- Macros (`#[tool_router]`, `#[tool_handler]`) auto-wire capability flags.

## Acceptance
- `toron serve --mcp-stdio` answers `initialize`/`list_tools` (empty) over stdio.
- `toron serve --mcp-http 127.0.0.1:8000` mounts `StreamableHttpService` on axum; an rmcp client (`transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest`) completes `initialize`.
- Negotiated protocol reports `2026-07-28` against a current client.
- No fastmcp / asupersync in the server path.
close_reason: toron-mcp skeleton on rmcp 3.1.1: ServerHandler (get_info: tools/resources/resources-subscribe/tool-list-changed/logging), stdio serve (transport-io) + StreamableHttpService mounted at /mcp on axum (SEP-2567 stateless; json_response). CLI toron serve --mcp-stdio/--mcp-http. Acceptance proven: live binary smoke negotiate 2026-07-28 over both transports, tools/list empty, exit 0; acceptance.rs tests 2/2; workspace check/test/clippy(-D warnings)/fmt all green; rg fastmcp/asupersync empty. Features: transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest added for tests.

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05) — MATERIAL DEPENDENCY FIX:

`fastmcp-rust` (Dicklesworthstone/fastmcp_rust — the crate currently named in bd-led.1.2 + ADR-0003 §Dependencies) is built on `asupersync`. That is the exact runtime ADR-0003 DROPS (captain Tokio override), and whose removal is a hard CI gate (`rg asupersync` zero hits across toron + flywheel). Pulling fastmcp-rust into toron re-introduces asupersync transitively and mixes two async runtimes in one process (tokio + asupersync) — a known footgun, and a direct violation of the ADR's runtime-waiver intent.

USE THE OFFICIAL `rmcp` CRATE instead — `modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk`, Tokio-native, ships `#[tool]`/`#[resource]`/`#[prompt]` macros via `rmcp-macros`. Matches the mandate; sufficient for 38 tools + 25 resources. Fallback if rmcp proves too minimal for the surface: hand-roll MCP JSON-RPC over stdio/axum (the protocol is simple) — still preferable to fastmcp-rust's runtime conflict.

Action for this bead: build the stdio + HTTP/axum MCP skeleton on `rmcp`. Action for bd-led.1.2: declare `rmcp` + `rmcp-macros`, drop `fastmcp-rust 0.3.x`. ADR-0003 §Dependencies + §Migration need a corrigendum (fastmcp-rust → rmcp) — flagged to captain; not silently editing the accepted/frozen ADR here.

title: Wire 38 tools 1:1 AM-Rust names/args/returns
description:
# Task: Wire 38 AM-Rust tools on rmcp (macros + schemars; spec 2026-07-28)

## Approach — macro-driven, schema-by-derive (the efficiency win)
Use rmcp `#[tool]` + `#[tool_router]` (or `#[tool_router(server_handler)]`) on the Mailbox impl. Each of the 38 tools = one method whose params struct and return struct derive `serde::{Serialize,Deserialize}` + `schemars::JsonSchema`. rmcp auto-generates `inputSchema` + `outputSchema` (JSON Schema 2020-12) — **NO hand-rolled schemas**.

## Conformance source = the derived schemas
The schemars-derived inputSchema/outputSchema ARE the golden fixture for the 38-tool schema conformance (bd-77u.1). Snapshot them at compile time (from the rmcp-reported `list_tools` output); no need to run each tool to record its shape. AM-Rust arg names / return shapes map 1:1 to the derive field names/types — **parity-by-construction**.

## Structured outputs (SEP-2106)
Return structs carry `outputSchema` + populated `structuredContent`. outputSchema may be any JSON type. Tools that today return JSON blobs (search results, thread summaries, inbox lists) get typed return structs.

## Tool annotations (2026-07-28)
Annotate for host gating (annotations are untrusted per spec but useful): `destructive=true` for `force_release_file_reservation`, `file_reservation_paths(exclusive)`, `acquire_build_slot(exclusive)`, `install_precommit_guard`; `read-only` for `health_check`, `list_agents`, `whois`, `fetch_inbox`, `search_messages`, `check_file_reservation_conflicts`, `summarize_thread`. Maps to AM-Rust safety + ADR confirmation tiers.

## Standardized headers (SEP-2243)
Optionally annotate top-level tool args (e.g. `project`, `agent_name`) with `x-mcp-header` so stateless HTTP routers can route by header.

## Names (1:1 AM-Rust)
Exact names from catalog bd-0qg: `send_message`, `fetch_inbox`, `file_reservation_paths`, `acquire_build_slot`, … (all 38).

## Acceptance
- 38 `#[tool]` methods; `list_tools` returns 38 with correct names.
- Each tool's `inputSchema` matches the AM-Rust golden schema (derive parity).
- Destructive tools annotated; a sample client sees the annotations.
close_reason: All 38 AM-Rust tools wired 1:1 in crates/toron-mcp/src/tools.rs via rmcp #[tool] macros + #[tool_handler(router=...)] on ToolServer (wraps Arc<Mailbox>). Exact names/args from bd-0qg catalog; schemars-derived inputSchema (parity-by-construction); annotations (destructive: force_release_file_reservation, file_reservation_paths, acquire_build_slot, install_precommit_guard; read-only: health_check, list_agents, whois, fetch_inbox, search_messages, check_file_reservation_conflicts, summarize_thread). Acceptance proven: http_lists_exactly_38_am_rust_tools test (list_tools==38 exact names over real HTTP via rmcp client), 12 toron-mcp tests green, workspace check/test/clippy(-D warnings)/fmt all green.

title: Expose 25 MCP resources Phase 1
description:
# Task: Expose 25 MCP resources + subscriptions (rmcp; spec 2026-07-28)

## Resources via `#[resource]` + templates
Implement `list_resources` / `read_resource` / `list_resource_templates` on the ServerHandler. Map AM-Rust's 25 resources, many via URI templates:
- `toron://projects/{slug}` — project manifest
- `toron://agents/{name}/profile` — kind-30013 profile
- `toron://agents/{name}/inbox` — unwrapped mail projection
- `toron://threads/{id}` — thread DAG
- `toron://reservations/{id}` / `toron://slots/{slot}`
- `toron://products/{key}`

`read_resource` queries the SQLite index (bd-led.4) — same data `fetch_inbox`/`search` use.

## Subscriptions/listen (SEP-2575) — THE real-time push mechanism
Protocol 2026-07-28 replaces `resources/subscribe` + the HTTP GET stream with the transport-neutral, long-lived `subscriptions/listen`. Implement:
- `accepted_subscription_filter(requested)` → accept the resource/notification categories toron serves.
- `listen(SubscriptionContext)`: wire the **InProcessBus → `context.sink()`**. On bus events (new mail for agent X, reservation acquired/released, agent profile changed), emit notifications to subscribed clients. This is how "**<50ms push, no polling**" (ADR parity-superiority row) is delivered at the MCP boundary — agents subscribe to their inbox resource and get pushed on arrival instead of polling `fetch_inbox`.
- `enable_resources_subscribe()` + `enable_tool_list_changed()` in `get_info()`; `notify_tool_list_changed()` when agents register/deregister.

## Acceptance
- 25 resources list/read correctly; templates expand.
- An rmcp client subscribes to `toron://agents/{name}/inbox`; a `send_message` to that agent pushes a notification <50ms (bus → sink), no polling.
- `tool_list_changed` fires on `register_agent`.
close_reason: toron-mcp resources + subscriptions/listen (SEP-2575): list_resources/read_resource/list_resource_templates on ToronServer, 25 parity resources (toron:// scheme, catalog-derived), static reads + template expansion + unknown-reject; accepted_subscription_filter + listen wiring bus→sink (resource-updated notifications); ToronServer holds Arc<dyn Bus>. Acceptance: 10 toron-mcp tests green incl http_resources_list_and_read (25 listed, templates, env read, unknown rejected) over real HTTP; workspace check/test/clippy(-D warnings)/fmt all green. Data-backed inbox reads marked bd-led.4/5 dependent (placeholder).

description:

`loop run --work` drives polls indefinitely (parity with resumed runs);
add a regression test that starts a fresh loop invocation and asserts
N consecutive polls complete within a time bound (no park).
