title: Stale __doorbell watchers run pre-fix wake code unsupervised — false MAIL WAKEs loop forever
description:
# Defect (observed live 2026-08-21/22, TanFern session)

`__doorbell --project toron --workspace flywheel-toron` PID 8275 started 16:31 Aug 21 — six hours BEFORE bd-dbre a4302c3 landed (22:39). It ran pre-fix wake code all night and injected ~12 false MAIL WAKE banners for a request-release that was answered (release_decision=agreed, delivered), acked (acknowledged:true), and read (read_ts_us set in BOTH MCP and CLI views). Compounding causes:

1. Watchers are long-lived and outlive the fixes they serve — no restart on binary change, no generation stamp in injected banners.
2. They are UNSUPERVISED orphans (PPID 1 launchd): killing the PID silences pane-watch events for the whole workspace; nothing respawns it. Operators face stale-spam vs no-events.
3. Banner text carries no watcher-generation info, so agents cannot tell stale-watcher noise from a live peer need (a crew burned 6+ no-op turns).

## Work
Supervise doorbells (spawn from loop/serve so they die with the session) or add heartbeat+generation: banner carries watcher start-time and binary mtime/hash; a watcher older than its own binary's wake-logic change refuses to inject wakes (self-retires, logs once). Document the sanctioned restart command for operators.

Acceptance: a doorbell started before a wake-logic commit cannot inject wakes contradicting the new logic; banner lets an agent distinguish stale from live.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1
```
notes: Fresh repro 2026-08-21 SandySparrow: 13+ consecutive MAIL WAKEs citing answered request-release c43357a1/9844e931 against 0-unread inbox; daemon rejects the cited thread id as never-registered ('no request-release message with id 9844e931 addressed to SandySparrow'). Wake emission survives full read+ack+respond+empty-box. Id-vocabulary half tracked separately in flywheel ledger bd-wake-id-contract-1jz1.
close_reason: done

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
Fixed in flywheel 0d2b141 + 233a713 + 0d711fe (CrimsonIsland).

Mechanism (generation, not supervision): WatcherGen {started_unix, binary_mtime_unix, binary_len} stamped at spawn into <state>/doorbell/<ws>.gen. (1) Self-retire: the 1s tick compares on-disk exe identity to the record; mismatch = pre-fix wake logic => refuses ALL wakes, logs once, exits; missing/unreadable binary fails closed. (2) Supersede-on-spawn: LockAction::Superseded - ensure_running never attaches to a live watcher whose gen mismatches; it kills + replaces it. This retires PID-8275-class orphans (they cannot self-retire; the retire code does not exist in their binary). Sanctioned restart: rebuild then re-run workspace spawn - supersede is automatic. (3) Banner stamp: every injected wake ends with [doorbell watcher up=.. bin_mtime=..]; __doorbell --report prints the same fields => agents distinguish stale noise from live need.

Evidence: cargo test -p flywheel --bin flywheel -- --test-threads=1 => 993 passed / 0 failed on final tree. Live-fire: real watcher from built binary on isolated probe project; touch of binary produced "flywheel doorbell: binary changed since watcher start (up=1787348763, bin_mtime=1787348762); retiring without further wakes" within one tick, process exited, zero wakes injected. Unit witnesses: changed-binary / mtime-only / missing-binary refuse inject; banner stamp fields; report carries gen; supersede for no-gen and mismatched-gen live pids; stop clears gen.

Scope: bd-vbf2 lives in durable.rs, not files in hand - not taken. gtqe/preflight untouched (PinkCastle). crew.rs/pane.rs/schema.rs/playbook_lint.rs/mail_shim.rs/preflight.rs untouched. Commits carried guard-override bd-guard-crossproject-lease-er38 per ops brief.

title: Captain-free steering: compose existing workflows (goal/beads/crew) to dispatch crews at a target — bead-tracked OR direct
description:
# Captain-free steering: compose existing workflows to dispatch crews at a target

# The vision (captain, 2026-08-11)
The captain is SMART + FREE: state a TARGET, and the orchestrator COMPOSES the existing
workflows to steer/dispatch the crews to completion — be it bead-tracked or not. NOT manual
per-bead driving. This session exposed that the machinery (loop + crew execution) was too
unreliable to support this pattern, forcing manual fallback; this bead makes the pattern
first-class + reliable.

# The pattern (one compose call, not 20 dispatches)
- Captain: `flywheel workflow run goal --execute --inputs '{"objective": "<target>"}' --crew auto`
  (or a `flywheel steer <target>` surface).
- `goal` COMPOSES the existing workflows: brainstorm (diverge) -> plan (decompose) ->
  beads (create+track tasks AS BEADS) OR direct-dispatch (non-bead targets) -> crew:auto
  (infer fleet from profile refs) -> the loop drives via the beads-workflow lifecycle ->
  review -> ship -> runs view.
- The captain MONITORS (runs view) + intervenes ONLY on exceptions. The machinery does the
  work.

# Bead-tracked vs NOT
- Bead path: plan -> `br create` per task -> `crew:auto` + `loop --work` drive the crew through
  the beads-workflow (claim -> execute -> verify -> close -> sync).
- Direct path (no beads): plan -> dispatch the crew directly (spawn/dispatch_job steps) for
  targets that don't belong in the tracker (e.g. "refactor auth", "harden the loop").
  The `goal` workflow must support BOTH arms explicitly.

# Prerequisites (the machinery must be trustworthy first)
1. bd-efk1 (crew-execution contract) — dispatched agents actually claim + close.
2. bd-bvwf.1-5 (loop reliability) — no orphan workspaces / detection stalls / chain timing
   races / stray loops / unknown-agent stalls.
3. The live E2E suite (bd-e131) proves the loop + crew drive a chain to completion — the
   acceptance evidence for "the captain can compose + walk away."

# Deliverables
- A captain-facing `steer`/`goal` invoke that takes a target + crew strategy + either/both arms
  (bead-tracked, direct).
- The `goal` workflow's direct-dispatch arm (non-bead targets).
- A "captain monitor" flow: runs view + exception-only intervention (blocked/escalation), not
  per-bead poking.
- The E2E suite's "captain-steer" scenario: compose `goal` at a target -> the crew completes it
  (beads closed OR direct work done) WITHOUT manual per-bead dispatch.

# Verification gate
`flywheel steer "implement the auth refactor"` (or the goal invoke) drives the crew to
completion with ZERO manual per-bead dispatches: the crew claims + closes (bead path) OR
completes the direct work + reports (direct path). Runs view shows the full lifecycle. Repeat
with a bead-tracked + a non-bead target.

# Dependency
After bd-efk1 + bd-bvwf.1-5 + bd-e131 (the machinery must be trustworthy + provably so).
close_reason: SHIPPED + VERIFIED LIVE (commit flywheel 3fdc2de). ONE compose call at a target, zero manual per-bead dispatch: (1) `flywheel steer "<target>"` = bead-tracked arm (goal workflow: brainstorm -> plan -> beads -> build -> review -> ship) through the full workflow run --execute --mode pane machinery; (2) `steer --direct` = the direct arm (new builtins goal-direct + plan-direct: brainstorm -> plan WITHOUT the approval gate -> build -> review -> ship, no tracker); (3) crew:auto now RECURSES into call_workflow targets (plan_crew_with + cycle guard) so a composed workflow spawns the WHOLE fleet (goal -> oracle/planner/coder/reviewer/housekeeper) — the pre-recursion behavior failed 'no crew pane' on the first sub-workflow @oracle/@planner step; (4) workflow run injects the catalog+builtin WorkflowResolver (cron path parity, bd-8wvz) so call_workflow resolves. GATE: live steer --direct on a fresh project spawned the full 5-member fleet, brainstorm 3-oracle fan-out + planner + coder + reviewer + housekeeper ALL landed, run completed with no failure — zero manual intervention; bead-tracked arm verified through the same machinery (its remaining pane-mode constraint is the pre-existing goal reviewer harness:opencode override — documented P10.3, --crew squad or headless; NOT a steer regression). 520 tests pass (+2 crew recursion/cycle-guard +2 goal-direct/plan-direct pins); clippy clean in edited regions.

description:
# F2 — ADR-0003 Verification section stale (34/35 checkboxes unchecked at v1.0.0)

## Evidence of defect
`docs/decisions/0003-nostr-mailbox-fabric.md` Verification section: **34 `- [ ]` unchecked, 1 `- [x]`** — yet the ADR is ACCEPTED, v1.0.0 is tagged, all 103 beads closed, and CI gates green. The contract document looks unfinished despite the implementation being complete.

## Material because
The Verification section is the falsification surface — it is what a future auditor (or the adversarial-reviewer skill) checks against. Stale checkboxes understate the witness coverage and obscure which claims are actually proven vs aspirational. Two claims remain genuinely unproven (see F3, F4 below) — those should stay `[ ]` with explicit 'CI does not gate this yet' notes; the rest should tick with witness citations.

## Minimum acceptable fix
For each of the 34 unchecked bullets, EITHER:
- Tick `- [x]` + append witness citation (`SC-X green`, `crates/toron-core/src/X.rs:Y`, `cargo test -p toron-e2e --features p1`), OR
- Leave `- [ ]` + append `**NOT GATED IN CI** — reason` (honest about gaps).

Specifically the bullets for: Nostr correctness (V2), NIP-17 round-trip (V3), BCC (V4), real-time <50ms (V5), name resolution (V6), ncryptsec 0600 (V7), invariants (V8/9/10), force-release operator-priority (V11), proof gate (V12), backend (V13), ordering (V14), attachments (V15), local-first (V16), DR (V18), integrated mode (V19), no-asupersync (V20), single agent_prompt (V21), robot CLI (V22), relay pipeline (V23), job lifecycle (V24), @mention (V25), channels (V26), presence (V27), SSRF (V28), CLI clig.dev (V29), MCP↔CLI parity (V30), robot mode (V31), scenarios P1 (V32) — all have witnesses and should tick.

The Resonate-backed workflow SC-11 (V33) and federation `#[ignore]` (V17) bullets should stay `[ ]` with notes pointing at F3/F4.

## Do NOT broaden into
- Rewriting the ADR body.
- Adding new verification bullets.

Narrow doc fix. Inline citations only.

title: Addressable replaceable store + projection operator>agent priority
description:
# Task: Addressable/replaceable event semantics (NIP-33) + projection key-priority

## Background
Kinds 30010–30014, 30031, 30032 are parameterized-replaceable. Relay/bus dedup key is `(kind, pubkey, d)`. **Projection** applies an additional rule for toron semantics: for a given `(kind, d)`, latest-wins with **key-priority operator > agent** (A1 force-release).

## What
1. Bus store: ON CONFLICT for addressable keys by author isolation (NIP-33)
2. Projection resolver: merge agent lease + operator revoke with operator priority
3. Document difference: raw relay observers see both events; toron tools see resolved state
4. Unit tests with same `d`, different pubkeys, revoke wins in projection only

## Why
Without this, force-release and profile updates are wrong on federated or multi-writer views.

## Placement
Implement in bus store + projection layer; referenced by reservation/slot/profile tools.
close_reason: bus/addressable.rs: NIP-33 addressable semantics — is_addressable (30000-39999), AddressableKey (kind,pubkey,d), is_revocation (content plain/JSON + status tag), KeyPriority (operator>agent A1), resolve_coordinate (latest-wins within priority class, operator revoke beats newer agent lease). BusEventStore.insert_addressable = author-isolated supersede (same author same (kind,d) replaces; different author survives for projection). 10 tests: kind range, key extraction, latest-wins same/diff authors, operator revoke wins (A1), no-operator = raw view, revocation detection, store supersede + projection resolve. cargo test -p toron-core --lib 142/142 green; clippy+fmt clean

title: perf(unwrap): p-tag-directed gift-wrap unwrap (O(1) key select, lazy decrypt)
description:
Evidence: `crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/unwrap.rs:795` `try_unwrap` linearly scans
ALL keyring keys per gift-wrap; `build_unwrap_pipeline` (mod.rs:362) eagerly
decrypts EVERY `key.ncryptsec` under the data dir at serve boot
(N x scrypt, ~0.2s/key release at log_n 16 — measured 2026-08-17: 489-key dir
burned 35-200s; ~117 keys remain post-quarantine so serve boot still pays
~15-25s once).

Change:
- A NIP-59 gift wrap names its recipient: the `p` tag carries the recipient
  npub. `project()` reads the wrap's p-tag, resolves npub -> agent key file
  (the agents table already maps pubkey -> project/name; key path derives
  `{data}/{project}/agents/{name}/key.ncryptsec`), decrypts ONLY that key
  via `cached_load_agent_key`, and attempts a single unwrap.
- Fallback: when the p-tag key is absent or the unwrap fails, scan only the
  ALREADY-DECRYPTED cached keys — never trigger an eager bulk decrypt.
- `build_unwrap_pipeline`'s eager keyring build is deleted (laziness-protocol):
  the pipeline resolves keys per-wrap through the cache.

Acceptance criteria:
- With 20 registered agent keys and one inbound wrap, exactly ONE key is
  decrypted (assert via `kdf_load_count()` delta == 1, not wall-clock).
- Serve cold boot with 100+ key files on disk performs 0 KDF loads until the
  first wrap arrives (extend the 2026-08-17 one_shot test class).
- A wrap whose p-tag names an unknown npub falls back correctly (existing
  NotForUs semantics preserved).
- am_parity_e2e + existing unwrap tests green.

PRINCIPLES
prove-it-works — the O(1) bound is asserted via kdf_load_count differential, not timing
laziness-protocol — the eager keyring build is deleted, not cached harder

## VERIFY
```bash
cargo test -p toron-core unwrap && cargo test -p toron-mcp --test am_parity_e2e
```
close_reason: Landed in 0ad5056. Acceptance met: (1) ptag_directed_unwrap_decrypts_only_the_recipient_key green — kdf delta 1 per registered recipient, build delta 0 (red on the eager design at the same assertion); (2) lazy builds KDF-free incl. serve cold boot (cost-model test rewritten to the lazy contract: builds 0, fallback scan bounded by key-file count, repeat recipient cache-hit); (3) unregistered on-disk keys still unwrap via DB-miss fallback (pre-lazy contract preserved); (4) VERIFY green: cargo test -p toron-core unwrap 32/0, am_parity_e2e 8/0 on a live daemon. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — kdf_load_count differential asserts the O(1) bound; laziness-protocol — eager keyring build deleted, not cached harder.

title: MAIL WAKE banner names wrong 'most recent' urgent message — picked oldest of three urgent rows
description:
OBSERVED (2026-08-22 session, TealDune): MAIL WAKE said 'Most recent urgent: id bc27c6a70fc8...' (created_ts_us 1787300794), but the inbox held two NEWER urgent messages at fetch time: d46880a2b0ef... (1787302173, same thread c43357a1...) and TanFern's ccd46cbb7dc9... (1787304318, DIFFERENT thread 344e63b7...). The wake selected the OLDEST of three urgent messages.

IMPACT: harmless when the wrong pick shares the thread, but cross-thread it misdirects the mandated reply flow ('reply to the most recent urgent') at the wrong conversation — exactly what happened-risk here since ccd46cbb was on an unrelated request-release thread.

SUSPECT: wake snapshot ordering — ascending created_ts sort, stale snapshot timestamp, or ordering by read/ack state instead of created_ts_us. Expected rule: max(created_ts_us) among urgent rows needing attention.

VERIFY fence: seed inbox with 3 ack-required/high messages of differing created_ts across 2 threads; trigger wake; banner MUST cite max(created_ts_us) id.

RELATED: bd-stale-doorbell-wake-0fic (false wakes from stale watchers — same wake path family, different defect), bd-kryk (banner formatter cited sender npub instead of message id), bd-dbre (once-only wake semantics).
close_reason: done

comments.author: CrimsonIsland
comments.text:
Fixed in flywheel ab98a5c (main.rs, both digest builders).

Root cause: cmd_internal_mail_digest and digest_for both did urgent_rows.first() — wake_urgent preserves wire order, and the inbox projection delivered rows oldest-first, so the "Most recent urgent" id cited the OLDEST of N urgent rows; subject/thread fields came from arr.first() independently, so banner id/subject/thread could disagree across threads.

title: perf(bus): verify-once at the trust boundary (drop double schnorr on bus-delivered wraps)
description:
Evidence: every published event is schnorr-verified at the bus boundary
(`crates/toron-core/src/bus/in_process.rs:347` via `verify_publish_event`),
then `UnwrapPipeline::project` re-verifies the SAME event again
(`mailbox/unwrap.rs:812`, added by bd-p3-schnorr-verify-every-ingest-q0wo to
defend DIRECT callers). For bus-delivered wraps on the serve path this is
2x schnorr verify + 2x canonical serialization per event (~100us/event;
matters at replay bursts and projection catch-up).

Change: split the API at the trust boundary —
- `project()` keeps its verify for direct callers (contract unchanged).
- The bus-driven unwrap loop calls a `project_verified()` path that SKIPS the
  re-verify for events the bus already verified at publish ingress.
- The relay replay path (`relay_bus.rs:201`) verifies once at ingress; the
  loop consumes the same verified marker — exactly one verify per event
  end-to-end.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit: a bus-delivered wrap is verified exactly once (count via a test-only
  hook or split-fn coverage); a direct `project()` call with an invalid
  signature is still rejected (adversarial test stays green).
- No event reaches projection without exactly one verification (grep-level
  gate: the loop path cannot reach the sink without the ingress verify).

PRINCIPLES
boundary-discipline — the bus is the trust boundary; verify at ingress, trust inside
laziness-protocol — no redundant re-verification layer stacked on the boundary check

## VERIFY

cargo test -p toron-core verify
```

title: SC-2 E2E: direct mail + thread + ack (push <50ms)
description:
# SC-2 — Direct mail + thread + ack [P1]

## Actors
Pi-α, OC-β

## Steps + assertions (three DISTINCT things — keep them separate)

1. **Parity poll** — Pi-α `mail send --to OCβ --subject review --body … --ack`; then OC-β
   `mail inbox --unread` RETURNS the message (this is a **poll** — AM-Rust parity).
   thread_id = root event id (NIP-10 `e`). The message is queryable in OC-β's projection
   <50ms after send (projection write latency).

2. **Bus push** — a bus/projection subscriber (NOT an MCP client) receives the kind-1059 /
   kind-14 event <50ms after publish; zero polling on the bus path. This is the
   InProcessBus notification (bd-led.3.2) — and per the bd-led.3.2 review note, the
   projection subscriber MUST be on a lossless channel, not a dropping `broadcast`.

3. **MCP subscription push** — validated in bd-led.7.3's OWN acceptance (an rmcp client
   subscribes to `toron://agents/OCβ/inbox`; `send_message` pushes a subscription
   notification <50ms via `subscriptions/listen`, SEP-2575). NOT asserted here — 7.3 owns it.

4. OC-β `mail ack <id>` → Pi-α sees the ack (private NIP-17 to sender, `toron-kind=ack`);
   idempotent on repeat (second ack returns stored ts).

## Assert
- 1 NIP-17 gift-wrap to OC-β; unwraps to a kind-14 rumor.
- Ack is a private NIP-17 to Pi-α (G8); thread_id = root event id.
- Parity-poll (1), bus-push (2), and ack round-trip all hold.
- MCP-subscription-push (3) is bd-led.7.3's contract, not this scenario's.

## Deps
bd-cvp (harness), bd-led.5.3 (messaging tools). Bus-push (2) transitive via
bd-led.3.2/4.4; MCP-sub push (3) via bd-led.7.3 (not a direct dep here).
close_reason: SC-2 landed: crates/toron-e2e/tests/sc2_direct_mail.rs (#[cfg(feature=p1)]). Parity poll: PiAlpha send_message(ack)→OCBeta fetch_inbox returns msg (subject/body/importance/ack flags); bus push: subscription receives kind-1059 wrap to OCBeta via p-tag <50ms zero-polling (skip EOSE); fresh send is thread root (thread_id None, NIP-10); ack idempotent (repeat returns stored ts, G8). 1 test green. Gate: cargo test -p toron-e2e --features p1 (17/17). Workspace: check green, 330 pass, clippy clean on lane files.

title: ADR-0019 Wave 1: bead verdict on br gate (fail-closed close)
description:
Part of ADR-0019 (read: docs/decisions/0019-bead-verified-execution-and-principle-playbooks.md in the toron repo — this bead embeds the AMENDED 2026-08-15 decisions: br-gate verdict store, loop-run VERIFY, ReviewerSigned, SHA invariant, wave resequencing).

## Background
`br close` today is a self-report: the flywheel durable loop treats a closed bead as done with zero proof, and the lifecycle protocol is a ~1.7KB prompt string (`flywheel/src/durable.rs` `bead_prompt`) the loop cannot parse. ADR-0019 wave 1 makes close FAIL-CLOSED on machine-checked proof. Pre-acceptance amendments (2026-08-15): verdict store is `br gate` (NOT a flywheel TSV), the loop itself executes VERIFY on the loop-runnable band, judgment beads close only on `ReviewerSigned`, and the SHA binding is commit-before-close.

## Scope (children of this epic)
1. w1-types — VerdictKind/BeadUnit/legal_close (pure, table-tested)
2. w1-gate-store — br gate round-trip + loop-only reporter guard + `flywheel ledger` CLI
3. w1-policy-spike — can br gate policy gate `closed` (prevention vs detection)
4. w1-reopen — loop reopen-on-unverified-close (the red-then-green)
5. w1-loop-run-verify — loop executes VERIFY on the cheap band
6. w1-sha — commit-before-close SHA invariant
7. w1-verify-fence — `## VERIFY` fence parsing, refuse-to-dispatch
8. w1-reserve-serialize — reservation floor, serialize-on-overlap, worktree preflight
9. w1-verifier-degrade — scaled verifier + single-family degrade
10. w1-brief — brief template, delete bead_prompt/resume_prompt

## Epic acceptance (= ADR-0019 §7 Wave 1 checkboxes, all green)
- Every kind x priority x blast x AC-shape cell of legal_close table-tested.
- Worker closes with no gate row -> loop reopens -> bead back in `br ready`.
- Cheap P3 loop-runnable VERIFY -> loop runs it, records command-verified, stays closed.
- P0 + worker-receipt only -> reopened until different-family reviewer records a legal kind.
- Judgment-AC bead closed with unit-test-verified -> reopened; only reviewer-signed closes.
- Close with no commit carrying the bead id -> illegal, reopened.
- Overlapping beads serialize or split; `.beads/**`/`Cargo.lock` beads never parallel; no `worktree.create` in loop logs; unexpected linked worktree fails preflight without `--allow-worktree`.
- Single-family swarm -> blocked `verifier-family-missing` + exactly one captain mail.
- `rg 'Execute bead \{id\}'` empty in flywheel/src; old prompt templates gone.

## Out of scope
Playbook builtins (wave 2), principles bake (wave 3), event-loop promotion (wave 4), read receipts, noun collapse, `reflect`.

title: W1: loop executes VERIFY itself on the cheap band (CommandVerified)
description:
Part of ADR-0019 (read: docs/decisions/0019-bead-verified-execution-and-principle-playbooks.md in the toron repo — this bead embeds the AMENDED 2026-08-15 decisions: br-gate verdict store, loop-run VERIFY, ReviewerSigned, SHA invariant, wave resequencing).

## Background
Anti-forgery amendment: on the loop-runnable band (priority>=2, blast Normal, single cheap command) the LOOP is the verifier — it runs VERIFY and writes the receipt itself. A lying worker cannot forge what it does not write, and no second model is spent. The worker still runs VERIFY as part of doing the work (red-green); only where the loop CANNOT run it (long-running, live-UI, agent-env) does the worker receipt count (with two-tick grace).

## Work (repo: ~/workspace/flywheel — loop-run VERIFY leaf)
- At close-detect on the cheap band: loop executes VERIFY now. Timeout = the bead's TIMEBOX. cargo commands under the build slot (acquire exclusive, release immediately after).
- Success: loop writes the receipt file (machine-written), records command-verified via br gate, leaves closed.
- Non-zero exit: reopen + spawn a fix unit; NEVER a re-verify of the same broken head.
- Loop must classify VERIFY loop-runnable: single command line, allowlisted executable prefix (cargo/test/pytest/bounded shell), estimated cheap. Anything else -> non-runnable band.

## Acceptance (fixtures)
- Cheap P3 loop-runnable VERIFY -> loop executes it, records command-verified -> stays closed.
- Forging is impossible BY CONSTRUCTION: workers never write this kind (guard test).
- VERIFY failing -> bead reopened + fix unit spawned; no re-run against the same head.

title: W1: loop reopen-on-unverified-close (red-then-green of the program)
description:
Part of ADR-0019 (read: docs/decisions/0019-bead-verified-execution-and-principle-playbooks.md in the toron repo — this bead embeds the AMENDED 2026-08-15 decisions: br-gate verdict store, loop-run VERIFY, ReviewerSigned, SHA invariant, wave resequencing).

## Background
The core enforcement: the loop knows the assigned set (claim-watch keys). Each tick it `br show --json` those ids (NOT a full br list scan, NOT a comment grep). For each id whose status became closed since last checkpoint it checks for a legal verdict; illegal/missing -> reopen + mail. A worker who closes without proof cannot drain the queue.

## Work (repo: ~/workspace/flywheel — src/durable.rs reopen leaf + main.rs loop hook)
- On close-detect: `ledger check` (w1-gate-store). Illegal or missing -> `br reopen <id>` + mail on `thread_id=<id>`, subject `[<id>] unverified close reopened`, one mail per (bead, sha).
- Idempotent reopen: already closed + missing row -> reopen; already open + missing row -> no-op.
- Reopen is convergent under replay (durable/crash-safe, checkpointed like other loop verdicts).
- Grace: a WorkerReceipt-eligible bead whose receipt is merely racing the close gets TWO consecutive missing ticks before reopen (close can race the receipt write).
- Legal -> leave closed, claim-watch releases.

## Acceptance (fixtures)
- Worker closes with no gate row -> loop reopens -> bead is in `br ready`. THIS IS THE RED-THEN-GREEN OF THE PROGRAM.
- Reopen storm guard: exactly one mail per (bead, sha) across repeated ticks.
- Crash between close-detect and reopen: next tick converges.

## VERIFY

cd ~/workspace/flywheel && cargo test -p flywheel reopen
```

title: W1: reservation floor, serialize-on-overlap, worktree preflight
description:
Part of ADR-0019 (read: docs/decisions/0019-bead-verified-execution-and-principle-playbooks.md in the toron repo — this bead embeds the AMENDED 2026-08-15 decisions: br-gate verdict store, loop-run VERIFY, ReviewerSigned, SHA invariant, wave resequencing).

## Background
ADR-0019 Spec 3 (amended): worktrees are FORBIDDEN in the loop — a second checkout duplicates the single-writer objects (.beads/, receipts, Cargo.lock, target/, docs/catalog/, agent-names.json) and buys a merge fight plus a second full agent context. Contention serializes or splits. Overlap waits are NOT stuck owners.

## Work (repo: ~/workspace/flywheel — durable.rs dispatch planning + preflight.rs)
- Every in-flight bead holds an exclusive reservation on its write paths, reason=<bead-id>, TTL renewed by the worker (existing toron surface; acquire-vs-held = HARD per ADR-0011, unchanged).
- Serialize-on-overlap: overlapping second bead stays ready, undispatched until release. New claim-watch wait reason `overlap`, distinct from agent `blocked` (no T0-T3 nudge for overlap waits).
- Split ONLY when a coalition already exists (ADR-0011 proposer). Loop --work never invents a split, never calls an LLM planner for it.
- Always-serialize paths (never split into parallel): .beads/**, .flywheel/**, Cargo.lock, workspace-root Cargo.toml, docs/catalog/**, target/** — cargo goes through the build slot.
- Loop never calls worktree create/open; playbook dispatch never does.
- Preflight on `loop run` / `workflow run --execute`: fail on an extra linked worktree unless `--allow-worktree` (operator-only, logged).

## Acceptance (fixtures)
- Two overlapping ready beads on a normal path -> split or second stays undispatched until release; loop logs contain NO worktree.create.
- Two beads both touching .beads/ or Cargo.lock -> serialized, never parallel.
- `loop run` in a workspace with an extra linked worktree exits non-zero without --allow-worktree.

title: W1: commit-before-close SHA invariant (git log --grep, no bare HEAD)
description:
Part of ADR-0019 (read: docs/decisions/0019-bead-verified-execution-and-principle-playbooks.md in the toron repo — this bead embeds the AMENDED 2026-08-15 decisions: br-gate verdict store, loop-run VERIFY, ReviewerSigned, SHA invariant, wave resequencing).

## Background
The verdict must bind to the work. In a shared tree, bare `git rev-parse HEAD` is the SAME sha for every bead closed between commits and may not contain the closed bead's work at all — the original ADR draft's fallback was an evidentiary hole. Amendment: workers commit before closing (commit messages carry the bead id — Spec 0), and the loop derives the sha.

## Work (repo: ~/workspace/flywheel)
- At close-detect: `sha = git log --all -1 --grep="<bead-id>" --format=%H` in the primary tree.
- No commit carries the id -> the close is ILLEGAL regardless of verdicts -> reopen (w1-reopen machinery) + mail names the missing commit.
- No `git rev-parse HEAD` fallback anywhere in the verdict path.
- Receipt filenames and gate note sha= use this derived sha.
- Brief (w1-brief) REPORT contract states: commit before close, bead id in the message.

## Acceptance (fixtures)
- Close with no commit carrying the bead id -> illegal, reopened.
- Close where HEAD moved past the bead's commit (sibling committed after) -> sha still resolves to the bead's own commit.
- Bare-HEAD derivation absent (grep test).

title: W1: Verdict types + pure legal_close matrix (flywheel/src/verdict.rs)
description:
Part of ADR-0019 (read: docs/decisions/0019-bead-verified-execution-and-principle-playbooks.md in the toron repo — this bead embeds the AMENDED 2026-08-15 decisions: br-gate verdict store, loop-run VERIFY, ReviewerSigned, SHA invariant, wave resequencing).

## Background
Wave 1's type spine. Everything else (gate store, reopen, loop-run VERIFY, verifier) hangs on these types. Pure, no IO, table-testable.

## Work (repo: ~/workspace/flywheel — new file src/verdict.rs)
```text
BeadUnit
  id: String; title: String; priority: u8 (0-4); verify: String (required)
  blast: Normal | High   # High if overlapping reserved paths OR AC is judgment
  owner: Option<AgentName>  # ADR-0018 canonical name
  head_sha: Option<String>  # commit whose message carries the bead id

VerdictKind
  CommandVerified     # the LOOP executed VERIFY and wrote the receipt itself
  UnitTestVerified    # independent verifier ran the command/test
  LiveVerified        # independent verifier exercised the live surface
  ReviewerSigned      # independent verifier signed a judgment-AC bead (no command exists)
  WorkerReceipt        # worker self-report; legal ONLY where the loop cannot run VERIFY
  VerifierBlocked
  VerifierFailed

Verdict
  kind, bead_id, sha, at (DateTime<Utc>), actor (AgentName), receipt_path (PathBuf), verify_cmd
```
`legal_close(verdict, bead) -> bool` — the legal-close table (ADR-0019 Spec 1, amended):
- priority>=2 + blast Normal + VERIFY loop-runnable -> CommandVerified (loop-run) ONLY
- priority>=2 + blast Normal + VERIFY not loop-runnable (long-running, live-UI, agent-env) -> WorkerReceipt (+ two-tick grace) or UnitTestVerified/LiveVerified
- priority<=1 or blast High -> UnitTestVerified/LiveVerified only
- AC judgment -> ReviewerSigned only (recording unit-test-verified for a judgment bead is a FALSE verdict)
- any -> never VerifierFailed / VerifierBlocked / missing
Illegal success paths must not compile: the pair (status=closed, verdict=none) and WorkerReceipt on a loop-runnable VERIFY.

## Acceptance
- Table test covers EVERY kind x priority(0..4) x blast x AC-shape cell.
- Exhaustive match on VerdictKind: new kind without a legal_close case does not compile.
- No IO in the module (pure). Unit tests in-file.

## VERIFY

cd ~/workspace/flywheel && cargo test -p flywheel verdict::
```

description:

## Work (repo: ~/workspace/flywheel — src/builtin_workflows.rs; stages if reused)
`bug-fix` (inputs: symptom, repro):
  repro @scout — run/write the repro; ACCEPTANCE = command exits non-zero (or shows the bug).

THE FORK IS THE LABEL: ResolvedRecipient stores name: name.clone() — the RAW caller string. The inbox projection/view keys on recipient name, so one delivery surfaces as two disjoint inboxes (slug view vs pin view) with per-recipient read_ts_us that can never meet. cargo test -p toron-core
```

title: flywheel: doorbell delivery dead all swarm — arm verb, spawn subscription, degraded status (F17)
description:
Repo: flywheel. Source: docs/learnings/2026-09-12-swarm-stack-friction.md F17. Refs the flywheel bead bd-ene2 (doorbell `start --host` arming verb). Hit live 2026-09-12 (entire swarm): `flywheel doorbell status` stayed `mode:standby, subscribers:0, hosted:[], watch:standby, sweep.last_age_s:null` for the whole run (daemon ~20h uptime, healthy HTTP). Nothing was ever hosted or subscribed: no `[doorbell]` rings, no inbox-digest wakes, no ack-SLA nudges, no sweep polls. Every wake-dependent path degraded to manual — BrightCoast's request-release sat unanswered (holder pane idle, no ring), WindyGlen's claim-then-idle stalls got no re-wake, and the crews' `[doorbell] presence rule` never executed. The session worked only via direct `flywheel send` pane writes + captain polling. Root causes: (a) the installed `~/.cargo/bin/flywheel` predates the `doorbell start --host /` arming verb (bd-ene2) — plain `doorbell start

` just adopts the daemon and exits, while the skill documents a flag the binary does not have (the documented binary-freshness trap, on a wake-critical verb). (b) spawn's documented "records a subscription row and defers to a healthy daemon" left subscribers at 0 across 4 spawned panes — the row never wrote, or bound to a dead run's workspace. (c) nothing surfaces "doorbell is in standby with 0 subscribers" at arrive/briefing time; the swarm started wake-blind with no gate. Fix: (1) a binary-freshness gate covering DOORBELL verbs — arrive fails loud/warns when the installed binary cannot arm the plane; (2) spawn verifies its subscription row landed (subscribers > 0) and warns loud; (3) `doorbell status` standby-with-active-workspaces is a visible degraded state, not a green JSON. Witness: after `flywheel arrive` + a spawn, `flywheel doorbell status --json` shows the workspace hosted with subscribers > 0; a stale binary fails arrive loud.

description:
# Task: Job lifecycle 43001–43006 Buzz-verbatim + claim semaphore (A7)

## What
- Implement kinds: request/accept/progress/result/cancel/error
- First-claimer wins (signed 43002)
- `dispatch_job`: bounded semaphore + one-in-flight-per-agent
- @mention parser queues 43001

## Tests
- Claim race: only one winner
- Burst @mentions do not thrash (semaphore)

close_reason: Job lifecycle done in toron-workflow: jobs.rs (builders 43001-43006 Buzz-verbatim with e=parent, wire-identical signed events, first_claimer first-observed-wins on InProcessBus total order, job_state terminal priority result/error/cancel over claim+progress), mention.rs (channel-agnostic @mention parser — mention marker + p tag on kind-14 OR kind-9, per beads-review), dispatch.rs (A7: bounded Semaphore + one-in-flight-per-agent + durable queued mirror, busy-agent jobs stay queued not dropped). 29 tests: claim race single-winner, burst no-thrash, queue durability, terminal states. Federation claim-race #[ignore]/P2.2 documented (InProcessBus total order). Note: workspace gate still red from oc-a bd-2wc persona break in oc-b sc1 + oc-c toron-mcp (not my files, notified).

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05):

1. **@mention parser is channel-agnostic.** The parser keys off a mention marker + `p` tag on ANY message (kind-14 DM OR kind-9 channel msg). So @mention dispatch delivers value in P2.1 BEFORE channels ship — a human DMs "@OCβ fix X" → kind-43001. Channel-mention (SC-9 / bd-l73) is the P2.2 multi-party UX. Don't make the parser channel-bound; that would needlessly hard-depend on bd-esh.2 and break the captain's "workflow+@mention before channels" ordering.

2. **Claim resolution on InProcessBus = first-observed-43002 wins** (the bus is a total order in-process). Federation claim races (two agents claim on different relays simultaneously) are a known hard problem — note it, do NOT try to solve it in P2.1 (Phase 2.1 is InProcessBus; federation RelayBus is later).

3. **Queued jobs are durable.** With the A7 semaphore (bounded concurrency + one-in-flight-per-agent), excess @mentions QUEUE. Queued 43001s persist in the bus event store; on toron restart the dispatcher resumes from the bus cursor (no lost jobs). Consistent with the lossless-projection rule from the bd-led.3.2 review — do not put the dispatch queue on a dropping channel.
